food_culture.description: Coastal Aviation's Zanzibar page highlights Stone Town's carved doors, coral-stone houses and the trading port of the Sultans of Oman as the heart of Swahili and Arab culture on the island.

food_culture.name: Forodhani waterfront food market
food_culture.description: After dark, stalls line the Forodhani Gardens waterfront in Stone Town grilling seafood and skewers and serving sugarcane juice; the evening market is a long-running local tradition.

title: Oslo, Bergen + the Fjords by Rail and Boat, Norway
best_time_description: Late May to September is the practical window: the Flåm Railway runs eight to ten times a day from May to October but only four times a day in winter (Flåmsbana), and the fjord cruise and Bygdøy ferry are fuller in summer. Check the cruise timetable for the exact date you travel; winter trips work but with fewer departures.
description: Norway's classic first-timer arc: the capital's waterfront and museums, the Bergen Line over the mountains to Myrdal, the steep Flåm Railway down to the fjord, a cruise through the UNESCO-listed Nærøyfjord (the heart of 'Norway in a Nutshell'), and then Bergen's old Hanseatic wharf, finished by the seven-hour train or a flight home.

days.title: Arrive Oslo
activities: Take the airport train or express bus from Oslo Airport Gardermoen to Oslo Central Station and check in near the station.
Walk the roof of the Oslo Opera House, a few minutes on foot from Oslo Central Station, for city and fjord views.
Evening stroll through the Bjørvika waterfront.
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Oslo Central Station or Bjørvika

days.title: Oslo: Munch, Akershus + Vigeland
activities: MUNCH in Bjørvika, which holds the world's largest collection of Edvard Munch paintings across 13 floors.
Walk the grounds of Akershus Fortress in the city centre.
Afternoon in Vigeland Sculpture Park in Frogner, with more than 200 sculptures by a single artist.
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Oslo Central Station or Bjørvika

days.title: Oslo: Bygdøy polar ships
activities: Visit the Fram Museum on Bygdøy to see the original polar expedition ship (the Bygdøynes ferry, route B9, runs seasonally from March/April to September/October; check ruter.no).
Note the old Viking Ship Museum on Bygdøy is closed; its replacement, the Museum of the Viking Age, is listed by Visit Norway as opening late 2027, so do not plan a visit.
Evening free for the Oslofjord islands on a regular public-transport ticket; do not miss the last ferry back.
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Oslo Central Station or Bjørvika

days.title: Oslo to Flåm by the Bergen Line
activities: Take the Vy train on the Bergen Line from Oslo to Myrdal (a Bergen Line train from Oslo takes about seven hours to Bergen; Vy says journeys from Flåm to Oslo take between six and eleven hours depending on route, with one change at Myrdal; check Vy or Entur for your date). Seat reservation is included in Single, Plus and Family tickets.

At Myrdal change to the Flåm Railway for the roughly 55-minute ride down to Flåm; tickets can be bought up to 120 days ahead, tickets are valid only for the departure printed, and there is no ticket office or machine at Myrdal, so buy in advance and take the first connection.
Spend the evening in Flåm village on the Aurlandsfjord.

days.title: Nærøyfjord cruise to Bergen (Norway in a Nutshell)
activities: Take the fjord cruise from Flåm through the Aurlandsfjord and the UNESCO-listed Nærøyfjord to Gudvangen, about two hours (Fjord Norway).

From Gudvangen continue by bus to Voss (about one hour) and by train from Voss to Bergen (about one hour); these two leg times are from a UK Nutshell operator's published breakdown, so confirm on Fjord Tours or Entur for your date.
Arrive Bergen in the evening and walk down to the harbour.

days.title: Bergen: Bryggen + Fløyen
activities: Walk Bryggen, the UNESCO World Heritage wharf, and the harbour fish market.
Ride the Fløibanen funicular to the 320 m summit of Mount Fløyen, about six minutes each way (floyen.no); city views and walking trails at the top.
Evening seafood at the harbour.

days.title: Bergen: museums + free afternoon
activities: A harbour walk and the museums around the city centre in the morning, then a free afternoon in the neighbourhoods behind Bryggen.
Check each museum's own site for opening days and hours before going.

days.title: Depart Bergen or return to Oslo
activities: Fly onward from Bergen Airport, or take the direct Vy train from Bergen back to Oslo, about seven hours with no changes and a seat reservation included in the ticket.
Book the train in advance in summer; Interrail/Eurail pass holders must reserve a seat on this route.

food_culture.name: Fresh seafood at Bergen's harbour
food_culture.description: Bergen's harbour fish market sells fresh seafood by the water, a long-standing part of the city's trading identity and an easy lunch between Bryggen and the funicular.

food_culture.name: Brunost (brown cheese)
food_culture.description: A sweet-savoury caramelised whey cheese eaten sliced thin with a cheese slicer on bread, crispbread or waffles, found on every Norwegian breakfast table.

food_culture.name: Fårikål
food_culture.description: Lamb and cabbage slowly cooked with whole black pepper, widely regarded as Norway's national dish and served mainly in autumn.

food_culture.name: Aquavit
food_culture.description: A caraway-flavoured Norwegian spirit drunk with festive meals, with the 'linje' aquavit style matured in casks that cross the equator by ship.

food_culture.name: Syttende Mai (Constitution Day)
food_culture.description: On 17 May Norwegians dress in regional bunad costume and march in children's parades; the day is celebrated in every town, including Oslo and Bergen.

food_culture.name: Bryggen and the Hanseatic trade
food_culture.description: The timber wharf buildings of Bergen's Bryggen are a UNESCO World Heritage Site that preserves the memory of the Hanseatic League's stockfish trade.

title: Tromsø Arctic Aurora Week, Norway
best_time_description: This is the aurora version of the trip: the northern lights may be visible in the Tromsø region from late August to early April, with organised tours starting early September and activity often strongest between about 20:00 and 02:00 (Visit Tromsø). The polar night runs about 27 November to 15 January (the sun stays below the horizon), whale watching runs roughly mid-November to late January, and winter brings dog sledding, Sámi reindeer experiences and snowmobiling. Midnight sun in Tromsø runs from mid-May to late July, a different trip with no aurora because the sky stays light.
description: A compact Arctic week from one base in Tromsø: polar-museum and cable-car sightseeing by day, aurora tours and Sámi culture in the evenings, and an island day trip, reached by a direct flight from Oslo.

days.title: Arrive Tromsø
activities: Fly Oslo to Tromsø direct, about two hours on the schedule listed by Norwegian (1 h 55 min to 2 h 0 min); the airport coach serves several central hotels.
Settle in and book at least two aurora evenings: Visit Tromsø advises more nights improve your chances and that tours sell out.
Evening organised aurora tour with a local guide, as advised by Visit Tromsø.

days.title: Tromsø: Fjellheisen + the Arctic Cathedral
activities: Ride the Fjellheisen cable car, a four to five minute ride to 421 m above sea level; the gondola was open daily 09:00 to 00:00 at the time of research, with rebuilding work under way and wheelchair access unavailable during it.
Visit the Arctic Cathedral in Tromsdalen, built in 1965 with a glass mosaic window; summer midnight-sun concerts are held here, so there will not be any in the dark season.
Evening free; keep one night spare for the aurora if the sky was cloudy.

days.title: Polar Museum, Polaria + Sámi culture
activities: The Polar Museum for Arctic expeditions from the 17th century to today.
Polaria, the Arctic experience centre with the northernmost aquarium and seal encounters.
Arctic University Museum of Norway, which has exhibitions and guided tours on Sámi history from ancient times to today.

days.title: Island day trip to Sommarøy
activities: Travel to Sommarøy, an island about an hour's drive from Tromsø known for sea safaris and kayaking (Visit Norway); confirm which activities run on your dates as many are seasonal.
Alternative in winter: dog sledding (autumn and winter), a Sámi reindeer experience (winter), or snowmobiling (winter); book through a local operator.
Second aurora evening if skies are clear.

days.title: Whales, fjord or a quiet day
activities: From mid-November to late January, whale watching is available from Skjervøy (a separate day trip; check operator departure times and pickup).
Outside that window, spend the day on a fjord or mountain tour or a slow day in town (cafes, the harbour, shops).
Last aurora evening if you still have not seen it.

days.title: Depart Tromsø
activities: Airport coach to Tromsø Airport for the flight home or back to Oslo (about two hours).
Allow extra time in winter for weather-related delays.

food_culture.name: Reindeer in Sámi cooking
food_culture.description: Reindeer is a traditional Sámi staple in northern Norway, served roasted, smoked or in stews; the Tromsø area has Sámi experiences in winter where the meat is cooked over a fire.

food_culture.name: Stockfish and cod from the north
food_culture.description: Wind-dried cod (stockfish) from Arctic Norway has been exported for centuries; fresh cod and fish soup turn up on most Tromsø menus.

food_culture.name: Mack beer from Tromsø
food_culture.description: Tromsø is home to the Mack brewery, founded in 1877, whose beer is sold in local pubs and shops in the city.

food_culture.name: Samefolkets dag (Sámi National Day)
food_culture.description: The Sámi people mark their national day on 6 February with flags, traditional dress and cultural events across northern Norway, including Tromsø.

food_culture.name: Sámi culture
food_culture.description: The Arctic University Museum of Norway offers exhibitions and tours on Sámi history from ancient times to modern life, a good introduction before a winter reindeer experience.

food_culture.name: Polar night and midnight sun
food_culture.description: Tromsø lives by the light: about 27 November to 15 January the sun stays below the horizon, and from mid-May to late July it does not set at all.

title: Stockholm, the Archipelago + Uppsala, Sweden
best_time_description: May to September: the summer archipelago boats (Strömma's Cinderella II to Vaxholm, Grinda and Sandhamn ran from 30 April to 27 September in its 2026 timetable, daily 18 June to 16 August) and the Linnaeus Museum in Uppsala (open May to September per Visit Sweden) all fall in this window. Year-round Waxholmsbolaget and SL boats still reach Vaxholm, but Skansen's hours shorten in autumn and winter (10:00 to 15:00 on weekdays October to March on its site). This is an editorial suggestion; check each operator's current timetable.
description: A car-free first-timer's Stockholm: the old town and the Vasa ship, a day in the inner archipelago at Vaxholm and another on Grinda by Strömma's Cinderella boat, a train day trip to the university town of Uppsala, and a last morning on Fjäderholmarna. Everything is by boat, tram or SJ train.

days.title: Arrive Stockholm + Gamla stan
activities: Check in, then walk Gamla stan, the old town on the island of Stadsholmen: Stortorget square, the Royal Palace and Stockholm Cathedral
Fika (a coffee and cinnamon bun break) in one of the old-town cafes
Evening stroll along the Strandvägen waterfront, where the Strömma archipelago boats used on days 3 and 4 depart from berth 14
days.lodging_suggestion: Gamla stan or Norrmalm near Stockholm Central

days.title: Djurgården: Vasa Museum + Skansen
activities: Vasa Museum: the warship that sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 and was salvaged after 333 years; buy tickets on the museum's website, but note it says pre-purchased tickets do not give priority in the queue

Skansen, which calls itself the world's oldest open-air museum, with 190 museum buildings and a zoo of Nordic wildlife; opening hours change by season (10:00 to 15:00 on weekdays from October to March on skansen.se), so check the day you go
Walk the Djurgården waterfront back toward the city
days.drive_time: Gamla stan to Djurgården by public transport; check SL for the current route

days.title: Inner archipelago: Vaxholm
activities: Boat from the city to Vaxholm: about 55 minutes on Strömma's Cinderella II from Strandvägen (2026 timetable) or about an hour on SL commuter ferry line 83 from Strömkajen/Slussen (Visit Sweden); a regular SL ticket is valid on line 83
Walk Vaxholm's waterfront and old streets

Vaxholm Kastell (the fortress island): in Strömma's 2026 timetable the change to the M/S Djurgården 4 boat in Vaxholm for Vaxholms Kastell ran daily 22 June to 23 August and on weekends 14 May to 14 June and 29 August to 6 September; confirm the 2027 dates
Return by boat in the afternoon
days.drive_time: Stockholm to Vaxholm by boat, about 55 min to 1 h

days.title: Island day: Grinda
activities: Strömma Cinderella II leaves Strandvägen (berth 14) at 10:00 and reaches Södra Grinda at 11:30 on its 2026 timetable (about 1 h 30 min, calling at Vaxholm on the way); it runs from 30 April to 27 September, daily 18 June to 16 August, with a reduced weekday pattern otherwise, so check the pattern for your date and the 2027 timetable
Walk Grinda's paths and swim from the rocks in warm weather; take your own food or check ahead what is open on the island, as services there are seasonal
Return boats pass Södra Grinda at 13:25, 15:55, 18:25 or 19:55 depending on date and take about 1 h 30 min to Strandvägen; do not miss the last one
Outside the summer season, swap this day for Fjäderholmarna (Fjäderholmslinjen from Slussen, about 20 to 30 minutes per Visit Stockholm and Visit Sweden; check its winter operation)
days.drive_time: Strandvägen to Södra Grinda by boat, about 1 h 30 min

days.title: Day trip to Uppsala by SJ train
activities: SJ train from Stockholm Central to Uppsala, under 40 minutes (Visit Sweden); commuter trains to Uppsala depart every 30 minutes through the day
Uppsala Cathedral, resting place of King Gustav Vasa and Carl Linnaeus
Gustavianum, the university museum
Linnaeus Garden, Sweden's first botanical garden (founded 1655), and the Linnaeus Museum in his former home, which Visit Sweden lists as open May to September
Gamla Uppsala (Old Uppsala): the royal burial mounds beside the Gamla Uppsala Museum and church; check the local bus connection from the city before you go
Try a Linnébulle, the giant cinnamon bun at Café Linné, before the train back
days.drive_time: Stockholm to Uppsala by train, under 40 min each way

days.title: Fjäderholmarna + departure
activities: Morning boat to Fjäderholmarna from Slussen, about 20 to 30 minutes (Visit Stockholm and Visit Sweden give 20 and 30); check whether it is running on the day, since the service is seasonal in places
Return to the city for a last fika and your onward travel
days.drive_time: Slussen to Fjäderholmarna, about 20-30 min by boat

food_culture.name: Fika
food_culture.description: The Swedish coffee-and-pastry break, taken in cafes and at work rather than eaten on the move; a cinnamon bun (kanelbulle) is the classic partner. Plan at least one in Gamla stan and one in Uppsala.

food_culture.name: Linnébulle
food_culture.description: A giant cinnamon bun that Visit Sweden names as a speciality of Café Linné in Uppsala, also sold at other cafes in the city.

food_culture.name: Köttbullar (Swedish meatballs)
food_culture.description: Small meatballs served with gravy, mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam; a standard dish on lunch menus in Stockholm.

food_culture.name: Home-brewed mead
food_culture.description: Visit Sweden lists home-brewed mead at Odinsborg Restaurant and Cafe in Gamla Uppsala, beside the royal mounds.

food_culture.name: Midsommar
food_culture.description: Swedish midsummer, held on the Friday between 19 and 25 June, with a flower-decked maypole, dancing and a festive table that traditionally includes pickled herring, new potatoes and strawberries. It is a public holiday period, so check opening days and book transport and meals ahead if you travel then.

title: Gothenburg, Marstrand + the West Coast Islands, Sweden
best_time_description: June to August is the easiest season: ferries run most often and the islands' summer cafes and swimming spots are open. May and September also work, with fewer services. Marstrand's Carlsten Fortress states it is open all year, but island ferries are less frequent in winter. This is an editorial suggestion; confirm every ferry on the Västtrafik travel planner for your date.
description: Sweden's west coast without a car: Gothenburg's Haga and Slottsskogen, the southern archipelago by ferry from Saltholmen, the island fortress town of Marstrand, the northern islands of Hönö and Öckerö, and the far southern island of Vrångö. All transport is Västtrafik tram, bus and ferry.

days.title: Arrive Gothenburg + Haga
activities: If coming from Stockholm, the train to Gothenburg takes around 3 hours (Gothenburg tourist board; SJ and VR run it); check the live timetable
Walk Haga, one of Gothenburg's oldest districts, with cobbled streets, cafes and small shops
Try a Hagabullen, the huge cinnamon bun at Cafe Husaren
Climb to Skansen Kronan, a late-17th-century fortification above Haga, for the view

days.title: Gothenburg city + Slottsskogen
activities: Slottsskogen, one of the city's largest and oldest parks, with a free zoo of Nordic animals including elk that goteborg.com says is open all year
Dinner at Fiskekrogen on Lilla Torget, which goteborg.com says has served fish since 1972 (check opening days and book)
Buy a Västtrafik Zone A ticket or day ticket: a Zone A ticket covers tram, bus and ferry for the island days

days.title: Southern archipelago: Saltholmen + Brännö
activities: Tram 11 from central Gothenburg to Saltholmen takes about 35 minutes; the Ö-snabben bus 114 takes about 25 minutes (goteborg.com)

Ferries from Saltholmen run about once an hour to Asperö, Brännö, Köpstadsö, Styrsö, Donsö and Vrångö; the Brännö Rödsten ferry (line 283) takes about 20 minutes and the Brännö Husvik ferry (line 282) about 50 minutes via several islands
Walk the island lanes and swim from the rocks in summer; take food or check ahead what is open
Plan the return so you catch the last ferry; a Zone A ticket covers the whole journey, and bikes are only taken if there is room
days.drive_time: Gothenburg to Saltholmen ~35 min by tram, then ~20 min by ferry

days.title: Marstrand + Carlsten Fortress
activities: Bus 302 from the Nils Ericson terminal at Gothenburg Central Station to Arvidsvik on Koön, about 1 h 10 min via Kungälv per Carlsten's website (an express bus 312 is about 55 minutes; confirm on Västtrafik)
Passenger ferry from Koön to Marstrandsön: about 2 minutes, every 15 minutes in the daytime; cars are not allowed on Marstrandsön

Walk about 200 m along the quay and up Kungsgatan (the last part is a steep hill) to Carlsten Fortress (built 1658); Carlsten says it is open all year, but opening hours, prices and guided tours are on its own pages and vary by season, so check before you go
days.drive_time: Gothenburg to Marstrand ~1 h 10 min by bus plus 2 min ferry

days.title: Northern archipelago: Hönö + Öckerö
activities: Check the Västtrafik planner for the connection from the city to Lilla Varholmen, the ferry landing
Ferry from Lilla Varholmen to Hönö, about 12 minutes; goteborg.com says these are free car ferries
From Hönö, reach Öckerö by the bridge, or by Bus 1 from Hönö ferry terminal
Spend the day walking between the island harbours and return by the same ferry
days.drive_time: Lilla Varholmen to Hönö ~12 min by ferry; city to ferry landing via Västtrafik

days.title: Vrångö or departure
activities: Option for a longer island day: Vrångö, the far southern island. From Stenpiren lines 281 and 282 take about 1 h 35 min via Styrsö and Donsö, with only two departures per day Monday to Friday (goteborg.com); from Saltholmen ferries run about hourly. Check the return times before you commit
Otherwise, a last fika in Haga and onward travel from Gothenburg Central
days.drive_time: Stenpiren to Vrångö ~1 h 35 min by ferry

food_culture.name: Hagabullen
food_culture.description: A very large cinnamon bun from Cafe Husaren in Haga that goteborg.com describes as probably the world's biggest cinnamon bun. Share one.

food_culture.name: Räksmörgås (shrimp sandwich)
food_culture.description: An open sandwich piled with shrimp, mayonnaise, egg and dill, a classic of Sweden's west coast.

food_culture.name: West coast shellfish
food_culture.description: Prawns, langoustine, mussels and oysters are the speciality of the Bohuslän coast north of Gothenburg; look for them on harbour menus and fish restaurants.

food_culture.name: Kräftskiva (crayfish party)
food_culture.description: A late-summer social meal, traditionally in August, centred on boiled crayfish eaten with bread and cheese, often outdoors with paper lanterns and party hats.

food_culture.name: Allemansrätten (right of public access)
food_culture.description: Sweden's tradition of public access, which lets people walk and swim on most uncultivated land and stay briefly, with responsibility for not disturbing or damaging. It underpins walking the islands' rocks and trails; keep away from private gardens and leave no trace.

title: Copenhagen, Roskilde, Helsingør + Odense, Denmark
best_time_description: May to September gives the longest days and is the only time the Viking Ship Museum's rowing and sailing trips run (1 May to 30 September per the museum). June to August is warmest and busiest; May and September are quieter. Tivoli Gardens is a seasonal park, so check its opening calendar if you visit outside summer.
description: Denmark's classic first-timer arc by train: Copenhagen's harbour, palaces and design, a day trip north to Hamlet's Kronborg Castle, the Viking ships and royal cathedral of Roskilde, then across the Great Belt to Odense, hometown of Hans Christian Andersen.

days.title: Arrive Copenhagen
activities: Arrive at Copenhagen Airport (Kastrup) and take the Metro or a DSB train into the city; the airport has both, so check the current timetable on rejseplanen.dk or dsb.dk for the fastest option to your hotel
Evening walk along Nyhavn harbour and the Inderhavnen waterfront
Dinner of smørrebrød (open-faced rye-bread sandwiches) at a traditional lunch restaurant if open in the evening, otherwise at a market hall such as Torvehallerne
days.lodging_suggestion: Indre By (city centre) or Vesterbro near the central station

days.title: Copenhagen: palaces and canals
activities: Rosenborg Castle and its Treasury, which displays the Danish crown jewels and crown regalia (buy tickets online; check Rosenborg's opening-hours page for current days)
Walk through the King's Garden (Kongens Have), then the Latin Quarter
Canal boat tour from Nyhavn or Ved Stranden, then Christiansborg Palace area and the Round Tower
Evening at Tivoli Gardens if it is in season (it is a seasonal park; check tivoli.dk/en/opening-hours-and-seasons; a Halloween season runs 2 October to 1 November 2026)
days.lodging_suggestion: Indre By (city centre) or Vesterbro near the central station

days.title: Day trip to Helsingør and Kronborg Castle
activities: DSB regional train from København H to Helsingør, about 55 minutes on a DSB K26 timetable example (a 19:22 departure arriving 20:17), with trains every 20 minutes per DSB; check the current timetable on rejseplanen.dk or dsb.dk for your exact train

Kronborg Castle (Hamlet's Elsinore, UNESCO World Heritage Site): kronborg.dk lists it open Monday to Sunday 10:00-17:00 with adult tickets 150 DKK at the door or 135 DKK online; check its opening-hours page for holiday closures. The English 'In Hamlet's Footsteps' tour runs 1 May to 31 December and requires registration
Walk Helsingør's old town and harbour, then return by train to Copenhagen
days.lodging_suggestion: Indre By (city centre) or Vesterbro near the central station

days.title: Roskilde, then on to Odense
activities: DSB InterCity from København H to Roskilde takes about 22 minutes (DSB); a regional train takes just over 25 minutes. Leave bags at the station lockers or carry them

Viking Ship Museum (Vindeboder 12): five original Viking ships from Skuldelev; rowing and sailing trips on Roskilde Fjord run daily 1 May to 30 September, sold as a separate ticket (check the museum's opening hours page; its hours were 10:00-16:00 on the day checked)
Roskilde Cathedral (Domkirke), a UNESCO World Heritage site and royal burial church; it can close for religious ceremonies, so check its hours (10:00-16:00 on the day checked)

Afternoon DSB InterCity from Roskilde to Odense across the Great Belt (Storebælt): København H to Odense takes about 1 hour 10 minutes on the InterCityLyn per DSB, with more than 50 departures a day; check the current timetable on rejseplanen.dk or dsb.dk for the Roskilde departure
days.lodging_suggestion: Odense city centre near the station

days.title: Odense: Hans Christian Andersen's town
activities: H.C. Andersen's House (Hans Christian Andersens Hus) with its audio guide in five languages and Café Deilig in the garden (tickets bought online; check hcandersenshus.dk for current hours, 10:00-17:00 on the day checked)
Walk the old streets of the Munke Mølle and Brandts Passage area along the Odense River
Visit the Funen Village open-air museum (Den Fynske Landsby) or a museum of your choice; check the seasonal opening dates before going
Evening dinner on Funen
days.lodging_suggestion: Odense city centre near the station

days.title: Back to Copenhagen and depart
activities: DSB InterCityLyn from Odense to København H, about 1 hour 10 minutes (DSB), more than 50 departures a day
Last stroll through Copenhagen's Torvehallerne market or the Strøget shopping street if time allows
Metro or DSB train to Copenhagen Airport for departure; allow time for the EU Entry/Exit System checks that apply to some non-EU travellers on departure

food_culture.name: Smørrebrød
food_culture.description: Smørrebrød are open-faced sandwiches on dense rye bread (rugbrød) with toppings such as pickled herring, smoked fish, roast beef or liver pâté. Lunch is the classic time to eat it at a traditional smørrebrød restaurant in Copenhagen, and it is also central to the julefrokost Christmas lunch.

food_culture.name: Wienerbrød (Danish pastry)
food_culture.description: What the world calls a Danish pastry is wienerbrød ('Vienna bread') in Danish. Bakeries across Copenhagen, Roskilde and Odense sell the laminated, butter-rich pastries in many shapes such as spandauer and kanelsnegl (cinnamon snail), usually with morning coffee.

food_culture.name: Stegt flæsk med persillesovs
food_culture.description: Crispy fried pork belly served with boiled potatoes and parsley sauce is a Danish home-cooking classic and is frequently named as the national dish. Look for it on the menus of traditional restaurants and canteens.

food_culture.name: Snaps and Danish beer with lunch
food_culture.description: Danish lunches and celebrations often pair smørrebrød with a cold lager or a small glass of snaps (aquavit), the caraway- or dill-flavoured spirit served ice cold. Carlsberg was founded in Copenhagen in 1847, and the city now has many craft breweries and bars.

food_culture.name: Hygge
food_culture.description: Hygge is the Danish idea of cosy, relaxed togetherness: candles, warm drinks, simple food and good company. You will notice it in cafés, in the way friends gather over coffee and cake, and in how much candlelight Danes use indoors, especially outside summer.

food_culture.name: Hamlet's Elsinore and Hans Christian Andersen
food_culture.description: Kronborg Castle in Helsingør is the setting of Shakespeare's Hamlet (Elsinore), though Shakespeare likely never visited it, according to the castle's own website. Odense is the birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen, whose fairy tales such as The Little Mermaid (the statue sits on Copenhagen's waterfront) are among the best-known Danish exports.

title: Aarhus, Legoland, Aalborg + Skagen, Jutland, Denmark
best_time_description: June to August is the best window: Legoland Billund is a seasonal park (it was in a Halloween season to 1 November 2026, so check its opening calendar outside summer), and long daylight helps for Skagen's beaches and Grenen. May and September are quieter with a shorter list of open seasonal attractions.
description: A different side of Denmark up the Jutland peninsula by train and bus: Aarhus with its art museum, open-air old town and Iron Age bog man, a day at the original Legoland in Billund, then Aalborg's architecture and a day at Skagen, Denmark's northern tip where two seas meet.

days.title: Copenhagen to Aarhus
activities: DSB InterCityLyn from København H to Aarhus H takes about 2 hours 48 minutes per DSB's Copenhagen-Aarhus page; check the current timetable on rejseplanen.dk or dsb.dk for your train
Settle into the Latin Quarter (Latinerkvarteret), Aarhus's old cobbled streets of cafés and small shops
Evening walk along the Aarhus Å river and the harbourfront
days.lodging_suggestion: Aarhus city centre or Latin Quarter

days.title: Aarhus: art and the old town
activities: ARoS Aarhus Art Museum (Aros Allé 2) and Olafur Eliasson's rooftop 'Your rainbow panorama'; aros.dk showed Monday closed, Tuesday to Friday 10:00-20:00 and Saturday and Sunday 09:00-17:00 the week checked (hours can vary on holidays; tickets at shop.aros.dk)
Den Gamle By (Viborgvej 2), the open-air town museum; its site showed 10:00-17:00 the day checked, and tickets bought in advance skip the queue (check the opening-hours page for the season)
Dinner in the Latin Quarter or Aarhus Street Food area
days.lodging_suggestion: Aarhus city centre or Latin Quarter

days.title: Day trip to LEGOLAND Billund
activities: Midttrafik bus 912X runs from Aarhus Rutebilstation (via Banegårdspladsen, Skanderborg and Horsens) to Billund Airport; Midttrafik's page does not state the running time, and secondary sources suggest about 90 minutes each way, so confirm on rejseplanen.dk and allow for it

LEGOLAND Billund Resort: the park is seasonal and has an opening calendar that changes through the year (hours were 10:00-18:00 on a day checked, with rides closing an hour earlier); check legoland.dk/en/plan-your-day/pre-visit/opening-hours before planning this day. Day tickets start at 349 DKK and are bought online
Return to Aarhus by the 912X bus the same evening, checking the last departure back
days.lodging_suggestion: Aarhus city centre or Latin Quarter

days.title: Moesgaard, then Aarhus to Aalborg
activities: Morning at Moesgaard Museum (Moesgård Allé 15, Højbjerg), home of the Grauballe Man, a well-preserved Iron Age bog body; check moesgaardmuseum.dk for opening days first as the museum showed 'Closed today' on a Monday when checked; buy tickets online
DSB InterCityLyn from Aarhus H to Aalborg takes about 1 hour 18 minutes, or about 1 hour 35 minutes on the slower InterCity, with more than 30 departures a day per DSB
Evening walk along the Limfjord waterfront in Aalborg
days.lodging_suggestion: Aalborg city centre near the station

days.title: Aalborg
activities: Utzon Center at Slotspladsen 4, the cultural venue designed by Jørn Utzon with his son Kim Utzon, his last project; check utzoncenter.dk for opening days and the current exhibition
Walk through Aalborg's old centre and along the Limfjord harbour
Dinner in Jomfru Ane Gade or a restaurant by the harbour
days.lodging_suggestion: Aalborg city centre near the station

days.title: Day trip to Skagen
activities: Train from Aalborg to Frederikshavn, then the Skagen line (Skagensbanen) to Skagen; the Skagen line is a 39.7 km single-track line, and a travel guide puts the Frederikshavn to Skagen ride at about 40 minutes, but the operator's own timetable could not be read, so confirm the through journey time and the changes on rejseplanen.dk before you go
Grenen, the sandy tip of Denmark where the Skagerrak and Kattegat meet
Skagen's old fishing harbour and its seafood; Skagens Museum holds the work of the Skagen Painters, so check its opening days before visiting
Return to Aalborg by train in the evening, checking the last departure
days.lodging_suggestion: Aalborg city centre near the station

days.title: Aalborg to Copenhagen and depart
activities: DSB InterCityLyn from Aalborg to København H takes about 4 hours 13 minutes per DSB, with more than 30 departures a day; leave early if you are flying out the same day
Metro or DSB train to Copenhagen Airport; allow time for EU Entry/Exit System checks on departure for those who are covered

food_culture.name: Rugbrød (Danish rye bread)
food_culture.description: Dense, dark rye bread (rugbrød) is the base of Danish lunch, topped with fish, meat or cheese as smørrebrød, or packed into lunch boxes. Bakeries in Aarhus and Aalborg sell it fresh, and it is eaten much more commonly than wheat bread at midday.

food_culture.name: Frikadeller
food_culture.description: Frikadeller are pan-fried Danish meatballs of minced pork (often mixed with veal), typically served with potatoes, gravy and red cabbage or pickled cucumber. They are home-cooking staples and appear on the menus of traditional restaurants and canteens across Jutland.

food_culture.name: Fresh fish and shellfish at Skagen
food_culture.description: Skagen is a working fishing port at Denmark's northern tip, and its harbour restaurants and fish shops serve locally landed fish and shellfish such as plaice and prawns. It is the place in this trip to eat the sea.

food_culture.name: Coffee and cake culture
food_culture.description: Danes drink a lot of coffee, and kaffe og kage (coffee and cake) is an everyday social ritual, often shared in cafés or at work. In Aarhus's Latin Quarter you will find small cafés and bakeries serving coffee with pastries.

food_culture.name: Hygge
food_culture.description: Hygge is the Danish sense of cosy, relaxed togetherness: candlelight, warm drinks, simple food and good company, which you will notice in cafés and homes year-round but especially outside summer.

food_culture.name: LEGO's hometown and the Skagen Painters
food_culture.description: The LEGO company began in Billund, where Legoland now stands. At the far northern tip, Skagen became an artists' colony in the late 1800s, and the Skagen Painters, who painted the light and the fishing community, are celebrated at Skagens Museum.

title: Warsaw, Krakow + Auschwitz-Birkenau, Poland
best_time_description: May-June and September-October are the easiest windows for walking two big cities and a half-day underground at Wieliczka. The Auschwitz Memorial is open all year (not on 1 January, 25 December and Easter Sunday), and its daily entry hours run from 7:30 AM with the last start between 2:00 PM (December) and 7:00 PM (June-August), so summer gives the most flexibility but also the hardest passes to get.
description: Poland's classic first-timer arc: Warsaw's rebuilt Old Town and the POLIN Museum, the 2 h 21 min Pendolino south to Krakow's Main Square and Wawel Hill, then two heavy, unmissable day trips: the Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial (free, but only with a pre-booked personal entry pass) and the Wieliczka Salt Mine.

days.title: Warsaw Old Town
activities: Arrive in Warsaw and settle into the centre
Walk the Old Town and Castle Square; the Old Town was rebuilt after the Second World War and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Dinner at a milk bar (bar mleczny) for cheap Polish home cooking, or a traditional restaurant in the Old Town
days.lodging_suggestion: Warsaw Old Town or the centre near Warszawa Centralna station

days.title: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
activities: POLIN Museum core exhibition on 1,000 years of Polish Jewish history. The museum is closed to visitors on Tuesdays and on a few listed dates (in 2026: 1 November and 24, 25 and 31 December); last entry to the core exhibition is 4 PM Wed-Fri and Sun-Mon (6 PM Saturday), so plan 2-3 hours and buy a ticket online
Walk through the former Muranow district around the museum
Evening along the Vistula boulevards or in the Praga district
days.lodging_suggestion: Warsaw centre, near Warszawa Centralna so tomorrow's train is easy

days.title: Warsaw to Krakow Main Square
activities: Morning in Warsaw (Royal Castle area or Lazienki Park)

PKP Intercity train from Warszawa Centralna to Krakow Glowny: about 2 h 21 min on the Express InterCity Premium (Pendolino), about 2 h 54 min on a regular InterCity (PKP Intercity). Tickets for the EIP Premium must be bought before boarding
Late afternoon on Krakow's Main Square (Rynek Glowny): Cloth Hall, St Mary's Basilica exterior, evening street food including a ring-shaped obwarzanek
days.drive_time: Train, ~2 hrs 21 min (EIP Pendolino) / ~2 hrs 54 min (IC)

days.title: Wawel Royal Castle + Kazimierz
activities: Wawel Royal Castle and Cathedral. Daily entrance limits apply and the entry time printed on your ticket must be observed; the castle sells tickets online up to a month ahead. Open Tuesday-Sunday 9 AM-5 PM; on Mondays only selected exhibitions open (10 AM-4 PM) with free tickets from the ticket windows while the pool lasts
Walk down the Royal Road to the Kazimierz former Jewish quarter
Dinner in Kazimierz

days.title: Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial and Museum
activities: ADVANCE TIMED ENTRY REQUIRED: entry is only possible with a personalised pre-paid entry pass booked at visit.auschwitz.org (no passes are sold at the entrance). Passes are released daily from 12:00 noon, up to 90 days ahead. Entry to the grounds is free; a guided tour with a museum educator is charged

Getting there: Lajkonik buses run from Krakow (MDA, Bosacka 18) to the Museum car park; the operator's 2026 timetable shows about 1 h 25 min (for example 06:15 departure, 07:40 arrival). Check the timetable for your day

Arrive at least 30 minutes before your start time for security checks. Bags may not exceed 35 x 25 x 15 cm; leave larger luggage in Krakow. A standard guided tour of Auschwitz I and Auschwitz II-Birkenau lasts about 3.5 hours; independent visitors should allow at least 90 minutes for each site. A free museum shuttle runs between the two sites, 3.5 km apart
The Museum is open daily except 1 January, 25 December and Easter Sunday. Plan a quiet evening afterwards
days.drive_time: Bus, ~1 hr 25 min each way (Lajkonik timetable)

days.title: Wieliczka Salt Mine
activities: Wieliczka Salt Mine Tourist Route: a guided 2-3 hour tour, about 800 steps in total (about 380 steps down to the first level at 64 m, then a lift back up from Level III at 135 m). Tickets are sold online, at a machine at the entrance and at the Danilowicz Shaft office if any are left; tours in languages other than Polish run at designated times, so buy ahead online. It is cool underground (0-18 C), so bring a layer

Getting there: the mine is about 10 km south-east of Krakow centre. Take the suburban train from Krakow Glowny to Wieliczka Rynek-Kopalnia (a few minutes' walk to the mine) or bus line 304 from Dworzec Glowny Zachod to Wieliczka Kopalnia Soli (zones I and II ticket)
Back in Krakow for the evening, or a second walk around Podgorze and the Vistula

days.title: Krakow Kazimierz + Podgorze
activities: Slow morning: the Planty park ring around the Old Town
Cross the Vistula to Podgorze and Ghetto Heroes Square, and the Schindler's Factory museum (check opening days and book ahead online)
Last supper of pierogi, zurek soup or a Krakow zapiekanka on Plac Nowy in Kazimierz

days.title: Depart Krakow
activities: Check out and head to Krakow Glowny station or Krakow Airport (Balice)
Allow time for Entry/Exit System (EES) checks if you are leaving the Schengen area from Poland, which has operated at all Polish border crossings since 10 April 2026

food_culture.name: Pierogi
food_culture.description: Half-moon dumplings with fillings such as potato and cheese (ruskie), sauerkraut and mushroom, or meat; a staple of Polish home cooking and on nearly every traditional menu in Warsaw and Krakow.

food_culture.name: Zurek
food_culture.description: A sour rye soup, often served with sausage and a halved egg, sometimes in a bread bowl; a traditional Polish soup especially associated with Easter.

food_culture.name: Obwarzanek krakowski
food_culture.description: A ring-shaped braided bread, boiled then baked and sold from street carts around Krakow's Old Town; it carries an EU Protected Geographical Indication.

food_culture.name: Zapiekanka
food_culture.description: A long toasted baguette half topped with mushrooms and melted cheese; a street-food classic sold at Plac Nowy in Krakow's Kazimierz district and at stands across Poland.

food_culture.name: Milk bars (bary mleczne)
food_culture.description: Cheap, cafeteria-style canteens that began in communist-era Poland and still serve simple dishes like pierogi, soups and cutlets, with several in central Warsaw and Krakow.

food_culture.name: Kazimierz and Jewish heritage
food_culture.description: Krakow's Kazimierz was the city's Jewish district for centuries; today it is a living quarter of synagogues, cafes and galleries, alongside Warsaw's POLIN Museum, together telling the history of Polish Jewry before and after the Holocaust.

food_culture.name: Respect at Auschwitz-Birkenau
food_culture.description: The former camp is a memorial and a cemetery; the museum asks visitors to behave with dignity and has rules on bags, photography and clothing, and its entry passes are personal and issued in the holder's name.

title: Wroclaw, Gdansk + Malbork Castle, Poland
best_time_description: Late spring to early autumn is best for Gdansk's waterfront and the Baltic coast; Malbork Castle's historical route has far longer hours from late April through the summer than in the October-April season, when its last entry is 12:45. Shoulder months (May, June, September) avoid the heaviest crowds.
description: A second Poland, away from the Krakow circuit: Wroclaw's market square, dwarfs and the Racławice Panorama, then PKP Intercity's Baltic Express across the country to Gdansk's Main Town and the Solidarity story, with a morning at the world's largest brick castle at Malbork.

days.title: Wroclaw Market Square
activities: Arrive in Wroclaw and check in near the Old Town
Walk the Market Square (Rynek) and around the Gothic Town Hall
Look for the small bronze dwarf statues scattered around the Old Town, a city trademark; dinner in the Old Town

days.title: Ostrow Tumski + Panorama of the Battle of Raclawice
activities: Cross to Ostrow Tumski, the cathedral island, and walk across the bridges at the Odra river

Panorama of the Battle of Raclawice at ul. J. E. Purkyniego 11, open every day 8:30 AM-7:00 PM per the National Museum in Wroclaw; buy tickets online ahead. The same ticket gives free entry to the National Museum's permanent exhibitions, the Ethnographic Museum and the Four Domes Pavilion within 3 months
Browse the Hala Targowa covered market, then an evening drink in the Old Town

days.title: Centennial Hall + Four Domes Pavilion
activities: Centennial Hall (Hala Stulecia), a UNESCO World Heritage reinforced-concrete landmark opened in 1913

Four Domes Pavilion (ul. Wystawowa 1, next to the Hall): closed Mondays; Tue-Thu 10 AM-4 PM, Fri 10 AM-6 PM, Sat 10 AM-8 PM, Sun 10 AM-6 PM per the National Museum. Note that the National Museum itself (pl. Powstancow Warszawy 5) is also closed Mondays
Evening at Wroclaw's Nadodrze district or the river banks

days.title: Wroclaw to Gdansk
activities: Morning in Wroclaw: last coffee on the Rynek

PKP Intercity to Gdansk Glowny: the fastest IC Baltic Express is quoted by PKP Intercity at 4 h 8 min between Gdansk and Wroclaw (its 2026/2027 timetable announcement); check the exact Wroclaw to Gdansk departure and duration in the timetable on the day of travel
Evening on Dlugi Targ (Long Market) and the Motlawa waterfront
days.drive_time: Train, ~4 hrs (PKP Intercity IC Baltic Express, 4 h 8 min quoted for Gdansk-Wroclaw)

days.title: Gdansk Main Town + European Solidarity Centre
activities: Walk the Royal Way: Golden Gate, Long Market with the Neptune Fountain, and the Motlawa river front with its Crane

European Solidarity Centre (Plac Solidarnosci 1) at the old Gdansk Shipyard, which tells the story of the Solidarity movement; ticket office hours are Mon-Fri 10 AM-6 PM and Sat-Sun 10 AM-7 PM and tickets are sold online
Dinner of Baltic fish or Polish food in the Main Town; try a glass of Goldwasser, the herbal liqueur associated with Gdansk

days.title: Malbork Castle
activities: Day trip to Malbork Castle Museum, the Teutonic Order fortress on the Nogat river. Gdansk to Malbork is about 50 minutes by road according to the castle museum, which also lists direct train connections from Gdansk (check the timetable for the exact departure)

Season note (1 October 2026-25 April 2027): the Historical Castle Route runs Tuesday-Sunday 9 AM-4 PM with the last entry at 12:45 PM, so aim to arrive by late morning; on Mondays only the Castle Grounds Route is open (free admission, tickets collected on site). Summer hours differ, so check zamek.malbork.pl. Buy tickets online
Return to Gdansk for the evening
days.drive_time: Road ~50 min each way (castle museum); direct trains from Gdansk, check timetable

days.title: Westerplatte + depart Gdansk
activities: Westerplatte peninsula, where the Second World War began on 1 September 1939; check how to reach it and its current opening arrangements before you go
Last walk along the Motlawa and a final pastry in the Main Town
Depart Gdansk (Gdansk Glowny station or Gdansk airport)

food_culture.name: Pierogi
food_culture.description: Half-moon dumplings with fillings such as potato and cheese, sauerkraut and mushroom, or meat; found everywhere from Wroclaw's Old Town restaurants to Gdansk's Long Market.

food_culture.name: Zurek
food_culture.description: A sour rye soup with sausage and egg, a long-standing Polish dish, often served at traditional restaurants in both cities.

food_culture.name: Goldwasser
food_culture.description: A herbal liqueur with flakes of gold leaf that is traditionally associated with Gdansk, sold in the city's gift shops and bars.

food_culture.name: Baltic fish
food_culture.description: Gdansk sits on the Baltic coast and many Main Town and Motlawa riverside restaurants serve herring, cod and salmon.

food_culture.name: Wroclaw's dwarfs
food_culture.description: Hundreds of small bronze dwarf statues are scattered around the Old Town; they began as a nod to the Orange Alternative, a 1980s anti-communist street-art movement, and are now a city trademark.

food_culture.name: Solidarity and the Gdansk Shipyard
food_culture.description: The Solidarity trade union was born at the Gdansk Shipyard in August 1980; the European Solidarity Centre keeps the 21 Demands boards, which are on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.

food_culture.name: Malbork and the Teutonic Order
food_culture.description: Malbork was the capital of the Teutonic Knights' monastic state in the 14th century; the castle is one of the largest brick fortresses in Europe, and the museum runs separate Historical Castle and Castle Grounds routes.

title: Budapest, Szentendre + the Danube Bend, Hungary
best_time_description: May to early October suits the Danube Bend best: scheduled cruise boats from Budapest to Visegrád run between May and October (Hungarian Tourism Agency), and the Visegrád Citadel and Esztergom dome climbs are pleasanter in dry, mild weather. Spring and early autumn avoid the crowds and heat of high summer; in winter the basilica's dome and crypt close earlier and boats do not run.
description: A first-timer's Hungary: three days in Budapest on both banks of the Danube and a thermal bath, then the Danube Bend north of the capital by suburban train and regional bus, with Szentendre's galleries, the hilltop Citadel at Visegrád and the great basilica at Esztergom, and a train back to Budapest.

days.title: Arrive Budapest
activities: Arrive at Budapest and check in on the Pest side, within walking distance of the Danube embankment (use the BKK public transport information or a taxi from the airport; no transfer time is given here because none was confirmed)
Evening walk along the Danube embankment and over the Chain Bridge to look up at Buda Castle Hill
Dinner in the city centre; try a goulash soup or a Hungarian wine bar

days.title: Buda Castle Hill + Széchenyi Thermal Bath
activities: Morning on Buda Castle Hill: Fisherman's Bastion and the Castle District streets

Afternoon at the Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Állatkerti körút 9-11): the operator's site lists opening 07:00-20:00 Monday to Thursday, 07:00-22:00 Friday and 08:00-20:00 Saturday and Sunday, notes hours may vary, and sells tickets online to skip the queue; bring swimwear
Evening on the Pest side

days.title: Pest: Parliament and the markets
activities: Hungarian Parliament: it is visited on a guided tour, so check the Parliament's official visitor site for tour times and book ahead (the site asked for a CAPTCHA when checked, so ticket rules are not quoted here)
Walk the Danube embankment on the Pest side and through the inner-city streets
Browse the Great Market Hall for paprika and local food (check its opening days before you go)
Pack a day bag: tomorrow starts early on the HÉV from Batthyány tér

days.title: Szentendre + Visegrád
activities: HÉV suburban line H5 from Batthyány tér to Szentendre: about 39-40 minutes per the Volánbusz 880-889 timetable (a 2021 edition hosted by szentendre.hu), so check the current timetable; the HÉV is a suburban railway that needs a ticket bought before boarding
Szentendre: ArtMill and the Ferenczy Museum Center and the town's galleries (Hungarian Tourism Agency)
Regional bus 880 from Szentendre bus station to Visegrád: about 43-45 minutes on the same Volánbusz timetable (check the current timetable and that the bus runs on your day)

Visegrád: the Citadel on the hill (steep, with long wooden stairs to the top) has exhibitions on royal court life and a replica Holy Crown exhibition; the Lower Castle holds the old royal palace and Salomon Tower, and a historical playground (Hungarian Tourism Agency); check opening hours before you go
Optional in season (May-October): Visegrád is reached by scheduled cruise boat from Vigadó tér in Budapest; check the Mahart PassNave timetable
days.drive_time: HÉV H5 ~39-40 min; bus Szentendre-Visegrád ~43-45 min (Volánbusz timetable, 2021 edition)

days.title: Esztergom + back to Budapest
activities: Bus from Visegrád to Esztergom: about 45-52 minutes on the Volánbusz 880-889 timetable (check the current timetable)

Esztergom Basilica, about 100 m tall and Hungary's largest church: entry to the church is free; the crypt, treasury, panorama hall and dome lookout are paid, and the dome climb is about 400 steps. Opening hours change by season and are shorter in winter (the dome closed at 16:30 in the October-December schedule), so check the basilica's site; renovation work is ongoing but the church stays open
Walk to St István Square and the Esztergom Castle Museum next to the basilica (check its hours)
Train from Esztergom to Budapest-Nyugati (line 2): the same timetable shows the train running about 65-77 minutes; check the current MÁV timetable
days.drive_time: Bus Visegrád-Esztergom ~45-52 min; train Esztergom-Budapest Nyugati ~65-77 min (Volánbusz timetable, 2021 edition)

days.title: Last morning in Budapest + depart
activities: Free morning in Budapest: a second visit to a favourite spot, a cafe, or the thermal bath if you skipped it
Depart from Budapest by train or air; allow time for the EU Entry/Exit System checks on departure if you are a non-EU traveller

food_culture.name: Gulyás (goulash soup)
food_culture.description: Hungary's best-known dish, a paprika-red beef and vegetable soup or stew eaten with bread. Found in restaurants in Budapest and in the Danube Bend towns; menus vary by kitchen.

food_culture.name: Thermal bath culture
food_culture.description: Budapest's thermal baths are a daily social habit as much as a tourist stop. The Széchenyi Thermal Bath in the City Park sells tickets online and lists daily opening hours on its own site.

food_culture.name: Szentendre art town
food_culture.description: The Hungarian Tourism Agency describes Szentendre's ArtMill, the Ferenczy Museum Center and many galleries as hosting fine art exhibitions, with small handicraft shops and cafes on its narrow streets.

food_culture.name: Visegrád Citadel and royal palace
food_culture.description: The Citadel above the Danube Bend holds exhibitions on medieval Hungarian royal court life and a replica Holy Crown exhibition; below it the Lower Castle has the old royal palace and the Salomon Tower (Hungarian Tourism Agency).

food_culture.name: Esztergom Basilica
food_culture.description: Esztergom is the birthplace of St Stephen I, Hungary's founding king, and its classical basilica, finished in 1869 after 47 years of building, is considered Hungary's largest church (Hungarian Tourism Agency). Liszt's Missa Solemnis was written for its 1856 consecration.

title: Eger + Tokaj Wine Country, Hungary
best_time_description: Late spring (May-June) and early autumn (September-October) are the best windows: Tokaj holds a Wine Days festival in early June and a harvest festival in early October (the 2026 editions ran 4-7 June and 2-4 October per tokaj.hu; check 2027 dates), and the cellar terraces of Eger's Szépasszony-völgy are open-air at their best in mild weather. Winter is quieter, with cooler cellar tastings.
description: Hungary's wine north-east of Budapest: Eger's castle, minaret and baroque centre with a night in the Valley of the Beautiful Women, an optional hiking day at Szilvásvárad, then across to the Tokaj wine region, a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape, for sweet and dry Tokaji wines.

days.title: Budapest to Eger
activities: Direct train from Budapest Keleti to Eger, less than 2 hours without changing (Visit Eger gives about 1 hour 55 minutes by train and about 1 hour 50 minutes by Volánbusz coach); check the MÁV timetable for your day
Dobó István tér, Eger's main square, for a first walk
Dinner in the centre
days.drive_time: Train, under 2 hrs (about 1 hr 55 min per Visit Eger)

days.title: Eger castle, minaret + Beautiful Women valley
activities: Eger Castle (Vár 1), the town's grandest monument, described as a half-day visit by Visit Eger
Basilica of Eger (Pyrker János tér 1), the second largest church in Hungary, and the Minaret (Knézich Károly utca 4), the only minaret in the world with a cross on top

The Líceum (Eszterházy tér 1): the Archdiocese library and the Observatory with the oldest camera obscura on the continent; opening hours are not published on the tourism site, so call Tourinform (+36 36 517 715) first
Evening in the Szépasszony-völgy (Valley of the Beautiful Women), the main wine-tasting area, with dozens of cellars; try Egri Bikavér (red) and Egri Csillag (white)

days.title: Szilvásvárad or the thermal bath
activities: Option A: Szilvásvárad, about 20 km from Eger, for the Szalajka valley and its cascade, a favourite hiking spot (Visit Eger); no transit time was confirmed, so check Volánbusz and MÁV timetables for the connection
Option B: Eger Thermal Bath (Petőfi tér 2), described by Visit Eger as one of the nicest town baths in the country with 13 pools
Evening: a second tasting in the Szépasszony-völgy or the Beatles museum on Csiky Sándor utca if you prefer an indoor stop

days.title: Eger to Tokaj
activities: Rail and bus connections only: Eger to Füzesabony is about 20 minutes (Visit Eger), after which you need MÁV services toward Miskolc and the Miskolc-Nyíregyháza line that MÁV's Tokaj InterCity trains use. No total journey time from an operator was confirmed, so plan this as most of a day and check the MÁV timetable at jegy.mav.hu
Tokaj railway station is at Vasútállomás u. 18 (listed on the town's tokaj.hu site)
Evening in Tokaj: a wine bar dinner
days.drive_time: Eger-Füzesabony ~20 min; onward connection time not confirmed, check MÁV

days.title: Tokaj wine region
activities: Tokaj sits in the UNESCO World Heritage Tokaj Wine Region Historic Cultural Landscape (Hungarian Tourism Agency)

Book a cellar tasting in advance: the town's tokaj.hu site lists wineries with addresses and phone numbers (see its Borászatok page); ask for dry Furmint, Hárslevelű, Sárga Muskotály and Zéta and the sweet wines the region is known for
The town's site also lists a Tisza ferry crossing at Rév köz 16; it was listed in 2023, so check it is running before you plan around it
Tokaj holds a Wine Days festival in early June and a Harvest Days festival in early October (2026 editions on tokaj.hu: 4-7 June, 2-4 October); expect rooms to be taken at those times

days.title: Tokaj back to Budapest
activities: MÁV's Tokaj InterCity trains run between Budapest Keleti, Miskolc and Nyíregyháza according to MÁV's service notices; no journey time from MÁV was confirmed, so check jegy.mav.hu for a service on your day
Arrive Budapest Keleti and connect to your onward travel
days.drive_time: Rail via Miskolc; time not confirmed, check MÁV

food_culture.name: Egri Bikavér
food_culture.description: One of the best-known and best-selling Hungarian dry red wines and a symbol of Eger, suggested by Visit Eger with spicy dishes and game, served chilled to 15-17 C.

food_culture.name: Egri Csillag
food_culture.description: The white counterpart to Eger's bull's blood: a complex dry wine that Visit Eger recommends as an aperitif or with poultry and white meat, chilled to 10-12 C.

food_culture.name: Szépasszony-völgy cellar valley
food_culture.description: Eger's number one place for wine tasting: a valley of family cellars and terraces just outside the centre, with dozens of cellars listed by Visit Eger.

food_culture.name: Eger Minaret
food_culture.description: The only minaret in the world with a cross on top (Visit Eger).

food_culture.name: Tokaji dry and sweet wines
food_culture.description: Tokaj-Hegyalja is known for sweet wine, but the town's own site says most of the harvest is dry; its varietal wines are Furmint, Hárslevelű, Sárga Muskotály and Zéta (Oremus), with the sweet wines the region's calling card.

food_culture.name: Tokaj wine festivals
food_culture.description: Tokaj holds a Wine Days festival in early June and a Harvest Days festival in early October, both listed on the town's tokaj.hu events pages.

title: Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent + Bruges, Belgium
best_time_description: Late spring (May to June) and early autumn (September to October) are the usual comfortable windows for walking these cities; summer is the busiest period for Bruges and Ghent, so book the Bruges Belfry and the Ghent Altarpiece ahead whenever you go. Ghent holds its Gentse Feesten street festival each July, which fills hotels.
description: Belgium's classic first-timer arc, all on direct SNCB trains from Brussels: two nights in the capital with a day trip to Antwerp (41 minutes by train), then Ghent (36 minutes) and Bruges (about 30 minutes onward) before returning to Brussels (1 hour 4 minutes). Grand-Place and chocolate, Rubens' Antwerp, Ghent's medieval canals and altarpiece, and Bruges' belfry and canals, with only short rail hops between bases.

days.title: Arrive Brussels
activities: Settle in near Brussels-Midi, Brussels-Central or the Grand-Place; SNCB direct trains from Brussels reach Antwerp, Ghent and Bruges, so any central base works for the whole trip
Grand-Place and the surrounding lanes, then the Manneken Pis
Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert for a look at the covered shopping arcade and a chocolate shop or two

days.title: Brussels highlights + day trip to Antwerp
activities: Morning: Mont des Arts viewpoint and the Cathedral of St Michael and St Gudula
Direct SNCB train Brussels to Antwerp, about 41 minutes (Antwerp to Brussels is listed at about 39 minutes)
Antwerpen-Centraal station hall, then the Grote Markt with the Brabo fountain
Cathedral of Our Lady, which holds paintings by Rubens (check current opening hours and any entry fee on the cathedral's own site)
Walk the old centre and return to Brussels by train in the evening
days.drive_time: Brussels to Antwerp by direct SNCB train, about 41 min each way

days.title: Brussels to Ghent
activities: Direct SNCB train Brussels to Ghent, about 36 minutes (SNCB route page average); get off at Gent-Sint-Pieters and take tram 1 to the centre (every 10 minutes, per Visit Bruges)
Graslei and Korenlei waterfront, Gravensteen castle, and the Korenmarkt area

St Bavo's Cathedral for the Ghent Altarpiece (Adoration of the Mystic Lamb): tickets sell out quickly, especially on weekends and holidays, so book well in advance. The upper inner panels are under restoration until 31 December 2026: on weekends and holidays the panels are displayed to the public in the cathedral, while from Tuesday to Friday restorers work live at the Museum of Fine Arts (MSK), so plan the day of the week accordingly
Evening canal-side dinner in the old centre
days.drive_time: Brussels to Ghent by direct SNCB train, about 36 min

days.title: Ghent to Bruges
activities: Morning in Ghent: wander the Patershol quarter and the quieter canals before checking out
Direct train Ghent-Sint-Pieters to Bruges, about 30 minutes (Visit Bruges), one to four direct trains per hour
Bruges station is a 20-minute walk from the Market Square (Visit Bruges); city buses 1 and 2 run every five minutes from the station to the centre
Markt square, the Burg, and the Basilica of the Holy Blood
Evening canal-side walk around Minnewater and the Begijnhof
days.drive_time: Ghent to Bruges by direct train, about 30 min (Visit Bruges)

days.title: Bruges: belfry, canals + beer
activities: Belfry of Bruges on the Markt: Musea Brugge recommends booking a timed slot online in advance and entry is capped per hour; the tower can close in gusty or stormy weather, and its hours change by season and over holidays
Canal boat tour from the central landing stages
Groeninge Museum or Memling's works at the Sint-Janshospitaal (check each museum's current opening days)
Brewery tour at De Halve Maan or a tasting at a traditional beer cafe

days.title: Return to Brussels + departure
activities: Direct SNCB train Bruges to Brussels, 1 hour 4 minutes on average per SNCB, with about 65 trains a day on the route
Last chocolate shopping or the Atomium, depending on your flight time
days.drive_time: Bruges to Brussels by direct SNCB train, ~1 h 4 min average

food_culture.name: Belgian beer culture
food_culture.description: Belgium's beer culture, from Trappist ales to lambic and the traditional brown cafes, is recognised on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage. In Bruges, De Halve Maan brews in the city centre; in Brussels and Ghent, a tasting flight in a traditional beer cafe is the easiest way in.

food_culture.name: Moules-frites
food_culture.description: Mussels steamed in white wine, celery and onion, served with fries and mayonnaise, are the dish most associated with Belgian brasseries.

food_culture.name: Waterzooi
food_culture.description: A creamy stew of chicken (or fish) with vegetables and cream, long associated with Ghent, and a good test of a traditional restaurant there.

food_culture.name: Brussels waffles and Belgian chocolate
food_culture.description: The rectangular Brussels waffle is lighter and crisper than its Liège cousin and is served with sugar or toppings; pralines from the chocolate houses around the Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert and the Grand-Place are Brussels' other signature sweet.

food_culture.name: Cuberdons (Gentse neuzen)
food_culture.description: Cone-shaped, soft-centred raspberry-flavoured sweets that are a Ghent speciality, sold from street stalls and sweet shops around the old centre.

food_culture.name: Gentse Feesten
food_culture.description: Ghent's ten-day summer street festival, held each July, fills the old centre with music, theatre and street food stalls; book lodging well ahead if your dates overlap.

food_culture.name: Rubens and the Flemish Primitives
food_culture.description: Antwerp's Cathedral of Our Lady holds paintings by Rubens, while Bruges and Ghent are home to Flemish Primitive masterpieces, from Memling in Bruges to the Van Eyck Ghent Altarpiece in St Bavo's.

title: Namur, Dinant, Bastogne + Liège, Wallonia
best_time_description: May to September is the easiest window for the Meuse valley, the Dinant citadel and the Ardennes forests; The Bastogne War Museum lists itself as open every day, but the weather can be cold and wet outside summer, and Namur's Citadel visitor centre has shorter hours from November.
description: Wallonia's river-and-forest side of Belgium, away from the Flemish art cities: Namur's hilltop citadel, Dinant on the Meuse with its couques and Leffe beer heritage, the Ardennes town of Bastogne and its Battle of the Bulge sites, and Liège with its 374-step Montagne de Bueren. Rail covers Brussels to Namur (1 hour 1 minute) and Liège to Brussels (55 minutes); the Ardennes legs are easier with a hire car because no official public-transport time could be confirmed for them.

days.title: Brussels to Namur
activities: Direct SNCB train Brussels to Namur, about 1 hour 1 minute on average, 16 trains in peak hours per SNCB's current listing

Namur Citadel: take the cable car from Place Maurice Servais (8 minutes up, 8 minutes down per the Citadel site) or walk up; the Citadel's tourist train runs weekday afternoons and more often at weekends
Evening in the old town around Place d'Armes and the Meuse-Sambre confluence
days.drive_time: Brussels to Namur by direct SNCB train, ~1 h 1 min average

days.title: Namur Citadel + underground tour
activities: Terra Nova Visitor Centre in the former barracks: the 450-metre guided underground tour covers the Citadel's construction, military use and soldiers' daily life (check the booking page for departure times and whether to reserve)

Visitor Center hours per the Citadel site: 28 September to 1 November, daily 10:00-18:00; from 2 November to 3 January, closed Mondays and 10:00-17:00 on other days; closed 24 and 25 December 2026 and 1 January 2027
The Old Forge (La Forge) on the Citadel grounds opens Saturdays and Sundays 13:00-16:00 only; other days by appointment
Afternoon walk along the Meuse and Sambre quays

days.title: Namur to Dinant
activities: SNCB line 154 runs Namur to Dinant; check the SNCB planner for the current journey time and whether buses replace trains on the day (this line had replacement buses during works in May and June 2026)

Dinant Citadel above the Meuse: the Citadel's website says the cable car is closed for major renovation, so allow for the climb on the staircase. Tickets are sold at the ticket offices at the top and bottom; same-day online booking is not available (online booking is possible at least 24 hours ahead); a combined ticket with an augmented-reality guide and a Meuse cruise is on offer
Maison Leffe museum (the Leffe beer story, which began at the Abbaye de Leffe in 1240) and a couque de Dinant, the honey biscuit, at Maison Jacobs
Riverside walk past the Collegiate Church, with the rock face behind
days.drive_time: Namur to Dinant by SNCB line 154; time not confirmed, check the SNCB planner

days.title: Dinant to Bastogne
activities: By hire car to Bastogne (no official public-transport time could be confirmed). By public transport, take a train to Libramont and TEC bus line 6 to Bastogne, which per a TEC announcement runs hourly on weekdays and serves the Mardasson memorial and stops near the War Museum; check letec.be for the current timetable
Mardasson Memorial, the star-shaped monument to the American soldiers of the Battle of the Bulge on the hill beside the museum
Evening in Bastogne's Place McAuliffe and a taste of the local speciality biscuit

days.title: Bastogne: Battle of the Bulge
activities: Bastogne War Museum (Colline du Mardasson 5): open every day 9:30-18:00 per the museum's site, tickets via its online appointment system, so book a slot in advance
Bastogne War Rooms (Rue de la Roche 38D), listed by the museum on its own site
Bois Jacques Battlefield, the forest where US paratroopers dug in, listed by the museum as a separate site on the same ticketing system

days.title: Bastogne to Liège + return to Brussels
activities: To Liège by hire car, or check letec.be for TEC's express line E69 Liège-Bastogne-Arlon (days of operation and running time not confirmed here)
Montagne de Bueren, the 374-step staircase with a 30% gradient, accessible at all hours (VisitWallonia), up to the citadel hillside for the view
Liège-Guillemins station by Santiago Calatrava, a short stop before your train
Direct SNCB train Liège to Brussels, about 55 minutes per SNCB's current listing
days.drive_time: Liège to Brussels by direct SNCB train, ~55 min

food_culture.name: Couque de Dinant
food_culture.description: A very hard, honey-flavoured biscuit that is Dinant's traditional treat; locals advise dunking it in a warm drink first. Maison Jacobs still bakes them by hand.

food_culture.name: Leffe
food_culture.description: Leffe beer takes its name from the Abbaye de Leffe near Dinant, where it was first brewed in 1240. The abbey no longer stands and brewing is now in Leuven, but Maison Leffe in Dinant tells the story and ends with a tasting.

food_culture.name: Flamiche
food_culture.description: A cheese tart associated with Dinant, found in the town's bakeries and cafes.

food_culture.name: Liège waffle and boulets liégeois
food_culture.description: The Liège waffle is a denser, caramelised dough studded with sugar pearls, eaten warm and plain. Boulets liégeois are large meatballs in a sweet-sour sirop de Liège sauce, served with fries, the city's classic main dish.

food_culture.name: Ardennes ham and pate
food_culture.description: Cured ham and pates from the Ardennes forests are the staple of regional deli counters in Bastogne and the surrounding villages; they appear on charcuterie boards and sandwiches across the region.

food_culture.name: Bastogne Nuts
food_culture.description: A local spiced biscuit sold in Bastogne, named for General McAuliffe's reply of 'Nuts!' when the town was surrounded in December 1944.

food_culture.name: Battle of the Bulge remembrance
food_culture.description: Bastogne is the centre of Belgium's memory of the 1944 Battle of the Bulge: the Mardasson Memorial, the War Museum, the War Rooms and the Bois Jacques battlefield are the main sites, and the town marks the 1944 anniversary each winter; check dates locally.

food_culture.name: Belgian beer culture
food_culture.description: Belgian beer culture, covering Trappist and abbey ales, lambic and brown cafes, is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list; in Wallonia it extends from Leffe in Dinant to the abbey breweries in the south of the region.

title: Hong Kong Classics: Peak, Harbour + Big Buddha
best_time_description: October to December is the usual window for sightseeing: the weather is cooler and drier, which matters for the Victoria Peak views and the open-air Ngong Ping cable car. Summers are hot and humid, and weather can suspend the cable car and affect ferries.
description: Hong Kong's first-timer circuit: Victoria Peak by Peak Tram, the Star Ferry across the harbour, Kowloon's Temple Street night market and a day on Lantau Island with the Ngong Ping 360 cable car to the Tian Tan Buddha.

days.title: Arrive Hong Kong, Central + Hollywood Road
activities: Arrive at Hong Kong International Airport and travel into the city; settle into a hotel in Central or Tsim Sha Tsui
Walk Hollywood Road to Man Mo Temple to see the hanging incense coils
Dinner of Cantonese roast meats or wonton noodles at a neighbourhood restaurant in Central or Sheung Wan

days.title: Victoria Peak + Star Ferry
activities: Ride the Peak Tram from its lower terminus on Garden Road in Central up to Victoria Peak (a short ride; weekend and holiday queues can be long, so check the Peak Tram website for hours and tickets)
Walk the Lugard Road circuit around the Peak for harbour views, then ride the tram back down
Cross Victoria Harbour on the Star Ferry from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui (about 9 minutes per the operator's published timetables; check starferry.com.hk for current sailings)
Evening along the Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront promenade

days.title: Kowloon: Temple Street + markets
activities: Morning dim sum at a traditional restaurant in Tsim Sha Tsui, Yau Ma Tei or Mong Kok
Explore Kowloon street markets in Mong Kok, such as the Ladies' Market and Goldfish Market
Evening at the Temple Street night market in Yau Ma Tei for street food, stalls and fortune-telling
Late dinner at a dai pai dong or cha chaan teng
days.lodging_suggestion: Tsim Sha Tsui or Yau Ma Tei

days.title: Lantau Island: Ngong Ping 360 + Tian Tan Buddha
activities: Take the MTR to Tung Chung and leave through Exit B to the Ngong Ping 360 terminal

Ride the Ngong Ping 360 cable car to Ngong Ping, a 25-minute ride; the official site gives 10:00-18:00 on weekdays and 9:00-18:30 on weekends and public holidays, and says service is suspended on scheduled servicing days and in bad weather, so check np360.com.hk before you go
Walk about 10 minutes from Ngong Ping Village to the Tian Tan Buddha and Po Lin Monastery
Return by cable car to Tung Chung (or by NLB bus 23 to Tung Chung, about 50 minutes per NLB, if the cable car is not running)

days.title: Departure day
activities: Last-minute shopping or a milk tea and egg waffle breakfast at a cha chaan teng or street stall
Transfer to Hong Kong International Airport for departure

food_culture.name: Dim sum
food_culture.description: Cantonese dim sum, small steamed and fried dishes eaten with tea, is the classic Hong Kong morning-to-lunch meal; order from a trolley or a paper tick-sheet depending on the restaurant.

food_culture.name: Hong Kong-style milk tea
food_culture.description: A strong black tea blended and mixed with evaporated milk, served at the casual local cafes known as cha chaan teng, alongside toast, noodles and baked dishes.

food_culture.name: Egg waffles (gai daan jai)
food_culture.description: A Hong Kong street snack of bubble-shaped waffle sold hot from street stalls and markets, eaten by tearing off the bubbles.

food_culture.name: Cantonese roast meats and wonton noodles
food_culture.description: Hong Kong's neighbourhood restaurants are known for char siu (barbecued pork), roast goose and duck, and wonton noodle soup, usually served over rice or noodles.

food_culture.name: Dai pai dong and night-market eating
food_culture.description: Open-air street food stalls and night markets such as the one around Temple Street are part of everyday Hong Kong eating, with plastic stools, shared tables and cooked-to-order dishes.

food_culture.name: Man Mo Temple and incense coils
food_culture.description: Hong Kong's temples, such as Man Mo Temple on Hollywood Road, burn large hanging incense coils and honour the gods of literature (Man) and martial arts (Mo).

title: Hong Kong Outdoors: Sai Kung, Lamma + Tai O
best_time_description: October to January suits hiking and ferry days: cooler, drier weather makes the Dragon's Back ridge and Lamma's coastal path far more comfortable than in the hot, humid summer, when typhoon warnings can disrupt boats and cable cars.
description: Hong Kong beyond the skyline: the Sai Kung volcanic coast and Sharp Island, a car-free walk on Lamma Island, the stilt-house village of Tai O on Lantau, and the Dragon's Back ridge hike to the sea.

days.title: Arrive Hong Kong
activities: Arrive at Hong Kong International Airport and transfer to the hotel
Evening walk and a Hong Kong-style milk tea at a cha chaan teng near the hotel

days.title: Sai Kung Town + Sharp Island
activities: Take the MTR to Diamond Hill (Exit C2) and bus 92 to Sai Kung Town, or MTR to Choi Hung (Exit C2) and minibus 1A (routes per the Hong Kong Geopark site; confirm current timetables)
Walk the Sai Kung waterfront and visit the Volcano Discovery Centre in Sai Kung Waterfront Park
Take the kaito ferry from Sai Kung Pier to Sharp Island, about 15 minutes, in the Hong Kong UNESCO Global Geopark
On weekends and public holidays only: bus 94 from Sai Kung to Pak Tam Chung, then Green Minibus 9A to the High Island Reservoir East Dam to see the hexagonal volcanic rock columns
Seafood dinner on the Sai Kung waterfront

days.title: Lamma Island
activities: Take the Hong Kong & Kowloon Ferry from Central Pier 4 to Yung Shue Wan on Lamma Island (about 30 minutes)
Walk the family trail across Lamma from Yung Shue Wan to Sok Kwu Wan (the island is car-free; the walk is a few hours, so carry water)
Late seafood lunch in Sok Kwu Wan, then ferry back to Central (check the HKKF timetable, as Sok Kwu Wan sailings are less frequent)

days.title: Lantau: Tai O fishing village
activities: Take the MTR to Tung Chung (Exit B) and NLB bus 11 to Tai O (about 52 minutes end to end per NLB)
Walk Tai O's stilt-house waterways and market lanes, and look for local specialities such as dried seafood and shrimp paste

Optional: continue by NLB bus 21 to Ngong Ping (about 18 minutes; buses 07:30 to 18:15 Monday to Saturday and 18:30 on Sundays and public holidays) for the Tian Tan Buddha, then bus 23 or the Ngong Ping 360 cable car (25 minutes, weather and maintenance permitting) to Tung Chung

days.title: Dragon's Back ridge hike
activities: Take the MTR to Shau Kei Wan and bus 9 from the Shau Kei Wan bus terminus to the To Tei Wan (Dragon's Back) stop on Shek O Road, where the trailhead begins

Hike the Dragon's Back ridge in Shek O Country Park (Hong Kong Trail stage 8) towards Big Wave Bay; Discover Hong Kong lists roughly 8 km and about 4 hours, moderate difficulty; there are no shops on the trail, so carry plenty of water and avoid the weekend crowds if you can
Swim or eat at Big Wave Bay, then bus 9 from Big Wave Bay Road back to MTR Shau Kei Wan

days.title: Departure day
activities: Slow morning with dim sum
Transfer to Hong Kong International Airport for departure

food_culture.name: Dim sum
food_culture.description: Cantonese dim sum, small steamed and fried dishes eaten with tea, is the classic Hong Kong morning-to-lunch meal; order from a trolley or a paper tick-sheet depending on the restaurant.

food_culture.name: Hong Kong-style milk tea
food_culture.description: A strong black tea blended and mixed with evaporated milk, served at the casual local cafes known as cha chaan teng, alongside toast, noodles and baked dishes.

food_culture.name: Egg waffles (gai daan jai)
food_culture.description: A Hong Kong street snack of bubble-shaped waffle sold hot from street stalls and markets, eaten by tearing off the bubbles.

food_culture.name: Cantonese roast meats and wonton noodles
food_culture.description: Hong Kong's neighbourhood restaurants are known for char siu (barbecued pork), roast goose and duck, and wonton noodle soup, usually served over rice or noodles.

food_culture.name: Lamma Island seafood villages
food_culture.description: Sok Kwu Wan on Lamma Island is known for its waterfront seafood restaurants where fish and shellfish are picked from tanks and cooked to order.

food_culture.name: Tai O stilt houses
