food_culture.description: Tai O is a fishing village on Lantau Island where the traditional stilt houses over the tidal waterway remain a living part of local culture, and dried seafood and shrimp paste are local products.

title: Luang Prabang, Vang Vieng + Vientiane, Laos
best_time_description: The cooler, drier months from November to February are the most comfortable for walking Luang Prabang, the waterfall pools at Kuang Si and river activities around Vang Vieng. The rainy season runs roughly May to October, when river and waterfall conditions change; check local conditions before swimming or tubing.
description: Laos's classic north-to-capital arc: the UNESCO-listed temple town of Luang Prabang with the turquoise tiers of Kuang Si, the karst and river scenery of Vang Vieng, then the capital Vientiane, linked by the Laos-China Railway instead of long mountain bus rides.

days.title: Arrive Luang Prabang
activities: Arrive at Luang Prabang International Airport (one of the designated eVisa ports); complete the free Lao Digital Immigration Form online within 3 days before arrival
Walk the old-town peninsula between the Mekong and the Nam Khan River, the core of the UNESCO World Heritage town
Climb Mount Phousi for the view over both rivers at sunset
Browse the evening night market on the main street, Sisavangvong Road

days.title: Temples, alms and the Royal Palace
activities: Watch the dawn alms-giving (tak bat) from the roadside, quietly and at a respectful distance; do not touch the monks or use flash
Wat Xieng Thong, the 16th-century royal temple at the tip of the peninsula
Royal Palace Museum (the former royal palace, now the National Museum); opening days and hours vary, so check before you go
Slow riverside dinner of Luang Prabang dishes

days.title: Kuang Si Falls
activities: Road trip to Kuang Si Falls: the multi-tiered waterfall with turquoise pools; swim in the lower pools and walk up to the top of the falls
Visit the Kuang Si Bear Rescue Centre run by Free the Bears beside the entrance path
Entrance tickets are bought at the site; go early to avoid the busiest hours
Evening back in town for khao soi or lam

days.title: Pak Ou Caves by Mekong boat
activities: Hire a longtail boat on the Mekong to the Pak Ou Caves, two limestone caves holding thousands of Buddha images
Stop at Ban Xang Hai, the riverside village known for rice-whisky (lao-lao) making
Back in town: handicraft shopping for hand-woven silk and paper
Pack for the train tomorrow

days.title: Train to Vang Vieng
activities: Laos-China Railway train to Vang Vieng: I could not open the operator's own timetable, so no departure or journey time is given here. Check the current timetable and buy tickets at the station ticket office or in the operator's ticket app, and allow for the station being outside the town centre.
Arrive in Vang Vieng and settle in near the Nam Song River
Evening sunset walk along the river with the limestone peaks behind

days.title: Vang Vieng: river and caves
activities: Float or kayak the Nam Song River; ask your operator about current water levels, which change with the season
Swim at the Blue Lagoon, the cave-side pool at Tham Phu Kham, early to beat tour groups
Climb to Tham Chang (Jang) cave for the viewpoint over the valley
Dinner in town

days.title: Train to Vientiane
activities: Laos-China Railway train to Vientiane: I could not open the operator's own timetable, so no departure or journey time is given here. Check the current timetable and buy tickets at the station ticket office or in the operator's ticket app, and allow for the station being outside the town centre.
Arrive in Vientiane and check in near the Mekong riverfront
That Luang (Pha That Luang), the golden stupa regarded as Laos's national symbol
Patuxai, the victory monument; climb to the top for the view over the city
Evening along the Mekong riverfront

days.title: Vientiane: COPE and Buddha Park
activities: COPE Visitor Centre: free entry, about the legacy of unexploded ordnance (UXO) in Laos and prosthetics and rehabilitation; open daily but its own page lists two closing times (4:00 and 5:00 pm), so go by mid-afternoon
Xieng Khuan (Buddha Park) on the Mekong's bank, a sculpture park of Hindu and Buddhist figures; confirm transport and hours locally
Last coffee or Beerlao, then depart from Wattay International Airport (check-in rules are set by your airline)

food_culture.name: Khao soi (Luang Prabang style)
food_culture.description: Northern Lao noodle soup of flat rice noodles in a pork and tomato broth topped with minced pork, served with fresh herbs and chilli on the side; distinct from the Thai curry noodle dish of the same name.

food_culture.name: Or lam
food_culture.description: A Luang Prabang stew of meat or buffalo with aubergine, mushrooms, long beans and sakhan, a woody vine that gives it a numbing, peppery edge.

food_culture.name: Sticky rice (khao niao) and laap
food_culture.description: Glutinous rice eaten by hand with fingers, the staple of the Lao table, served beside laap, a minced meat or fish salad with lime, herbs and toasted rice powder; laap is regarded as a national dish.

food_culture.name: Tak bat dawn alms-giving
food_culture.description: Each morning in Luang Prabang monks walk the streets collecting offerings of sticky rice from lay people; it is a living religious practice, so observe quietly from a distance and do not treat it as a photo opportunity.

food_culture.name: Baci (basi) ceremony
food_culture.description: A traditional Lao ceremony in which elders tie white cotton strings around the wrists of guests or travellers to wish them health and good fortune; you leave the strings on for a few days.

food_culture.name: Beerlao and lao-lao
food_culture.description: Beerlao is the country's best-known beer, drunk across Laos; lao-lao is the local rice spirit, made in villages such as Ban Xang Hai on the Pak Ou route.

food_culture.name: Luang Prabang as a UNESCO World Heritage town
food_culture.description: UNESCO inscribed the town for its blend of traditional Lao urban architecture and colonial-era buildings; the peninsula between the Mekong and the Nam Khan holds its temples, royal and noble houses.

title: Pakse, Bolaven Plateau + 4000 Islands, Laos
best_time_description: November to February is the cooler, drier window for waterfall viewpoints on the Bolaven Plateau, the climb at Wat Phou and cycling on the Mekong islands. The rainy season runs roughly May to October, when roads on the plateau can be slow; confirm conditions locally.
description: Southern Laos at a slow pace: the Mekong city of Pakse, the coffee-growing waterfalls of the Bolaven Plateau, the Khmer-era Wat Phou at Champasak, then the Mekong islands of Si Phan Don (the 4000 Islands), where the river fans out into channels and falls.

days.title: Arrive Pakse
activities: Arrive at Pakse International Airport (a designated eVisa port); complete the free Lao Digital Immigration Form online within 3 days before arrival
Wander the Mekong riverfront and Dao Heuang market
Visit the hilltop Golden Buddha at Wat Phou Salao for the view over the Mekong and the Xe Don

days.title: Bolaven Plateau waterfalls and coffee
activities: Hire a driver or rent a motorbike for the Bolaven Plateau loop; I could not verify road times, so ask your guesthouse for a current estimate
Tad Fane (Tat Fane), the twin waterfall plunging into a gorge, and Tad Yuang
Visit a coffee plantation near Paksong and taste coffee from the plateau's volcanic soil
Overnight in or near Tad Lo

days.title: Tad Lo and Champasak
activities: Morning at the Tad Lo waterfalls and nearby villages, walking at the village's own pace and asking before photographing people
Continue to Champasak, the small Mekong town beside Wat Phou; arrange a driver or bus in Pakse and confirm times locally
Evening along the Mekong riverfront in Champasak

days.title: Wat Phou and the islands
activities: Wat Phou, the UNESCO-listed Khmer temple complex on the slope of Phou Kao mountain; the visit involves steps and a climb, so go early; tickets are bought on site
See the ancient axis from the riverbank to the mountaintop and the nearby Tomo Temple, part of the same World Heritage landscape
Head south to Ban Nakasang and take a boat to Don Det or Don Khon in Si Phan Don; confirm boat times with your guesthouse
Sunset over the Mekong channels
days.lodging_suggestion: Don Det or Don Khon, Si Phan Don

days.title: Si Phan Don by bicycle
activities: Cycle Don Khon: the old French railway bridge between Don Det and Don Khon and the remains of the colonial-era railway
Li Phi Falls (Tat Somphamit), the rapids where the Mekong squeezes through rock channels
Relax by the river with a hammock and Lao dishes of Mekong fish
days.lodging_suggestion: Don Det or Don Khon, Si Phan Don

days.title: Khone Phapheng Falls and onward
activities: Visit Khone Phapheng Falls on the mainland, among the largest waterfalls on the Mekong by volume
Optional boat trip near Ban Hang Khone to look for the rare Irrawaddy dolphin; sightings are not guaranteed and tour boats should keep their distance
Return towards Pakse for a flight or onward bus; confirm onward transport times with your guesthouse

food_culture.name: Bolaven Plateau coffee
food_culture.description: The volcanic-soil plateau around Paksong is Laos's main coffee-growing area; plantation visits near Paksong serve coffee grown on the plateau.

food_culture.name: Mok pa (steamed fish in banana leaf)
food_culture.description: Mekong river fish mixed with herbs, chilli and dill, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed or grilled; common in riverside restaurants in Champasak and Si Phan Don.

food_culture.name: Khao piak sen
food_culture.description: A Lao noodle soup of thick, hand-cut rice-and-tapioca noodles in a chicken or pork broth, a common breakfast and lunch across the country including Pakse's markets.

food_culture.name: Khao niao and jeow
food_culture.description: Sticky rice eaten by hand with jeow, Lao dipping sauces made from roasted chilli, herbs and fermented fish or tomato.

food_culture.name: Boun Wat Phou festival
food_culture.description: An annual Buddhist festival held at Wat Phou in Champasak with processions and offerings around the Magha full moon, usually February; confirm the date before planning around it.

food_culture.name: Wat Phou's Khmer heritage
food_culture.description: UNESCO describes the temple complex as one of the most significant sites associated with the Khmer Empire, part of a designed landscape with a road that once led to Angkor.

food_culture.name: Mekong river life in Si Phan Don
food_culture.description: On the islands the river fans out into channels and falls; fishing, rice farming and boat transport still shape daily life, and the railway bridge between Don Det and Don Khon is a remnant of the French colonial period.

title: Tashkent, Samarkand, Bukhara + Khiva, Uzbekistan
best_time_description: April to early June and September to October are the comfortable windows: warm days and cool evenings for walking the monuments. Summer in Bukhara and Khiva is very hot, so shift sightseeing to early morning and late afternoon, and winter is cold with fewer visitors.
description: The classic Silk Road loop: Tashkent's bazaars, Samarkand's Registan and Timurid tombs, Bukhara's walkable old town of domes and madrasas, and the walled desert city of Khiva. Samarkand and Bukhara are linked by the Afrosiyob high-speed train; the long leg to Khiva is the one hard day.

days.title: Arrive Tashkent
activities: Arrive and register your stay: hotels normally register foreign guests with the authorities, so keep the slip
Chorsu Bazaar: domed market hall for dried fruit, nuts, bread and spices
Evening plov in Tashkent; the Central Asian Plov Center is the best-known place for the festive pilaf cooked in giant cauldrons
days.lodging_suggestion: Tashkent (old town or near Amir Timur Square)

days.title: Tashkent to Samarkand by Afrosiyob
activities: Afrosiyob high-speed train, Tashkent to Samarkand in about 2 hours 15 minutes (an Uzbekistan Railways schedule reported by UzDaily had train 776 leaving Tashkent 13:56 and reaching Samarkand 16:14, 2 h 18 min; morning departures also run, so check the timetable at eticket.uzrailpass.uz and book ahead)
Check in near the Registan and walk the lit-up squares in the evening
Dinner of Samarkand-style plov or lagman

days.title: Samarkand: Registan and the great tombs
activities: Registan: the three madrasas (Ulugh Beg, Sher-Dor, Tilya-Kori); entry is ticketed
Gur-e-Amir, the mausoleum of Timur
Bibi-Khanym Mosque and Siab Bazaar next door, where Samarkand's round non bread is sold

days.title: Samarkand to Bukhara
activities: Early at Shah-i-Zinda, the avenue of tiled mausoleums
Ulugh Beg Observatory on Chupan-Ata hill
Afternoon Afrosiyob to Bukhara, about 1 hour 30 minutes (third-party listings show 1 h 31 to 1 h 37; confirm the departure time on eticket.uzrailpass.uz)
Evening at Lyabi-Hauz, the pool plaza at the heart of old Bukhara

days.title: Bukhara old town
activities: Poi Kalon complex: Kalyan minaret and Mir-i-Arab madrasa
The Ark of Bukhara, the old citadel
The trading domes (Toki Zargaron and Toki Sarrafon) for suzani, ceramics and knives
Evening tea at a choyxona

days.title: Bukhara: tombs and palaces
activities: Samanid Mausoleum, a 10th-century brick tomb
Chashma-Ayub and Bolo-Hauz Mosque
Chor Minor, the four-minaret gatehouse
Sitorai Mokhi-Khosa, the last emir's summer palace outside the old town

days.title: Bukhara to Khiva across the Kyzylkum
activities: Long overland day: the road is about 430 km and takes around 7 hours by car; a daytime train is usually reported at about 6 hours (no current timetable was confirmed, so check eticket.uzrailpass.uz)
Arrive Khiva in the afternoon and walk the Itchan Kala walls at sunset

days.title: Khiva: Itchan Kala
activities: Itchan Kala, the walled inner city (UNESCO World Heritage); entry is ticketed
Kalta Minor, the turquoise unfinished minaret
Tash Khauli Palace and Kunya-Ark
Islam Khoja Minaret view; Juma Mosque with its forest of carved wooden columns

days.title: Khiva and onward
activities: Morning walk on the Itchan Kala walls

Return to Tashkent: Jaloliddin Manguberdi high-speed train (reported timetable: Tashkent 07:00 to Khiva 14:31, 7 h 31 min, running from Tashkent Tue/Thu/Sat with returns from Khiva Wed/Fri/Sun; confirm days and times with Uzbekistan Railways) or a domestic flight from Urgench (about 35 km from Khiva; book ahead)

food_culture.name: Plov (osh)
food_culture.description: Uzbekistan's national dish of rice cooked with lamb or beef, carrots and chickpeas in a kazan. Each region has its own version; in Tashkent it is traditionally eaten at midday in large plov centres.

food_culture.name: Non (tandoor bread)
food_culture.description: Round, stamped bread baked on the walls of a clay tandoor. Samarkand's thick non, patterned with a chekich stamp, is the best known; bread is treated with respect and never put face down on a table.

food_culture.name: Shivit oshi
food_culture.description: A Khorezm speciality of bright green dill-infused noodles served with a meat and vegetable stew and yogurt, found in Khiva.

food_culture.name: Samsa
food_culture.description: Pastry baked in the tandoor, usually filled with minced lamb and onion; Bukhara and Samarkand bakeries sell them hot in the morning.

food_culture.name: Green tea at a choyxona
food_culture.description: Tea is served in a pot with small bowls (piyola) in teahouses and homes; the host pours a bowl and returns it to the pot three times before serving, and guests are offered dried fruit, nuts and sweets alongside.

food_culture.name: Suzani embroidery
food_culture.description: Bright hand-embroidered silk and cotton cloths, traditionally a bride's dowry. Bukhara and Samarkand workshops and the Bukhara trading domes are the places to see them made and sold.

food_culture.name: Registan and the madrasa tradition
food_culture.description: The Registan's three tiled madrasas in Samarkand are the best surviving example of Timurid and later Central Asian religious architecture, with blue-tiled domes and ornamented portals.

food_culture.name: Khiva's Itchan Kala
food_culture.description: The walled inner town of Khiva is a living old city of mosques, madrasas and minarets inside mud-brick walls, one of the best-preserved Silk Road cities in Central Asia.

title: Fergana Valley: Kokand, Rishtan + Margilan, Uzbekistan
best_time_description: April to June and September to October for pleasant weather and orchards in bloom or harvest. July and August are hot, and winter is cold. The valley is a craft heartland rather than a monument circuit, so the mood is workshops and bazaars.
description: The Fergana Valley is Uzbekistan's craft heartland, east of Tashkent. Kokand's khan's palace, Rishtan's blue-glazed ceramics, Margilan's silk and ikat, and Andijan, the birthplace of Babur, make a quieter route than the Silk Road cities. Transfers between towns are short, so most time is spent in workshops and bazaars.

days.title: Arrive Tashkent
activities: Arrive and register your stay (hotels usually do this)
Chorsu Bazaar and the old-town Khast-Imam complex with its Quran of Caliph Uthman
Plov dinner

days.title: Tashkent to Kokand
activities: Morning train from Tashkent to Kokand (a tour operator lists the journey at about 4 hours 15 minutes; confirm times on eticket.uzrailpass.uz and book ahead)
Khudayar Khan Palace, built in 1873 by the last khan of Kokand
Juma Mosque with its wooden columns, and the Dahmai Shokhon necropolis

days.title: Kokand to Rishtan
activities: About one hour by car to Rishtan (operator estimate)
Rishtan's potters' workshops, famous for blue and turquoise glazes, and the International Ceramics Center
Continue about one hour to Margilan (operator estimate) in the afternoon

days.title: Margilan silk and ikat
activities: Yodgorlik Silk Factory in Margilan, where silk is reeled, dyed and woven by hand for ikat (ask about guided tours)
Margilan Crafts Development Center in a 19th-century madrasa
Margilan's old town and bazaar

days.title: Andijan and return
activities: Andijan, birthplace of Babur, founder of the Mughal dynasty, and the Babur memorial and museum
Evening or midday train back to Tashkent (confirm the Andijan to Tashkent timetable at eticket.uzrailpass.uz and book ahead; the train time was not confirmed in this research)

days.title: Tashkent and departure
activities: Tashkent Metro stations with their ornate Soviet-era design
Amir Timur Square and Independence Square
Depart or continue to the Silk Road cities

food_culture.name: Fergana plov
food_culture.description: Plov, the national rice-and-meat dish, is cooked in a kazan in every valley town and eaten at midday and at celebrations; each town claims its own version.

food_culture.name: Manti and samsa
food_culture.description: Steamed dumplings and tandoor-baked pastry filled with lamb and onion are bazaar staples throughout the valley.

food_culture.name: Dried fruit and nuts
food_culture.description: The valley's orchards supply apricots, raisins, walnuts and almonds sold by weight in every bazaar.

food_culture.name: Green tea at a choyxona
food_culture.description: Tea is served in a pot with small bowls; sharing a pot with a host is the standard sign of hospitality across the valley.

food_culture.name: Margilan ikat (khan atlas)
food_culture.description: Silk threads are tie-dyed before weaving to give the blurred patterns of ikat. Margilan is Uzbekistan's best-known centre for it, and many weavers still work by hand.

food_culture.name: Rishtan ceramics
food_culture.description: Rishtan potters make plates and bowls with a blue-green glaze coloured with ishkor, a plant ash, and decorated by hand; many family workshops open to visitors.

food_culture.name: Babur and the Fergana Valley
food_culture.description: Zahiruddin Muhammad Babur, founder of the Mughal dynasty, was born in Andijan in 1483, linking the valley to India's history; he later wrote his memoirs, the Baburnama, about the valley.

food_culture.name: Kokand Khanate
food_culture.description: Kokand was the capital of an independent khanate in the 18th and 19th centuries; the Khudayar Khan Palace is its surviving showpiece.

title: Havana, Viñales, Cienfuegos + Trinidad, Cuba
best_time_description: The dry months, roughly December to April, are the sensible window; the Atlantic hurricane season runs from early June to the end of November and the rainy season from April to October, which can bring flooding and damaged roads (Global Affairs Canada). Before booking: the UK FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cuba and the German Federal Foreign Office (19 Oct 2026) strongly advises against travel, citing a fuel and power crisis, reduced flights and limited long-distance buses; Global Affairs Canada reports daily unpredictable power cuts. Plan for power cuts, carry cash and a printed D'Viajeros QR code, and keep flexible bookings.
description: Cuba's classic first-timer arc: Old Havana and the Malecón, a tobacco-valley stop in Viñales, the French-planned bayside city of Cienfuegos and colonial Trinidad, finishing back in Havana. Intercity transport in Cuba is disrupted by fuel shortages, so treat every leg as provisional and confirm it locally.

days.title: Arrive Havana
activities: Arrive at José Martí International Airport (the UK FCDO says only Terminal 3 is operating); confirm your flight is still running before you go
Complete the D'Viajeros form beforehand and carry the QR code and proof of medical insurance
Check in to a casa particular or hotel in Vedado or Habana Vieja
Evening walk on the Malecón seafront promenade

days.title: Old Havana
activities: Habana Vieja, the historic centre, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982 (cuba.travel)
Catedral de la Habana and the squares around it
Walk the old streets toward the harbour; El Morro fortress across the bay
Live music in the evening

days.title: Malecón, Vedado + Hotel Nacional
activities: Morning at Hotel Nacional de Cuba on the Malecón
Walk through Vedado's tree-lined streets
Optional: look into the tickets for a ballet or music evening (Havana hosts an international ballet festival, listed on cuba.travel; dates vary)

days.title: Havana to Viñales
activities: Travel west to Viñales; the road and bus options change with fuel supply. Ask your casa particular or a Cuban state agency for a transfer, or a Viazul seat if the service runs. Check the operator for the current timetable and book ahead; I could not open a timetable I could verify.
Settle in and see the valley at sunset
days.drive_time: Duration not verified from an operator source; confirm when booking

days.title: Viñales valley
activities: Walk or ride through the valley among the limestone mogotes
Visit a tobacco farm to see how cigars are rolled
Book any guided excursion through your host

days.title: Viñales to Cienfuegos (long transit day)
activities: Return east via Havana and on to Cienfuegos; this is the longest and least predictable leg of the trip, so book transport in advance and expect to lose most of the day. No operator timetable was verified for this leg
Evening stroll on Parque José Martí
days.drive_time: Duration not verified; allow most of the day

days.title: Cienfuegos to Trinidad
activities: Morning in Cienfuegos: the historic centre, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2005 for its 19th-century planned layout (cuba.travel), Parque José Martí and the Malecón
Castillo de Jagua is the area's fortress, seen from the bay (cuba.travel names it); ask locally how to visit

Move on to Trinidad; Escambray (11 Feb 2026) reported a Viazul service Trinidad-Cienfuegos-Playa Larga-Varadero running unaffected by fuel cuts then. Check the operator for the current timetable and book ahead; I could not open a timetable I could verify.
days.drive_time: Duration not verified from an operator source

days.title: Trinidad
activities: Walk Trinidad's historic centre
Torre Manaca Iznaga in the Valle de los Ingenios sugar valley (named on cuba.travel)
Playa Ancón on the Península Ancón: cuba.travel lists a tourist beach bus with departures at 9:00, 11:00, 14:00 and 17:00 (returns 10:30, 12:30, 15:00, 18:00); confirm it is running
Live music in the evening

days.title: Trinidad to Havana, depart
activities: Travel to Havana; Escambray (11 Feb 2026) listed a Viazul service Trinidad-Havana airport-Havana terminal as unaffected then. Check the operator for the current timetable and book ahead; I could not open a timetable I could verify.
Fly home; allow extra time because fuel shortages have cut flights
days.drive_time: Duration not verified from an operator source

food_culture.name: Ropa vieja and moros y cristianos
food_culture.description: Shredded stewed beef in tomato sauce served with rice cooked with black beans, found on menus at paladares (privately run restaurants) and casa particular dinners across the island. Supplies are tight, so menus can be short.

food_culture.name: Mojito and daiquiri
food_culture.description: Rum-based Havana classics, served in the old town bars; ask for the rum brand and whether ice and mint are available during shortages.

food_culture.name: Son music
food_culture.description: Cuban son, with guitar, tres and percussion, is played live in bars and plazas in Havana and Trinidad; cuba.travel lists 'bailes y sones cubanos' as part of daily life in Havana.

food_culture.name: Casas particulares
food_culture.description: Rooms in family homes, the standard budget lodging, usually with breakfast and dinner on request. Ask about backup power and water before you book.

food_culture.name: Tobacco farming in Viñales
food_culture.description: Small farms in the valley grow tobacco and roll cigars by hand for visitors; buying cigars on the street risks fakes, so buy from official shops or farms.

title: Havana + Varadero Beach Week, Cuba
best_time_description: December to April is the dry, cooler window and the best time for the beach; the Atlantic hurricane season runs from early June to the end of November (Global Affairs Canada). Before booking: the UK FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cuba and the German Federal Foreign Office (19 Oct 2026) strongly advises against travel, citing a fuel and power crisis, reduced flights and limited long-distance buses; Global Affairs Canada reports daily unpredictable power cuts. A beach-resort base keeps logistics simpler than touring, but hotels outside the big resorts can still lose power and fuel for transfers is capped.
description: Three days in Havana, then the Hicacos Peninsula resort strip at Varadero for beach time, with a stop along the Vía Blanca coast road. A shorter route with just two bases, suited to people who want a beach after the city and less intercity travel.

days.title: Arrive Havana
activities: Arrive at José Martí International Airport; confirm your flight is still operating
Complete D'Viajeros beforehand and carry the QR code and proof of medical insurance
Settle in at a casa particular or hotel in Vedado
Evening along the Malecón

days.title: Habana Vieja
activities: Habana Vieja, the historic centre, UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982 (cuba.travel)
Catedral de la Habana and the old squares
El Morro fortress across the harbour

days.title: Vedado + Hotel Nacional
activities: Hotel Nacional de Cuba on the Malecón
Vedado's streets and neighbourhood cafés
Evening music or ballet if a performance is on; schedules and festival dates vary

days.title: Havana to Varadero via the Vía Blanca
activities: Transfer east along the Vía Blanca coast road; a private transfer arranged through your host makes the stops below possible. A Viazul bus is the cheaper option if it runs on this route: Check the operator for the current timetable and book ahead; I could not open a timetable I could verify.
Possible stops listed by cuba.travel: Peñón del Fraile (Km 55, Santa Cruz del Norte, known for its piña colada) and the Mirador de Bacunayagua lookout (Km 82)
Check in at Varadero and take a first walk on the beach
days.drive_time: Duration not verified from an operator source; confirm when booking

days.title: Varadero beach day
activities: Beach day on the Hicacos Peninsula
Ask your hotel about snorkelling or boat excursions; availability depends on fuel and weather

days.title: Matanzas or a second beach day
activities: Option A: day trip to the city of Matanzas for the old centre; confirm transport locally
Option B: another day at the beach and a sunset walk

days.title: Return to Havana and depart
activities: Transfer back to Havana. Escambray (11 Feb 2026) listed a Viazul route Trinidad-Cienfuegos-Playa Larga-Varadero, so Varadero is on the bus network, but check the Havana leg. Check the operator for the current timetable and book ahead; I could not open a timetable I could verify.
Fly home; allow extra time because fuel shortages have cut flights
days.drive_time: Duration not verified from an operator source

food_culture.name: Piña colada at Peñón del Fraile
food_culture.description: cuba.travel lists Peñón del Fraile, on the Vía Blanca at Km 55 in Santa Cruz del Norte, as a bar known for its piña colada.

food_culture.name: Grilled chicken at Roca Azul
food_culture.description: cuba.travel lists the Roca Azul restaurant (Carretera Central, Km 68, Madruga) for its grilled chicken; it sits on the central highway rather than the coast road, so only stop if you travel by that route.

food_culture.name: Langosta and fish dishes in Varadero
food_culture.description: Seafood is the beach-resort staple. Cuban lobster is a famous dish, but availability and prices vary, so check the price first.

food_culture.name: Cuban son and trova
food_culture.description: Live acoustic music in Havana's bars and squares; cuba.travel lists 'bailes y sones cubanos' as part of everyday life in the capital.

food_culture.name: Paladares
food_culture.description: Privately run restaurants, often in family homes, are where many travellers eat in Havana. Menus depend on what supplies the owner could find that day.

title: Montego Bay, Negril + Ocho Rios, Jamaica
best_time_description: December to April is the dry season (the Jamaica Tourist Board gives the wet season as May to November), so beaches, Dunn's River Falls and the long drives are easiest then. Hurricane Melissa (October 2025) badly damaged western Jamaica. The Jamaica Tourist Board's hotel tracker (visitjamaica.com/travel-alerts/hotel-reopenings, rolling updates, no date shown) lists most Negril and Ocho Rios properties as open but ten Montego Bay properties as reopening later, mostly in 2027, so confirm that your hotel and each attraction is operating before you book. Dunn's River Falls keeps its regular hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. daily, but opens at 7:00 a.m. on Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, which are its cruise-ship days, so expect crowds on those mornings.
description: Jamaica's north coast in one arc: the Hip Strip and Doctor's Cave Beach in Montego Bay, Seven Mile Beach and the cliffs of Negril, then Dunn's River Falls and the waterfalls around Ocho Rios, finishing with a stop at the Green Grotto Caves on the way back to the airport.

days.title: Arrive Montego Bay
activities: Land at Sangster International Airport, which the Jamaica Tourist Board describes as just around the corner from the Hip Strip (Jimmy Cliff Boulevard, on Gloucester Avenue)
Swim and snorkel at Doctor's Cave Beach, where snorkel and scuba gear can be rented
Dinner on the Hip Strip

days.title: Rose Hall + Falmouth
activities: Tour Rose Hall Great House and hear the legend of Annie Palmer; check the current tour times with the house before you go
Drive to the historic town of Falmouth in Trelawny, which the Jamaica Tourist Board puts about 45 minutes outside Montego Bay

At dusk, a boat tour on the Luminous Lagoon near Falmouth (the Jamaica Tourist Board suggests going at dusk); the tour operators set their own departure times, and the Jamaica Tourist Board's attraction-status page lists the Falmouth lagoon tours as open
Rafting on the Martha Brae River is listed as closed on that status page, so do not plan around it unless it has reopened
days.drive_time: Montego Bay to Falmouth, about 45 minutes

days.title: Montego Bay to Negril
activities: Drive from Montego Bay to Negril, about 1 hour 30 minutes according to the Jamaica Tourist Board
Walk or swim on Seven Mile Beach
Watch the sunset, then head to Rick's Cafe (listed as open on the Jamaica Tourist Board status page), known for cliff jumping
days.drive_time: Montego Bay to Negril, about 1 hour 30 minutes
days.lodging_suggestion: Negril (Seven Mile Beach or the cliffs)

days.title: Negril beaches + cliffs
activities: Spend the day on Seven Mile Beach or on the quieter cliff side of Negril, where boutique hotels overlook the water
Optional sunset and evening at Rick's Cafe if you did not go on day 3
days.lodging_suggestion: Negril (Seven Mile Beach or the cliffs)

days.title: Negril to Ocho Rios
activities: Drive from Negril back through Montego Bay (Negril to Montego Bay is about 1 hour 30 minutes per the Jamaica Tourist Board) and on along the north coast to Ocho Rios. No official minute figure for Montego Bay to Ocho Rios was found; the Prime Minister has said congestion on parts of this road adds to travel time, so check a live map and treat this as a half-day of driving
Stop at Puerto Seco Beach in Discovery Bay if you want a swim; the Jamaica Tourist Board places it about halfway between Ocho Rios and Montego Bay
Evening in Ocho Rios
days.drive_time: Negril to Montego Bay about 1 hour 30 minutes, then Montego Bay to Ocho Rios (allow roughly half a day for the whole transfer)

days.title: Dunn's River Falls + Konoko Falls
activities: Climb Dunn's River Falls (Urban Development Corporation park, open daily 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays; the Jamaica Tourist Board says it is a five-minute drive from the Ocho Rios cruise port); tickets are bought at the park entry, and the park has a waiver and release form, so read it before you climb
Konoko Falls, 5 to 10 minutes from the Ocho Rios port per the Jamaica Tourist Board (listed as open)
Optional: Mystic Mountain (listed as open on the status page)
days.drive_time: Ocho Rios port to Dunn's River Falls, about 5 minutes; to Konoko Falls, 5 to 10 minutes

days.title: Green Grotto Caves + departure
activities: Drive west along the north coast toward Montego Bay and stop at the Green Grotto Caves (listed as open on the Jamaica Tourist Board status page); the Jamaica Tourist Board puts them about 30 minutes east of the Martha Brae Rafting Village
Fly home from Sangster International Airport, or from Norman Manley International Airport in Kingston, which the Jamaica Tourist Board puts about 90 minutes from Ocho Rios
days.drive_time: Ocho Rios to Kingston airport, about 90 minutes (Jamaica Tourist Board); Ocho Rios to Montego Bay not officially timed, check a live map

food_culture.name: Jerk chicken and pork
food_culture.description: Jerk is Jamaica's best-known dish: pork or chicken seasoned with pimento (allspice) and hot pepper and smoked slowly. The Jamaica Tourist Board says Boston Bay in Portland is known for it, and jerk is sold by street vendors in Kingston at night.

food_culture.name: Ackee and saltfish
food_culture.description: The national dish: the soft, yellow ackee fruit cooked with salted cod, onion and pepper, often served at breakfast with fried dumpling or breadfruit. Ackee must be fully ripe and properly prepared, so eat it at a restaurant or cook shop rather than improvising.

food_culture.name: Patties
food_culture.description: The flaky, turmeric-yellow Jamaican pastry filled with beef, curried goat, callaloo or other fillings; the Jamaica Tourist Board lists Devon House Bakery in Kingston for lobster, curry goat, beef and callaloo patties.

food_culture.name: Rum
food_culture.description: Jamaica has long-established rum estates; the Jamaica Tourist Board's itinerary names Hampden Estate and Appleton Estate. Appleton is described as about a two-hour drive south of the Montego Bay area, so it needs its own day and is not part of this route.

food_culture.name: Bamboo-raft river rides
food_culture.description: Rafting on the Martha Brae River near Falmouth is a long-running north-coast visitor tradition. The Jamaica Tourist Board's status page lists it as closed at the time of research, so check whether it has reopened.

food_culture.name: Reggae and Rastafari
food_culture.description: Reggae is Jamaica's signature sound, and the Jamaica Tourist Board points visitors to Rick's Cafe in Negril and the Hip Strip in Montego Bay for nightlife. For the genre's roots go to Kingston's Trench Town and the Bob Marley Museum, which is on the East Jamaica itinerary.

title: Kingston, Blue Mountains + Port Antonio, Jamaica
best_time_description: December to April is the dry season, which the Jamaica Tourist Board gives as the best time to hike Blue Mountain Peak (wet season May to November). Check the day of the week before you fix dates: the Bob Marley Museum is closed on Sundays and some major public holidays, and Reach Falls is reported to be open Wednesday to Sunday only. Eastern Jamaica (Kingston and Port Antonio) is the part of the island the Jamaica Tourist Board's hotel tracker shows with every listed property open, but Hurricane Melissa (October 2025) did damage roads in Portland and St. Thomas, so confirm road and attraction status before you go.
description: Reggae history and coffee in the hills, then the quiet green east: the Bob Marley Museum and Devon House in Kingston, Blue Mountain coffee and Blue Mountain Peak, then Port Antonio's jerk, rafting and waterfalls.

days.title: Arrive Kingston
activities: Land at Norman Manley International Airport, about 20 minutes from downtown Kingston and about 30 minutes from the New Kingston business district (Jamaica Tourist Board)
Devon House, the mansion of George Stiebel, Jamaica's first Black millionaire, with a patty from its bakery and ice cream from I-Scream (flavours include rum and raisin, stout, coconut and guava)
days.drive_time: Airport to downtown Kingston, about 20 minutes; to New Kingston, about 30 minutes

days.title: Bob Marley Museum + Trench Town
activities: Bob Marley Museum, 56 Hope Road: open Monday to Saturday, with guided tours every hour from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.; closed Sundays and some major public holidays; allow about 75 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes; adults 13 and over US$25, ages 4 to 12 US$12, 3 and under free; the museum asks guests to book tours online in advance. If this day falls on a Sunday, swap it with another day
Trench Town Culture Yard, which the Jamaica Tourist Board calls the cradle of reggae
National Gallery of Jamaica, the largest and oldest public art museum in the Caribbean (established 1974); check its opening days before you go

days.title: Blue Mountain coffee
activities: Drive up to Irish Town for a one-hour tour of Craighton Estate (owned by the Japan-based Ueshima Coffee Company): a walk round the working coffee farm and historic great house, the history of Jamaican coffee and a tasting. The Jamaica Tourist Board's status page lists it as open; no official hours or booking rules were found, so confirm with the estate

Alternatively or additionally, Mavis Bank Coffee Factory, the only fully integrated Jamaica Blue Mountain Coffee facility (a processing tour of about 45 minutes ending with a cup of coffee); hours and reservations were not confirmed from an official page, so call ahead
Optional: Holywell in the Blue and John Crow Mountains National Park, where rangers lead guided walks and run a visitors' centre
days.drive_time: Kingston to Irish Town: no official drive time found, check a live map; Holywell is about 20 minutes' drive from RafJam in Irish Town (Jamaica Tourist Board)
days.lodging_suggestion: Holywell cabins, Whitfield Hall or Wildflower Lodge (Blue Mountains)

days.title: Blue Mountain Peak (optional)
activities: Hike Blue Mountain Peak (7,402 ft, the island's highest point) from the trailhead near Whitfield Hall: about 7 miles up, roughly 4 hours up and about 7 hours for the whole trail. The road to the trailhead needs four-wheel drive. Lodges such as Whitfield Hall and Wildflower Lodge arrange local guides and pickups from Kingston or Mavis Bank, and the Jamaica Conservation and Development Trust (JCDT) arranges Portland Gap hikes with rustic accommodation. Many hikers start in the small hours to catch sunrise; take a flashlight and warm layers, as the summit is cold and windy
Rest-day alternative: coffee estates, Holywell, or a quiet day in the hills
days.drive_time: Peak hike: about 4 hours up, about 7 hours round trip
days.lodging_suggestion: Whitfield Hall, Wildflower Lodge or Portland Gap cabins

days.title: Kingston to Port Antonio
activities: Drive from Kingston to Port Antonio, about 2 hours (the Jamaica Tourist Board describes a two-hour transfer; it also gives about 2.5 hours for Portland from Ocho Rios or Kingston, so allow 2 to 2.5 hours). A JUTC bus, route 710, was launched on 23 September 2026 between Port Antonio and downtown Kingston via St. Thomas, Monday to Saturday, with a trip described as about two hours; the schedule had not been published, so confirm it
Jerk at Boston Bay (Jamaica Tourist Board: Boston Bay is known for jerk pork and chicken; Boston Beach is listed as open)
Swim at Frenchman's Cove (listed as open), where river water runs into the sea, or at Blue Lagoon
days.drive_time: Kingston to Port Antonio, about 2 hours (Jamaica Tourist Board)

days.title: Reach Falls + Rio Grande
activities: Reach Falls for emerald pools and hidden caves (listed as open on the Jamaica Tourist Board status page). The Urban Development Corporation is reported to open it Wednesday to Sunday and public holidays, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed Mondays and Tuesdays; that schedule comes from a guidebook and an undated UDC notice, so confirm before driving out. No official drive time from Port Antonio was found
Bamboo-raft trip on the Rio Grande starting at Rafter's Rest (listed as open on the status page); tour length and prices were not found, so check with the raft captains

days.title: Return to Kingston + depart
activities: Drive back to Kingston and Norman Manley International Airport (about 2 hours to Kingston, then about 20 to 30 minutes across town; leave a buffer for a flight)
Optional stops: Somerset Falls, described by the Jamaica Tourist Board as a swimming and relaxing spot on a former plantation
days.drive_time: Port Antonio to Kingston, about 2 hours

food_culture.name: Boston Bay jerk
food_culture.description: The Jamaica Tourist Board calls Port Antonio Jamaica's home of jerk and says Boston Bay is known for jerk pork and chicken. Eat it at the roadside jerk centres there, typically with festival or bammy.

food_culture.name: Jamaica Blue Mountain coffee
food_culture.description: Grown in the Blue Mountains and processed at Mavis Bank Coffee Factory, the island's largest integrated Blue Mountain facility, and at estates such as Craighton. Tours end with a cup, so you can taste it where it is grown.

food_culture.name: Devon House patties and ice cream
food_culture.description: Devon House Bakery's patties come in fillings such as lobster, curry goat, beef and callaloo, and Devon House I-Scream is known for rum and raisin, stout, coconut and guava flavours.

food_culture.name: Fish tea, festival and bammy
food_culture.description: The Jamaica Tourist Board names Gloria's Seafood City in Kingston for fish tea, curried shrimp, and festival with bammy: a thin fish broth, sweet fried cornmeal dumpling and flat cassava bread.

food_culture.name: Reggae in Kingston
food_culture.description: Kingston is where reggae was made: the Bob Marley Museum is the singer's home and recording studio, and Trench Town Culture Yard is called the cradle of reggae by the Jamaica Tourist Board. The Kingston Creative Art Walk on Water Lane is held on the last Sunday of each month.

food_culture.name: Maroon heritage
food_culture.description: The Moore Town Maroons in Portland are one of Jamaica's Maroon communities, descendants of people who escaped slavery and built independent mountain settlements. The Jamaica Tourist Board lists a visit with Moore Town Maroons and Nanny Falls; arrange it through a local guide.

title: Panama City, the Canal + Portobelo, Panama
best_time_description: December to April is the dry season (Tourism Panama calls it the best time for beaches and activities on the Caribbean coast at Portobelo); the rest of the year is the green, rainy season, when rainforest walks are lush but showers are likely. Miraflores is open daily year-round. Expect very large crowds in Portobelo around 21 October, the Black Christ day.
description: Panama's capital and its canal in five days: the colonial lanes of Casco Antiguo, ships rising through the Miraflores Locks, rainforest birding at Gamboa and Soberania National Park, the Spanish forts of Portobelo on the Caribbean coast, and the ruins of the original Panama Viejo.

days.title: Arrive Panama City + Casco Antiguo
activities: Arrive at Tocumen International Airport; Tourism Panama says the airport has a direct Metro station connection to the city centre, and the MiBus card (sold at the airport) works on both buses and the Metro; white SET tourism taxis are also at the airport

Walk Casco Antiguo (the San Felipe quarter, a UNESCO World Heritage district) in the order Tourism Panama suggests: Plaza Santa Ana, Plaza Herrera (Museo de la Mola), Plaza de Francia, Paseo Esteban Huertas on the old city wall, the Teatro Nacional, then Plaza de la Independencia with the Cathedral Basilica Santa Maria la Antigua and the Interoceanic Canal Museum
Sunset drinks at a Casco Antiguo rooftop bar; the district is compact and best explored on foot, with scarce parking
Before you go, read the notice Tourism Panama links from its Casco Antiguo page about the 9 October 2026 earthquake for any limits on access to heritage buildings
days.lodging_suggestion: Casco Antiguo or near Cinta Costera

days.title: Miraflores Locks + Metropolitan Natural Park
activities: Go to the Miraflores Visitor Center (about a 15-minute drive from downtown, per Tourism Panama), open daily 8:00 am to 6:00 pm, with the ticket office closing at 5:00 pm; non-resident adult admission is B/.17.22, ages 6 to 12 B/.7.22, under 6 free (Panama Canal Authority visitor site, check for changes); tickets can be bought online

Allow about 1.5 hours: viewing decks over the locks plus the 3D Panama Canal film at the IMAX theatre (about 45 minutes; screenings at 8:45, 9:45, 11:00, 12:15, 1:30, 2:45, 4:00 and 5:15). Ship transit times vary, so check the transit schedule on the visitor site before choosing your slot

Afternoon in Parque Natural Metropolitano, a 230-hectare tropical forest inside the city, open daily 7:00 am to 4:30 pm with a small entrance fee (non-nationals about US$5 as of October 2025, paid at the Visitor Center); the easy Los Momotides trail needs no guide, and the moderate Mono Titi trail climbs to a Cerro Cedro viewpoint over the city and the canal

days.title: Gamboa + Soberania National Park
activities: Drive or take a taxi to Soberania National Park, which Tourism Panama says is about 30 minutes from the city (Avenida Omar Torrijos toward Gamboa); local buses from Albrook terminal to Chilibre also stop at the park's administrative centre

Start early on Pipeline Road, the park's best-known birding track (Tourism Panama says it holds the record for most bird species seen in 24 hours, 357), and climb the 32 m observation tower at the Panama Rainforest Discovery Center (run by the Avifauna foundation; confirm hours and fees at avifauna.org.pa)

Optional afternoon on Gatun Lake: tours from Gamboa and the Causeway offer a partial canal crossing, sailing or fishing around the lake's islands with chances to see monkeys and birds. Book these in advance
If you prefer a hike on history, parts of the 1527 Camino de Cruces (Cruces Trail) are walkable, and El Charco trail has natural pools

days.title: Portobelo and the Caribbean forts
activities: Drive about 1.5 hours from Panama City on the Panama-Colon highway (turnoff at Sabanitas; the toll must be paid in cash), or go by bus from Albrook to the Colon terminal and then a taxi or bus to Portobelo; the whole trip by bus takes 2.5 to 3 hours, per Tourism Panama

See the Spanish colonial forts of Portobelo, part of the UNESCO-listed Fortifications on the Caribbean Side of Panama, with ruins and old cannons, and the Church of San Felipe, which houses the Black Christ (Nazareno of Portobelo)
Optional snorkelling or diving on the reefs of Portobelo National Park through a local operator

Bring cash: Tourism Panama says many local restaurants and boat services do not take cards. Seasonal notes: the Black Christ day is 21 October and draws very large crowds on the Sabanitas to Portobelo road; the Congo Mass is held at San Felipe on the last Sunday of each month; Diablos and Congos celebrations take place on Saturdays from late January until Ash Wednesday

days.title: Panama Viejo + departure
activities: Visit Panama Viejo, the ruins of the first permanent European settlement on the Pacific (settled 1519, UNESCO World Heritage), about a 10-minute drive or 30-minute bus ride from the centre; climb the bell tower for views of the skyline and see the old cathedral ruins and the artisan market
Head to Tocumen airport for your onward flight; allow generous time and check opening hours and ticket prices at Panama Viejo before you go, as the official tourism page does not state them

food_culture.name: Sancocho de gallina
food_culture.description: Panama's national comfort soup: chicken stewed with ordinary (yam-like) root vegetables, corn and culantro, found in family restaurants throughout the capital.

food_culture.name: Patacones and ceviche
food_culture.description: Twice-fried green plantain discs eaten as a side or snack; Panamanian ceviche is usually made with corvina (sea bass) cured in lime and is widely served in Panama City.

food_culture.name: Afro-Caribbean cooking on the Colon coast
food_culture.description: Portobelo's restaurants serve Afro-Caribbean dishes built on coconut, fresh fish and plantain, according to Tourism Panama, alongside some international menus; bring cash.

food_culture.name: Panamanian coffee
food_culture.description: Panama is known for its highland coffees, including the Geisha variety that Tourism Panama calls one of the most sought-after in the world; cafes in Casco Antiguo are a good place to try a cup.

food_culture.name: Diablos y Congos of Portobelo
food_culture.description: Afro-colonial carnival tradition on the Caribbean coast, with devils and Congo characters in satirical street theatre, held on Saturdays from late January until Ash Wednesday, with the main festivals every two years.

food_culture.name: The Black Christ of Portobelo
food_culture.description: A dark wooden image of Jesus Nazarene kept in the Church of San Felipe; pilgrims travel to Portobelo for its feast day on 21 October, many walking the road from Sabanitas.

title: Boquete Highlands + Bocas del Toro, Panama
best_time_description: January to March suits both halves: it falls in the dry season (December to April) for the Chiriqui highlands, and February and March are usually the least rainy months in Bocas del Toro, which has some rain nearly all year (the Ministry of Agricultural Development's climate bulletin puts the first minimum of Caribbean-side rainfall in February or March; a second drier spell around September and October is reported by travel guides). Boquete is cool, 12 to 30 C according to Tourism Panama. Boquete's flower and coffee fair is held each January (7 to 18 January in 2026; check the dates for the year you travel).
description: From the cool coffee highlands of Chiriqui to the Caribbean archipelago of Bocas del Toro: a short hop by plane to David, Boquete's coffee farms and Volcan Baru National Park, a road and boat crossing over the mountains to Isla Colon, then island days of marine park snorkelling, Afro-Caribbean culture and beaches, with a 45-minute flight back to Panama City.

days.title: Arrive Panama City
activities: Arrive at Tocumen International Airport and transfer into the city by Metro (Tourism Panama says a Metro station connects directly to the airport), taxi or ride-hailing app
Easy evening in Casco Antiguo or along the Cinta Costera; keep the day light because tomorrow starts with a domestic flight from a different airport, Marcos A. Gelabert (Albrook)

Safety note for planning: a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck central Panama on 9 October 2026 and national press reported damaged roads and bridges in Veraguas, Los Santos, Herrera and Coclé; the Pan-American Highway runs through that area, so choose flights for the long legs and check current road advisories before travelling overland

days.title: Fly to David, then up to Boquete
activities: Fly Albrook (Marcos A. Gelabert) to David; Tourism Panama says domestic flights from Albrook and Tocumen reach David in under an hour, and flights from Tocumen are also available. Book early and confirm the flight with the airline, as schedules change

From David it is about 50 minutes by taxi or rental car to Boquete (rental cars are available at Enrique Malek airport in David). The bus alternative from Albrook's Gran Terminal takes about 6 hours to David, then another bus or car to Boquete, per Tourism Panama; skip it right after the earthquake unless roads are confirmed open
Settle in and walk Bajo Boquete; evenings are cool

days.title: Coffee farms + Jaramillo
activities: Take a plantation tour at a Boquete coffee farm; Tourism Panama highlights coffee tours including the Geisha variety. Reserve ahead and ask the farm about the harvest and processing season, as the tourism board does not publish dates
Lunch in Jaramillo, which Tourism Panama describes as a farm-to-table dining area, and try one of the local breweries
Option for a more active afternoon: whitewater rafting on the Chiriqui Viejo River, which has rapids of all levels, through a local operator

days.title: Volcan Baru National Park
activities: Hike in Volcan Baru National Park (summit 3,474 m, the highest point in Panama) with a certified guide or tour operator, as Tourism Panama recommends. The Los Quetzales trail is a birdwatchers' favourite for the resplendent quetzal

The Boquete route to the summit can take as little as 6 hours depending on fitness, and tours often drive part of the way in a modified 4x4; the Los Llanos route from Volcan is harder and can take up to 8 hours. On a clear day the summit offers views of both the Atlantic and Pacific. Carry warm clothing, a flashlight, water and snacks, as clouds are common. A short Los Quetzales walk is the easier choice if you do not want to summit
Rest evening in Boquete

days.title: Over the mountains to Bocas del Toro
activities: Travel from Bajo Boquete to Puerto Almirante, about 3.5 hours by car per Tourism Panama (public transport goes through David and then a bus to Almirante; allow extra time). Check that your route is open before leaving
Take the water taxi from Puerto Almirante to Isla Colon, about 35 minutes (Tourism Panama); no schedule is published by the tourism board, so ask your hotel in Bocas Town how to book it
Evening in Bocas Town, the main base, with the widest choice of hotels, tours, restaurants, ATMs and nightlife; Isla Colon has the only paved roads in the archipelago

days.title: Bastimentos National Marine Park + Old Bank
activities: Take a boat tour from Bocas Town (water taxis and tours link the islands, and many can pick up from the hotel pier) to Bastimentos National Marine Park, Panama's first marine park, for snorkelling over the coral; the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute has a station in the archipelago
Visit Old Bank, an Afro-Caribbean community on Bastimentos, where calypso, reggae and guari-guari (a local Creole language mixing English, French and Spanish) are part of everyday culture
Water temperature is about 26 C all year, per Tourism Panama

days.title: Isla Carenero + free day
activities: Walk around Isla Carenero, which takes about an hour, past beaches, bars, hotels and surf breaks; surf spots in the area suit all levels, and Bastimentos has wilder waves for experts (Tourism Panama)

Alternatively spend the day on the mainland side with a certified guide: La Amistad International Park (PILA), the Palo Seco protected forest, or a village stay with the Naso Tjer Di indigenous community
Last dinner in Bocas Town; try Afro-Caribbean coconut-based dishes

days.title: Fly Bocas to Panama City
activities: Fly Isla Colon (Captain Jose Ezequiel Hall International Airport) to Albrook (Marcos A. Gelabert), about 45 minutes per Tourism Panama; Bocas flights have been rescheduled at times for weather or technical reasons, so keep a buffer before any international departure
International flights leave from Tocumen, a different airport from Albrook, so allow time and a taxi transfer between them; do not book a same-day onward connection tightly

food_culture.name: Geisha coffee from the Chiriqui highlands
food_culture.description: Boquete's cool, high farms produce some of Panama's best-known coffee; Tourism Panama calls the Geisha variety one of the most sought-after in the world and lists plantation tours as a main Boquete activity.

food_culture.name: Rondon and coconut-based Caribbean cooking
food_culture.description: Bocas del Toro has an Afro-Caribbean food culture, with coconut, fish and plantain at its core; rondon is the best-known coconut stew of the Caribbean coast, usually cooked with fish and root vegetables.

food_culture.name: Farm-to-table dining in Jaramillo
food_culture.description: Tourism Panama describes the Jaramillo area outside Boquete as a farm-to-table dining spot, using the highlands' produce.

food_culture.name: Feria de las Flores y del Cafe
food_culture.description: Boquete's flower and coffee fair is held each January (7 to 18 January in 2026).

food_culture.name: Guari-guari and Afro-Antillean heritage
food_culture.description: Bocas del Toro's culture, per Tourism Panama, includes calypso and reggae, Afro-Caribbean cuisine and guari-guari, a local language mixing English, French and Spanish.

food_culture.name: Naso Tjer Di indigenous community
food_culture.description: On the mainland side of Bocas del Toro, visitors can stay in the villages of the Naso Tjer Di, one of Panama's indigenous peoples, as Tourism Panama notes.

title: La Paz, Lake Titicaca + Sucre, Bolivia
best_time_description: The dry season, roughly May to October, is the sensible window: the UK and Canadian advisories describe November to March as the rainy season, with landslides and flooded or impassable roads, and road blockades (state of emergency declared 20 June 2026, expected to run to about 17 December 2026) can disrupt buses and flights at any time of year. Nights at La Paz and on the lake are cold in the dry months, so pack layers.
description: Bolivia's classic first-timer arc: start in La Paz at about 3,640 m, take in the ruins at Tiwanaku, spend two nights on the shore of Lake Titicaca at Copacabana with a day on the Isla del Sol, then drop to the lower, warmer colonial city of Sucre. Altitude is the main planning issue, so the route keeps the first days easy and finishes lower.

days.title: Arrive La Paz (3,640 m)
activities: Arrive at El Alto airport and take a registered or radio taxi into the city; the UK FCDO warns of fake taxis and fake police at the La Paz bus terminal and El Alto airport and of 'express kidnapping', so do not get into an unmarked car or a taxi that already has other passengers.

Altitude: Global Affairs Canada puts La Paz at 3,640 m and warns high-altitude illness can be fatal. Do nothing strenuous today, drink water, and skip alcohol; if symptoms worsen, descend and seek care.
Short, flat evening walk near your hotel; keep bags in sight and use a money belt, since petty theft is common in central La Paz.

days.title: La Paz by cable car
activities: Ride Mi Teleférico, the cable-car network linking La Paz and El Alto (its lines are named Línea Roja, Amarilla and Azul on its site); check the operator's site for current line hours before you plan the day.
Wander the central streets and markets on foot at an easy pace, with breaks; stick to busy streets and watch bags in crowds.
Early night to help with acclimatization.

days.title: Tiwanaku ruins
activities: Half-day excursion to Tiwanaku: Crillon Tours' half-day tour (SKU LPB-T6) states it 'takes five hours' and visits the Puerta del Sol, the Kalasasaya temple and the Akapana pyramid; entrance fees are included in that tour. Independent visitors should confirm opening days and any ticket requirements before going.
Afternoon free in La Paz; take it slowly.

days.title: La Paz to Copacabana
activities: Take a tourist-oriented bus to Copacabana: the trip is about 3 hours by road (a route-planner estimate; confirm with the bus company), and the FCDO says tourist-oriented companies tend to be safer than the cheapest buses. Check the Bolivian roads authority (ABC) status map first, because blockades can stop buses without warning and a ticket marked 'condicionado' means the company does not guarantee arrival.

Walk Copacabana's lakefront and the town, and pick a boat operator for tomorrow. FCDO and Global Affairs Canada both warn that Lake Titicaca boats are often basic: make sure life jackets are provided and avoid anything that looks overloaded.
Lake level is higher than La Paz (about 3,800 m), so cold nights are normal.

days.title: Isla del Sol
activities: Boat from Copacabana to the Isla del Sol and a day walking on the island. Ask the operator at the dock for the current crossing time and return departure; the island communities collect their own entry fees, so carry small cash. Operators' times and prices were not verified for this itinerary.
Return to Copacabana by boat the same day, or sleep on the island if you have a warm sleeping layer; either way, confirm the last boat back.
Sunset on the Copacabana shore.

days.title: Copacabana back to La Paz
activities: Morning bus back to La Paz, about 3 hours (a route-planner estimate; confirm with the company), arriving by mid-afternoon at the latest to leave margin before the next day's flight.
Evening: dinner of salteñas or a plato paceño somewhere busy and central.

days.title: Fly to Sucre
activities: Fly from La Paz (El Alto) to Sucre (Alcantarí airport). A route-planner lists Boliviana de Aviación, with a connecting itinerary taking about 2 hours 15 minutes via Cochabamba; check the airline's live schedule on boa.bo, since direct and connecting options vary by day. Flying avoids the overnight bus, which a route-planner lists at roughly 9.5 to 13 hours.
Sucre is much lower than La Paz and Potosí; it is above 2,300 m but, per the CDC, outside the yellow-fever area. Expect easier breathing and a milder climate.
Afternoon walk around Plaza 25 de Mayo.

days.title: Sucre's historic centre
activities: Casa de la Libertad on Plaza 25 de Mayo, where Bolivia's independence was signed: open Monday to Friday 8:30 to 16:30 and Saturday and Sunday 9:00 to 13:00, last entry one hour before closing, guided tours every hour, closed on public holidays; the museum's own site lists Bs. 50 for foreigners (confirm at the door).
Walk the whitewashed colonial streets, markets and plazas of the historic centre.
Departure: fly out of Sucre, or continue to Potosí (about 3 hours by bus per a route-planner) to join the second Bolivia itinerary.

food_culture.name: Salteñas
food_culture.description: Baked, juicy pastries filled with meat or chicken in a slightly sweet, spiced gravy, traditionally eaten as a mid-morning snack in Bolivian cities including La Paz and Sucre; eat them carefully, since the filling is liquid.

food_culture.name: Trucha (Lake Titicaca trout)
food_culture.description: Trout served grilled or fried along the Copacabana waterfront, a staple of the lakeside menus.

food_culture.name: Plato paceño
food_culture.description: A La Paz plate of boiled corn, potatoes, fava beans and fried cheese, often with a meat portion; it is a classic of the city's traditional restaurants.

food_culture.name: Mate de coca
food_culture.description: Tea made from coca leaves, widely drunk at altitude in Bolivia as a traditional remedy; it is a local custom, not a cure for altitude illness, and coca-based products may not be allowed through some countries' customs on departure.

food_culture.name: Api morado
food_culture.description: A hot, spiced purple-corn drink usually served with a fried pastry at morning stalls and cafes in the highlands, welcome on cold altiplano mornings.

food_culture.name: Ch'alla to the Pachamama
food_culture.description: An Andean offering to Mother Earth in which a little drink is poured on the ground before drinking, practised in Aymara and Quechua communities and visible in Bolivian celebrations.

food_culture.name: Aymara and Quechua highland culture
food_culture.description: Lake Titicaca and the altiplano are the homeland of the Aymara, and Sucre sits in Quechua-speaking country; Tiwanaku, the pre-Inca site near La Paz, is the region's best-known archaeological place.

food_culture.name: Bolivia's colonial capital
food_culture.description: Sucre's Casa de la Libertad is where Bolivia's declaration of independence was signed, and the city remains the constitutional capital while La Paz is the seat of government.

title: Uyuni Salt Flat, Potosí + Tupiza, Bolivia
best_time_description: Dry season, about May to October, is the safest window: Tupiza Tours says Isla Incahuasi cannot be visited in January to March on its three-day route (January to April on its four-day route) and the route may change with a night in Colchani, and the FCDO and Global Affairs Canada describe November to March as the rainy season, with landslides and roads impassable for days and the salt flat becoming dangerous. A thin layer of water on the salt flat in the wet months is what produces the famous mirror reflections (Tupiza Tours sells a separate 'stars and reflections' add-on), so the mirror effect and the safest roads are in direct tension: only go in the wet season with a reputable operator who confirms the route daily. Nights are very cold at 4,000 m and above in the dry months.
description: A high-altitude road trip through southern Bolivia: the silver-mining city of Potosí, the Uyuni salt flat, and the red-rock country around Tupiza, linked by a multi-day 4x4 crossing. The five-day version is Potosí, Uyuni and the three-day 4x4 loop; the seven-day version adds the bus south to Tupiza and its canyons.

days.title: Potosí (4,090 m)
activities: Arrive in Potosí; Sucre to Potosí buses take about 3 hours (a route-planner estimate; confirm with the bus company), so many travellers come from Sucre. Global Affairs Canada puts Potosí at 4,090 m, higher than La Paz: take it easy, drink water, and avoid alcohol on arrival.
Visit the Casa Nacional de Moneda, the old colonial mint; its own site lists phone (+591) 62-25406 and WhatsApp +591 71005518 for visiting hours and guided-visit rules, so check there before you go.
Walk the colonial centre at an easy pace and get an early night.

days.title: Potosí's Cerro Rico, then bus to Uyuni
activities: Mine tours are optional: Global Affairs Canada lists 'Potosi mine tours' among adventure activities to book only through well-established operators. The mines are at altitude and are working mines; skip them if you have heart or lung problems or are not acclimatized.
Afternoon bus Potosí to Uyuni, about 4 hours per a route-planner (confirm with the company; roads can be blocked, and a 'condicionado' ticket is not guaranteed).

Arrive in Uyuni (3,665 m per the operator, 3,656 m per Global Affairs Canada) and book or confirm the tour for tomorrow with a reputable operator: there are no official minimum standards for salt-flat tour companies (FCDO).

days.title: Uyuni to Polques hot springs (day 1 of the 4x4 loop)
activities: Start the three-day Uyuni loop with a reputable operator. Tupiza Tours' version (a 4x4 crossing of about 700 km, starting and ending in Uyuni) leaves at 8:30 am and visits the train cemetery, the mining town of San Cristobal, the Canon de la Anaconda and nearby lagoons, then the Salar de Chalviri and the open-air Polques hot springs (about 35 degrees C, altitude 4,000 m). Other operators run similar loops; confirm the route, vehicle, oxygen and the lodging standard before paying.

Overnight in basic shared lodging (rooms of 4 to 6 beds, shared bathrooms) at around 4,000 m. It is very cold in the dry months, so bring a warm sleeping layer. Attraction entrance tickets are not included in that operator's price.

If your 4x4 operator offers the four-day Uyuni to Tupiza route instead (Tupiza Tours' four-day route, about 1,000 km, 2,850 m to 5,000 m, can run in either direction), take it and skip days 6 and 7's bus leg; its day-by-day was published only for the Tupiza to Uyuni direction, so confirm the order and arrival time.

days.title: Laguna Colorada, geysers and the Siloli desert
activities: Desierto de Dali (4,750 m), the Laguna Verde and Laguna Blanca viewpoint below the Licancabur volcano, the Sol de Manana geysers (about 5,000 m) and Laguna Colorada with its flamingos.
Desierto de Siloli (4,500 m) with the Arbol de Piedra, then the Ruta de las Joyas lagoons (Honda, Chiarkhota, Hedionda and Canapa) and the Ollague volcano viewpoint.

Sunset on the salt flat, then a night in a salt-built hostel (Tupiza Tours lists Atullcha, 3,650 m). Rainy-season note from that operator: January to March the route may change and the group may sleep in Colchani instead.

days.title: Salar de Uyuni at sunrise, Isla Incahuasi, back to Uyuni
activities: Leave about 5:30 am for sunrise on the Gran Salar de Uyuni, then Isla Incahuasi's petrified-reef trail among giant cacti. Tupiza Tours says the island cannot be visited from January to March on its three-day route and January to April on its four-day route; on its Uyuni day tour the Incahuasi entry (about US$4.5) is a separate payment.

Photo stops on the open flat, Playa Blanca (the first salt hotel), the Ojos de Sal salt works and the Colchani artisan market; the operator's three-day loop arrives back in Uyuni around 1:00 pm. A 5-day trip can end here, with a flight or bus out of Uyuni.

Mirror effect: when the flat is covered with a shallow sheet of water in the rainy season it reflects the sky, and Tupiza Tours sells a separate stars-and-reflections tour. The same wet season brings landslides and impassable roads (UK FCDO, Global Affairs Canada) and Canada calls the flat dangerous to visit then, so only go with an operator who confirms the route each day.

days.title: Uyuni to Tupiza
activities: Travel to Tupiza (2,850 m, the red-rock town in Potosi department). A route-planner estimates the Uyuni to Tupiza bus at about 4 hours with two daily departures, but it was not confirmed with an operator and the road can be slow; ask at the Uyuni bus offices and allow a full day.
Altitude drops here, so sleep is easier. Settle in and walk the town in the late afternoon.

days.title: Tupiza canyons
activities: Tupiza Tours' Tupiza half-day tour lasts about 3 hours with departures at 9:00 or 14:30 and returns around 12:00 or 17:30, visiting the Puerta del Diablo, Valle de los Machos and Canon del Inca; altitude 2,800 m to 3,100 m.

Or the full-day Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid tour (about 10.5 hours, 7:30 start, about 220 km, 2,850 m to 4,100 m), which stops at Huaca Huanusca, where the page says the outlaws made their final robbery on 4 November 1908, and San Vicente, the shootout house and cemetery.
Onward: Tupiza is near the Argentine border at Villazon; check current crossing arrangements and your passport stamps with the border authorities.

food_culture.name: Llama steak and quinoa
food_culture.description: Llama meat and quinoa are staples of the southern altiplano around Uyuni, where quinoa is one of the main crops, and are on the menus of the town's restaurants.

food_culture.name: Salteñas potosinas
food_culture.description: A baked, juicy meat pastry eaten across Bolivia, with Potosí and Sucre claiming their own versions, usually a mid-morning bite.

food_culture.name: Quinoa soup
food_culture.description: A thick Andean soup of quinoa, potatoes and vegetables that is warming food at altitude and common in the Uyuni and Potosí areas.

food_culture.name: Mate de coca
food_culture.description: Coca-leaf tea, the traditional drink at altitude in Bolivia, widely offered at hotels; a custom, not a cure for altitude illness.

food_culture.name: Singani
food_culture.description: Bolivia's grape brandy, produced in the valleys of southern Bolivia around Tarija and used in the national cocktail, the chuflay.

food_culture.name: Offerings in the Potosí mines
food_culture.description: Miners in Potosí make offerings to El Tío, the underground spirit, and to the Pachamama, a living tradition of the working mines on Cerro Rico.

food_culture.name: Potosí's silver history
food_culture.description: Potosí's Cerro Rico was a major source of colonial-era silver, and the Casa Nacional de Moneda records its minting history.

food_culture.name: Tupiza and the Wild West legend
food_culture.description: The Tupiza area is tied to the story of Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, who met their end in a shootout in San Vicente in 1908 according to local operators.

title: Windhoek, Sossusvlei + Swakopmund, Namibia
best_time_description: Aim for May to October. The UK Foreign Office says the rainy season runs January to April, when gravel roads deteriorate, so the long gravel legs to Sesriem and the coast are easier outside those months. Coastal Swakopmund and Walvis Bay sit in the Namib fog zone (UNESCO calls the Namib Sand Sea a coastal fog desert), so bring a layer for the coast.
description: Namibia's southern classic as a self-drive loop: Windhoek, the Namib-Naukluft Park at Sesriem and Sossusvlei (inside the UNESCO-listed Namib Sand Sea), then the coast at Swakopmund and Walvis Bay, with the Cape Cross Seal Reserve to the north, and back to Windhoek. Distances come from Namibia Wildlife Resorts and the Erongo Regional Council; most roads outside the main corridors are gravel, so the route is planned around daylight driving.

days.title: Arrive Windhoek
activities: Land at Hosea Kutako International Airport; since 1 April 2025 UK, US, Canadian, Australian and German passport holders need an e-visa applied for online or a visa on arrival here (see the visa check for your passport) and the passport must have six months' validity and three blank pages
Collect the rental car and ask the company which gravel roads the contract covers; the UK Foreign Office warns that many policies do not cover single-vehicle accidents on gravel
Stock up on water and food in the capital before the remote legs; the German Foreign Office advises against long intercity drives after dark
Keep doors locked and valuables out of sight at busy Windhoek intersections (UK Foreign Office advice)

days.title: Windhoek to Sesriem
activities: Drive to Sesriem, 334 km from Windhoek according to Namibia Wildlife Resorts (NWR); no official drive time was found, so leave early and plan to arrive well before dark

Expect gravel on the approach roads: the German Foreign Office says only the main roads are paved, recommends two spare tyres and warns of punctures; keep to 80 km/h or below on gravel (UK Foreign Office)
Fill the tank before leaving the last large town; Sesriem has a filling station and shop per NWR
Book Sesriem Campsite or Sossus Dune Lodge in advance through NWR (online booking was unavailable on 19 October 2026; requests go to reservations@nwr.com.na)
Optional sunset drive to Elim Dune, run from Sesriem by NWR
days.lodging_suggestion: Sesriem Campsite or Sossus Dune Lodge, Namib-Naukluft Park

days.title: Sossusvlei, Dead Pan + Sesriem Canyon
activities: Drive the 60 km from Sesriem to Sossusvlei (NWR) for the star-shaped dunes, which NWR says rise to about 325 m from their base
Walk to Dead Pan, the white clay pan with camelthorn skeletons carbon-dated at 500 to 600 years; NWR runs a 2x4 shuttle to Deadvlei, bookable from Sesriem, for vehicles without 4x4
Guests of Sossus Dune Lodge, inside the park, can reach Sossusvlei before sunrise and stay until after sunset (NWR); other visitors should check the gate times at Sesriem
Walk Sesriem Canyon, a gorge about 1 km long and 30 to 40 m deep

Park fees (Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism notice of 15 January 2026, published by Namibia Wildlife Resorts): from 1 April 2026 foreign adults pay N$280 (N$140 entrance + N$140 conservation), foreign children above 8 and below 16 pay N$180, children aged 8 and under are free, and a vehicle with up to 10 seats pays N$60. The notice does not say how long one payment covers, so confirm at the gate; the same table covers the Namib-Naukluft Park except Sandwich Harbour
days.lodging_suggestion: Sesriem Campsite or Sossus Dune Lodge, Namib-Naukluft Park

days.title: Sesriem towards the coast through the Namib-Naukluft Park
activities: Drive north-west to Swakopmund through the Namib-Naukluft Park; NWR names the Kuiseb Canyon and the Welwitschia Trail as features of the park along this side
No official distance or drive time for this leg was found: treat it as a full day, set off at first light and reach Swakopmund before dark
Optional detour: Naukluft Camp is 100 km from Sossusvlei and 253 km from Windhoek (NWR) if you want a night in the Naukluft mountains instead
Keep two spare tyres and plenty of water; gravel sections here are the likeliest place for punctures

days.title: Swakopmund and the Dune Belt
activities: Walk Swakopmund's seafront and jetty; check the town's museums and shops for current opening hours
Visit the Dune Belt between Swakopmund and Walvis Bay, part of Dorob National Park (Erongo Regional Council); desert adventure activities such as quad biking run here, booked through local operators

Drive out to the Moon Landscape east of town, which the Erongo Regional Council lists among the area's main attractions and which crosses into the Namib-Naukluft Park, so park fees can apply (see the fee note on day 3)

days.title: Walvis Bay lagoon and Sandwich Harbour
activities: Drive 40 km south from Swakopmund to Walvis Bay (Erongo Regional Council)
Visit Walvis Bay Lagoon, a Ramsar wetland that the municipality says holds flamingos, pelicans and migratory birds
Take a marine boat tour from Walvis Bay; the Erongo Regional Council lists Benguela dolphins, seals, pelicans and sunfish, with the occasional Southern Right whale

Sandwich Harbour lies about 30 km further south (Erongo Regional Council) in the Namib-Naukluft Park and is normally visited with an operator on a 4x4 excursion; its fee is lower than the main parks: N$150 per foreign adult and N$50 per vehicle up to 10 seats from 1 April 2026 (MEFT notice)
Return to Swakopmund for the night

days.title: Cape Cross Seal Reserve
activities: Drive north through Henties Bay, which is 70 km from Swakopmund, to the Cape Cross Seal Reserve, home to thousands of Cape fur seals (Erongo Regional Council)
