Cape Cross is in the same park-fee table as Etosha and the Namib-Naukluft Park: N$280 per foreign adult and N$60 per vehicle up to 10 seats from 1 April 2026 (MEFT notice); keep a safe distance from the seals
Return to Swakopmund for a last coastal dinner

days.title: Swakopmund to Windhoek
activities: Drive back to Windhoek on the main road inland; no official distance or drive time was found, so allow most of a day and keep the Hosea Kutako airport check-in time in mind
The German Foreign Office warns that intercity accident risk is often underestimated because of wildlife, fatigue and distraction, and that help in remote areas can take hours
After a crash, contact the rental company and the MVA Fund at 9682 (German Foreign Office)
Return the car and fly home, or add the northern Etosha itinerary

food_culture.name: Kapana and braai
food_culture.description: Namibia's street grill: strips of beef cooked over coals and sold hot from roadside stalls, the everyday version of the national habit of cooking meat over an open fire (braai). Stalls are most common in Windhoek's northern townships; go with a local guide or a trusted tour.

food_culture.name: Game meat and biltong
food_culture.description: Oryx (gemsbok), kudu and springbok appear on restaurant menus across the country, and air-dried meat (biltong) is the standard road-trip snack to buy in town before the long gravel legs.

food_culture.name: Coastal oysters and seafood
food_culture.description: Walvis Bay is a working fishing and port town (Erongo Regional Council); the cold Atlantic coast makes oysters and fish the signature order in Swakopmund and Walvis Bay, often after a lagoon or boat trip.

food_culture.name: Namibian lager
food_culture.description: A cold local lager at sunset after a Sossusvlei or dune day is the usual order across the country; ask for what the lodge or bar has on tap.

food_culture.name: German colonial heritage at the coast
food_culture.description: Swakopmund was a German colonial port, and its seafront architecture and cafe culture still show it. NWR describes Namutoni's fort, in the north, as a historic German fort of 1897; the colonial history is part of the country's story and is shown differently by different museums, so read the displays critically.

food_culture.name: Namib Sand Sea, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
food_culture.description: UNESCO calls the Namib Sand Sea the only coastal desert in the world with extensive fog-influenced dune fields, inscribed for its two dune systems, gravel plains and fog-fed wildlife; Sossusvlei lies inside it.

food_culture.name: The Topnaar of the Kuiseb
food_culture.description: The Erongo Regional Council describes the Topnaar people as living off what the Namib Desert offers along the Kuiseb River; they are a living community, not an attraction, so ask before photographing people and buy from community-run stalls where you can.

title: Etosha National Park + Damaraland, Namibia
best_time_description: May to October is the sensible window for a self-drive: the UK Foreign Office says gravel roads deteriorate in the January to April rainy season, and the 2026 Etosha gate schedule shows the longest days from September to January (gates closing as late as 19:39 in January) and the shortest in June (closing 18:25).
description: Namibia's wildlife north: drive from Windhoek to Etosha National Park's eastern gate at Namutoni, cross the park west through Halali, Okaukuejo and Dolomite, leave by Galton Gate for Damaraland and the UNESCO rock engravings of Twyfelfontein, then return south via Omaruru. Park fees and gate times come from the Namibia Wildlife Resorts website (Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism fee notice and the 2026 gate schedule).

days.title: Windhoek to Namutoni
activities: Collect the rental car and drive to Namutoni, 486 km from Windhoek according to Namibia Wildlife Resorts (NWR), passing Tsumeb, which is 110 km from Namutoni; no official drive time was found

Plan to be inside the park before the gate closes: NWR's 2026 schedule has gates closing between about 18:25 and 19:39 depending on the week, and the times change every Monday, so check the week of travel

Do not drive in the dark: the German Foreign Office advises avoiding long intercity drives after dark, and fuel is not guaranteed at NWR lodges, so fill up in Tsumeb and calculate the fuel needed for the whole park
Book NWR camps in advance (the booking system was unavailable on 19 October 2026; requests go to reservations@nwr.com.na)

days.title: Namutoni, Fisher's Pan and King Nehale waterhole
activities: Self-drive the eastern waterholes; NWR describes Namutoni as close to Fisher's Pan, a hotspot for birders
Visit the fort at Namutoni, a historic German fort built in 1897 that holds a museum (NWR)
Watch the flood-lit King Nehale waterhole from the fort in the evening (NWR)
NWR runs guided morning, afternoon and night drives from the resort if you prefer a guide

Park fees (Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism notice of 15 January 2026, published by Namibia Wildlife Resorts): from 1 April 2026 foreign adults pay N$280 (N$140 entrance + N$140 conservation), foreign children above 8 and below 16 pay N$180, children aged 8 and under are free, and a vehicle with up to 10 seats pays N$60. The notice does not say how long one payment covers, so confirm at the gate; park entrance covers Etosha

days.title: Namutoni to Halali
activities: Drive west across the park to Halali, which NWR places at the base of a dolomite hill among mopane trees and says is a draw for leopard, rhino and elephant; Halali is 451 km from Windhoek (NWR)
Stop at waterholes on the way; NWR notes popular waterholes sit close to Halali
Watch the floodlit waterhole at the resort after dinner
Be in camp before the gates close; NWR publishes the gate opening and closing times by week and says they change every Monday

days.title: Halali to Okaukuejo
activities: Continue west to Okaukuejo, which NWR says is famous for its flood-lit waterhole where lions, elephants and black rhino are common sightings; Okaukuejo is 432 km from Windhoek and 17 km from the park's southern entrance
Spend the evening at the flood-lit waterhole, where NWR says wildlife can be watched close up both day and night
Book a guided game drive through NWR if you want an expert spotter

days.title: Okaukuejo to Dolomite Camp
activities: Drive west into the less-visited western part of the park to Dolomite Camp, 570 km from Windhoek (NWR); NWR lists Olifantsrus campsite 50 km from Dolomite and 130 km from Okaukuejo
Bring all fuel and food you need for the day; fuel at NWR lodges is not guaranteed (German Foreign Office)
Olifantsrus, which NWR says opens at sunrise and closes at sunset, is a campsite with day-visitor picnic facilities until 16:00

days.title: Dolomite to Damaraland
activities: Leave Etosha by Galton Gate, 70 km from Olifantsrus (NWR), and drive south-west into Damaraland; no official distance or drive time for this leg was found, so plan a full day and arrive before dark
Expect gravel: the German Foreign Office says only the main roads are paved, and advises two spare tyres
Smartraveller notes ATMs are not always available in remote areas, so carry cash and fill the tank where you can

days.title: Twyfelfontein rock engravings
activities: Visit Twyfelfontein or /Ui-//aes, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with one of Africa's largest concentrations of petroglyphs, mostly of rhinoceros, elephant, ostrich and giraffe, plus painted rock shelters; UNESCO notes the engravings are the work of San hunter-gatherers over at least 2,000 years
Check at the site entrance for guide and entry arrangements; no fee or opening times were confirmed from an official page
Optional: the Brandberg, Namibia's highest mountain (Konigstein, 2,606 m), is known for its rock paintings including the 'White Lady' (Erongo Regional Council)

days.title: Damaraland to Omaruru
activities: Drive south to the Omaruru district, where the Erongo Regional Council lists private game reserves and guest farms; the 79,000 ha Erindi Game Reserve lies on the region's eastern edge
Allow a full day on mixed gravel and tar; keep to 80 km/h or below on gravel and avoid driving after dark (UK Foreign Office)

days.title: Omaruru to Windhoek
activities: Drive to Windhoek and return the car; no official distance or drive time was found, so leave margin before an international flight at Hosea Kutako International Airport
After a crash, contact the rental company and the MVA Fund at 9682 (German Foreign Office)

food_culture.name: Potjiekos and braai at the camp
food_culture.description: Etosha's camps have restaurants, but many visitors cook in the open: the Halali and Okaukuejo camps list braai (barbecue) facilities at their bush chalets (NWR), and the potjie, a stew cooked in a three-legged cast-iron pot over coals, is the traditional camp-fire dish.

food_culture.name: Game meat
food_culture.description: Kudu, oryx and springbok are common on lodge menus in the north; ask for the local game cut rather than a generic steak.

food_culture.name: Sundowners at a waterhole
food_culture.description: The floodlit waterholes at Okaukuejo, Halali and Namutoni are the evening focus in the park; a cold drink on the benches at dusk while animals come to drink is the camp ritual.

food_culture.name: Camp-hours discipline
food_culture.description: Etosha runs on daylight: NWR publishes gate opening and closing times by week (they change every Monday), and Olifantsrus camp opens at sunrise and closes at sunset, so the day is planned around being inside a camp before the gates close.

food_culture.name: Twyfelfontein or /Ui-//aes rock art
food_culture.description: UNESCO inscribed Twyfelfontein for its rock engravings and paintings, a record of the ritual practices of San hunter-gatherers over at least two millennia; the site is protected, so keep to the paths and do not touch the engravings.

food_culture.name: Fort Namutoni, a German colonial fort
food_culture.description: NWR describes Namutoni Resort as built into an old German historic fort of 1897 with a museum; visit it for the colonial-era history, which is told from several sides across Namibia.

title: Maun, Okavango Delta, Moremi + Chobe, Botswana
best_time_description: May to August is the dry winter: the Okavango flood from Angola arrives in the Delta and peaks around June to July, so mokoro and boat trips are at their best and wildlife gathers on the river at Chobe, but mornings are cold and demand is highest, so book camps well ahead. September to October is hot and dry with game concentrated at shrinking water. November to April is the green season with rain, birds and lower prices; some roads in Moremi and Khwai flood (the Maun to Kasane road through Moremi was closed by flooding in March 2026), so use flights between parks.
description: Fly into Maun, spend nights deep in the Okavango Delta poling a mokoro and walking islands, move on to Moremi Game Reserve for game drives, then fly to Kasane for the Chobe River elephants.

days.title: Arrive Maun
activities: Land at Maun Airport (MUB), the gateway to the Okavango Delta; most international travellers connect through Johannesburg or Gaborone
Visit the Maun waterfront and a craft market, and confirm your camp's light-aircraft or road transfer time with the booking office
Check that your passport has at least 6 months validity and the pages Botswana asks for; Ebola health screening and a health declaration apply at the airport

days.title: Into the Delta
activities: Fly or transfer into a camp in the Okavango Delta; deep Delta and island camps are normally fly-in by light aircraft, with timings set by the camp
Afternoon mokoro excursion poled by a local guide through reed channels
Dinner and campfire at camp, listening for hippos

days.title: Mokoro and walking safari
activities: Dawn mokoro trip then a guided walking safari on a Delta island with a licensed guide
Look for lechwe, birds and elephants near the channels
Optional sunset mokoro; activities depend on water level

days.title: To Moremi Game Reserve
activities: Light-aircraft or road transfer from the Delta to a camp in or beside Moremi Game Reserve (e.g. Xakanaxa or Khwai area); confirm the route and timing with your camp

Park entry for Moremi and Chobe is set by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (DWNP): a per-person per-day entry fee for non-citizens plus a per-vehicle fee, paid in Botswana pula; confirm the current tariff and pay or book with DWNP or your operator before arrival.
Evening game drive

days.title: Moremi game drives
activities: Full day of morning and afternoon game drives; Moremi's mix of lagoon, woodland and floodplain is known for big cats and wild dogs
A mokoro or boat outing in the lagoons if water allows
Do not self-drive the Moremi to Khwai road in the wet season without checking DWNP: flooding closed this road in March 2026

days.title: Fly Maun to Kasane
activities: Transfer to Maun and take a scheduled flight to Kasane (Air Botswana lists Maun to Kasane; timetable aggregators show about 45 minutes to 1 hour, a few flights a week, so confirm days with the airline before fixing your dates)
Settle into Kasane and take a sunset river cruise on the Chobe River
days.drive_time: Maun to Kasane flight, about 45 min to 1 hr (Air Botswana; confirm days)

days.title: Chobe Riverfront
activities: Morning game drive in Chobe National Park along the riverfront, famous for large elephant herds in the dry season

Park entry for Moremi and Chobe is set by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (DWNP): a per-person per-day entry fee for non-citizens plus a per-vehicle fee, paid in Botswana pula; confirm the current tariff and pay or book with DWNP or your operator before arrival.
Afternoon boat safari on the Chobe River for elephants, hippo and birdlife

days.title: Depart Kasane
activities: Transfer to Kasane Airport (BBK); Air Botswana lists Kasane to Gaborone flights for onward international connections
Optional morning visit to a craft stall or riverbank walk in Kasane before departing

food_culture.name: Seswaa
food_culture.description: Botswana's celebration dish: beef (or goat) boiled until tender, then pounded and shredded, usually served with bogobe (sorghum porridge) or pap and a vegetable relish. Served at weddings and funerals and on request in Maun and Kasane restaurants.

food_culture.name: Bogobe and morogo
food_culture.description: Bogobe is a soft sorghum or maize porridge, the everyday staple of Botswana; morogo is the wild or cultivated leafy greens cooked alongside it. Look for it on lunch menus at local cafes in Maun.

food_culture.name: Phane (mopane worms)
food_culture.description: Dried or stewed mopane caterpillars, a seasonal protein snack sold at roadside markets and eaten across northern Botswana. Fried with onion and tomato, they taste nutty and salty.

food_culture.name: Chibuku and traditional sorghum beer
food_culture.description: Opaque, lightly sour sorghum beer sold in cartons (Chibuku, nicknamed shake-shake) and brewed at home as bojalwa jwa setso. Tasting it is a social rather than a tourist custom, so ask locally.

food_culture.name: Kgotla
food_culture.description: The kgotla is the traditional village meeting place where a chief and community discuss and settle matters in the open. Most villages have one; you may be able to visit with a local guide and should ask before entering.

food_culture.name: Mokoro dugout poling
food_culture.description: Mokoros are the shallow canoes that people of the Delta region have long used to move through channels, poled standing up by a guide called a poler; many are now fibreglass rather than carved wood. A poler-led mokoro trip is the traditional way to see the Delta's water level.

food_culture.name: Pula, the word for rain
food_culture.description: Pula means both rain and the national currency, and the national greeting for good fortune is the cry 'Pula!'. In a dry country, rain is blessing, which is why the green season from November to April is celebrated.

title: Kasane, Chobe + Victoria Falls Day Crossing, Botswana
best_time_description: May to October is the dry season, when elephants and other game come down to the Chobe River and water-based safaris are most rewarding; October is very hot. The volume of water at Victoria Falls changes through the year, so check current flow before the day crossing. November to April is the green season with rain, birds and fewer visitors; roads in the park can be wet.
description: A compact base at Kasane: river cruises and game drives in Chobe National Park, a day across the Kazungula border to see Victoria Falls, and a slow riverside day, linked by one international flight into Kasane.

days.title: Arrive Kasane
activities: Fly to Kasane Airport (BBK); Air Botswana lists a Kasane to Gaborone route, and travellers also arrive by road from Victoria Falls Airport or Livingstone
Check in at a Kasane lodge on the Chobe River
Sunset on the river front; Ebola health screening and a health declaration apply to arrivals

days.title: Chobe River + game drive
activities: Morning game drive in Chobe National Park along the riverfront

Park entry for Moremi and Chobe is set by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (DWNP): a per-person per-day entry fee for non-citizens plus a per-vehicle fee, paid in Botswana pula; confirm the current tariff and pay or book with DWNP or your operator before arrival.
Afternoon boat cruise on the Chobe River, the classic way to see elephants and hippo at close range

days.title: Victoria Falls day crossing
activities: Leave Kasane before 07:00 so that you cross the Kazungula border ahead of the morning tour queues; the border is generally open from 06:00 to 20:00 (operator guidance, confirm locally)
Road transfer to Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe, about 80 km: roughly 90 minutes each way including border formalities, per operator guidance; a day trip is about 6 to 8 hours door to door

Walk the Falls rim in Victoria Falls National Park (Zimbabwe), entry fee paid on site, then return to Kasane. You need a Zimbabwe visa if your passport requires one, and your Botswana visa or exemption must still allow you to re-enter Botswana. Zimbabwe entry rules depend on your passport; check with its embassy
Alternative: cross by the Kazungula Bridge to Zambia and visit the Falls from Livingstone, about 85 km and sometimes up to an hour slower because of truck traffic
days.drive_time: Kasane to Victoria Falls, about 80 km, ~90 min incl. border; allow 6-8 hours return

days.title: Chobe sunrise + river day
activities: Early start for a second Chobe National Park morning game drive
Leisure afternoon: craft shopping in Kasane or a sunset cruise
Dinner of seswaa or grilled river fish at a Kasane restaurant

days.title: Depart Kasane
activities: Transfer to Kasane Airport (BBK) for flights to Gaborone and onward
Optional last river-view breakfast before departure

food_culture.name: Seswaa
food_culture.description: Botswana's celebration dish: beef (or goat) boiled until tender, then pounded and shredded, usually served with bogobe (sorghum porridge) or pap and a vegetable relish. Served at weddings and funerals and on request in Maun and Kasane restaurants.

food_culture.name: Phane (mopane worms)
food_culture.description: Dried or stewed mopane caterpillars, a seasonal protein snack sold at roadside markets and eaten across northern Botswana. Fried with onion and tomato, they taste nutty and salty.

food_culture.name: Chibuku and traditional sorghum beer
food_culture.description: Opaque, lightly sour sorghum beer sold in cartons (Chibuku, nicknamed shake-shake) and brewed at home as bojalwa jwa setso. Tasting it is a social rather than a tourist custom, so ask locally.

food_culture.name: Kgotla
food_culture.description: The kgotla is the traditional village meeting place where a chief and community discuss and settle matters in the open. Most villages have one; you may be able to visit with a local guide and should ask before entering.

food_culture.name: Mokoro dugout poling
food_culture.description: Mokoros are the shallow canoes that people of the Delta region have long used to move through channels, poled standing up by a guide called a poler; many are now fibreglass rather than carved wood. A poler-led mokoro trip is the traditional way to see the Delta's water level.

food_culture.name: Pula, the word for rain
food_culture.description: Pula means both rain and the national currency, and the national greeting for good fortune is the cry 'Pula!'. In a dry country, rain is blessing, which is why the green season from November to April is celebrated.

food_culture.name: Braai and grilled river fish
food_culture.description: Kasane's riverfront lodges serve braai (grill) of beef and boerewors and, where available, freshwater fish from the Chobe-Zambezi system, usually with pap and relish.

title: Kigali, Gorilla Trekking + Lake Kivu, Rwanda
best_time_description: Rwanda's dry season (June to mid-September, per Visit Rwanda) gives the easiest trails and roads for gorilla trekking; the rainy seasons run roughly mid-February to May and mid-September to mid-December, and forest paths turn muddy after rain. Gorilla trekking runs year-round. Volcanoes National Park is the coolest part of the country, so pack warm layers for evenings in Musanze. RDB's 30% low-season gorilla permit discount (November to May) only applies if the trip also includes two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe, or one night in each, so it does not apply to this route as written.
description: A gorilla-focused first trip to Rwanda: a night in Kigali, the Volcanoes National Park mountain gorillas near Musanze (permit booked months ahead), a golden monkey hike, then two nights on the red-sand shore of Lake Kivu at Rubavu before returning to Kigali. Road legs are about three hours Kigali to Musanze and about an hour Musanze to Rubavu, per Visit Rwanda.

days.title: Arrive Kigali
activities: Arrive at Kigali International Airport; non-visa-exempt nationalities can buy a visa on arrival (see the visa rules for your passport). Foreign nationals who have been in or transited through the DR Congo in the previous 30 days are refused entry under Rwanda's current Ebola measures (RDB notice, 25 May 2026), and health screening runs at the airport.
Visit the Inema Arts Centre and a local market, both suggested on Visit Rwanda's own Kigali stops; confirm opening hours locally
Early night: tomorrow starts with a three-hour drive north

days.title: Kigali to Musanze + the Gorilla Guardian's Centre
activities: Private transfer or hired driver from Kigali to Musanze, about 3 hours (Visit Rwanda's gorilla-tracking itinerary)
Learn the park's history at the Gorilla Guardian's Centre (listed on Visit Rwanda's Safari and Gorilla Tracking itinerary)

The gorilla permit must already be bought: USD 1,500 per person for foreign visitors, 96 permits per day in all of Rwanda, booked in advance on the RDB booking portal or through a licensed tour operator. The minimum age is 15, and documents are checked at the park gate, so a booking made under the wrong name or passport can be refused even if paid.
Musanze is cool in the evenings; unpack long trousers, sturdy hiking boots, gaiters and a light waterproof
days.drive_time: Kigali to Musanze, ~3 hrs by road
days.lodging_suggestion: Musanze (near Kinigi, 13 km from the Volcanoes National Park headquarters)

days.title: Mountain gorilla trekking
activities: Be at the Volcanoes National Park headquarters in Kinigi for the 7:00 briefing, where guides assign gorilla families by fitness
Trek into the forest: the hike can take from about 30 minutes to 4+ hours depending on the family assigned, and the walk back can take as long

Spend one hour with the gorillas (groups are capped at 8 visitors); keep at least 7 m away, do not eat, drink or smoke near them, and cover your mouth if you cough. Anyone with a cold, flu or other contagious illness may be refused access

RDB's refund terms: another chance or full refund if the gorillas' movement prevents tracking all day, 75% refunded if you walk all day without reaching a family, no refund for late arrival, flight delays or no-shows
Porters are available for a small fee
days.drive_time: Hotel to park headquarters, a short drive at sunrise

days.title: Golden monkeys, then Musanze to Rubavu
activities: Golden monkey tracking in the Volcanoes National Park (Visit Rwanda's 3-day gorilla itinerary adds it on the day after the gorilla trek); it needs a separate RDB permit, and the price was not confirmed for this guide, so check the RDB booking portal
Drive from Musanze to Rubavu on Lake Kivu, about 1 hour (Visit Rwanda says Rubavu is an hour away from the Volcanoes National Park)

Evening walk on Rubavu's lakeside promenade. Rubavu town is on the Congo border: Global Affairs Canada advises a high degree of caution in parts of Rubavu district near the DRC border and says the Gisenyi-Goma crossing is prohibited for most travellers. Do not plan any crossing, and check current UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada advice before you book Rubavu.

days.title: Lake Kivu day
activities: Kayak or paddle on Lake Kivu; Visit Rwanda lists watersports and kayaking tours here, and describes the shore as red sandy beaches with warm, clean water

Start the Congo Nile Trail, which begins in Rubavu and runs 227 km south to Rusizi in six stages; walk or cycle a short section of the first stage rather than a full day, as stage details were not confirmed
Visit a tea or coffee plantation near Rubavu (Visit Rwanda mentions plantations nearby)
Alternative if you want a wildlife morning: primate tracking in nearby Gishwati-Mukura National Park (listed on Visit Rwanda's Rubavu page; permit and price not checked)

days.title: Back to Kigali and depart
activities: Drive Rubavu back to Kigali via Musanze: about 1 hour to Musanze plus about 3 hours on to Kigali (Visit Rwanda times), so allow roughly 4 hours plus a stop and leave early for an afternoon flight

If time allows, add the Kigali Genocide Memorial in Gisozi (open about 09:00 to 17:00, last entry 16:00; from 13:00 on the last Saturday of each month because of Umuganda community work); see the second Rwanda itinerary for details
Fly home from Kigali International Airport
days.drive_time: Rubavu to Kigali via Musanze, ~4 hrs total

food_culture.name: Brochettes
food_culture.description: Grilled skewers of goat, beef or fish are a staple of Rwandan roadside bars and evening restaurants, usually eaten with fried plantain (igitoki) or chips and a cold drink. Ask the cook which cut is on offer that day.

food_culture.name: Isombe
food_culture.description: A traditional Rwandan dish of pounded cassava leaves cooked down with eggplant, spinach and sometimes groundnuts, often served alongside ubugari, a stiff cassava or maize porridge. It is a good vegetarian option in Musanze and Rubavu restaurants.

food_culture.name: Rwandan coffee and tea
food_culture.description: Visit Rwanda notes tea and coffee plantations around Rubavu, and Rwanda grows both for export. A cup after a hike or a plantation visit is a simple way to taste the hills you have been driving through.

food_culture.name: Kwita Izina gorilla naming ceremony
food_culture.description: Visit Rwanda describes Kwita Izina as the annual ceremony at which newborn mountain gorillas are given names, and recommends it as a special time to visit Volcanoes National Park. Dates vary, so check the Visit Rwanda site if you want to time a trip around it.

food_culture.name: Umuganda community work
food_culture.description: Rwandans take part in monthly community service work on the last Saturday of the month; some visitor sites, including the Kigali Genocide Memorial, open later that day because of it. Expect slower mornings and plan transfers accordingly.

food_culture.name: Inema Arts Centre
food_culture.description: A Kigali art gallery and studio space that Visit Rwanda lists among its Kigali stops. It is a good place to see contemporary Rwandan painting and to buy works directly.

title: Akagera Safari, Nyungwe Forest + Kigali Memorial, Rwanda
best_time_description: The dry season (June to mid-September, per Visit Rwanda) is the easiest time for Akagera's game drives and Nyungwe's muddy trails; the rainy seasons run roughly mid-February to May and mid-September to mid-December. Visit Rwanda says the Nyungwe canopy walk is open all year, with more chance of rain in the afternoons, so book the walk for the morning in wet months. Akagera is generally the warmest part of the country.
description: A wildlife and forest route that avoids the gorilla permit: a game drive and a Lake Ihema boat trip in Akagera National Park in the east, a respectful visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial, then a long drive west to Nyungwe Forest for chimpanzee tracking and the canopy walkway. Drive times are long: Kigali to Akagera is 4 to 5 hours by Visit Rwanda's figure, Akagera back to Kigali about 3 hours, and Kigali to Nyungwe about 5 hours.

days.title: Arrive Kigali
activities: Arrive at Kigali International Airport; non-visa-exempt nationalities can buy a visa on arrival (see the visa rules for your passport). Foreign nationals who were in or transited through the DR Congo in the previous 30 days are refused entry under Rwanda's current Ebola measures (RDB notice, 25 May 2026).
Visit the Inema Arts Centre and a local market (both on Visit Rwanda's Kigali list) and rest before the early start to Akagera

days.title: Kigali to Akagera National Park
activities: Drive east from Kigali to Akagera, about 4 to 5 hours by Visit Rwanda's Safari and Gorilla Tracking itinerary (mostly paved, with a rougher final section); a Visit Rwanda-hosted 2019 operator package gives about 2.5 hours, so allow the longer figure and ask your lodge for current road advice
Evening boat trip on Lake Ihema for hippos, Nile crocodiles and waterbirds (Visit Rwanda lists the boat trip as a highlight)
Stay inside the park: Visit Rwanda lists lodges, a seasonal bush camp in the north, and camping at specific sites
days.drive_time: Kigali to Akagera, ~4-5 hrs by Visit Rwanda (a 2019 operator package says ~2.5 hrs)
days.lodging_suggestion: Lodge or camp inside Akagera National Park

days.title: Full day in Akagera
activities: Full-day game drive with a guide: the park can only be explored by vehicle (guided or self-drive), and the park rents vehicles and guides; Visit Rwanda lists buffalo, lion, leopard, elephant, giraffe, spotted hyena and zebra
Visit Rwanda says 18 eastern black rhinos have been reintroduced and the park has about 490 bird species
Individual seats on night drives are offered by the park; book ahead through the park, as availability and prices were not confirmed
Guided walks are also available (Visit Rwanda)
days.lodging_suggestion: Lodge or camp inside Akagera National Park

days.title: Akagera to Kigali + Genocide Memorial
activities: Drive back to Kigali, about 3 hours (Visit Rwanda)

Visit the Kigali Genocide Memorial in Gisozi, about 10 minutes from the city centre: the memorial's own site describes it as the final resting place of 250,000 victims of the Genocide against the Tutsi and a place of remembrance and learning. Open about 09:00 to 17:00 with last entry at 16:00, seven days a week, but from 13:00 on the last Saturday of each month because of Umuganda. Guided tours are given by guides, many of them survivors; groups should book in advance (more than 15 people at least a week ahead). The memorial asks visitors to dress and behave respectfully; entry fee and photography rules were not stated on the pages checked, so ask at the entrance.
Allow quiet time afterwards; dinner in the city

days.title: Kigali to Nyungwe Forest
activities: Leave early for Nyungwe: a New Times article puts Kigali to Nyungwe at about 5 hours; the tourism board gives no figure, and some operators stop in Huye on the way, so allow a full travel day

If you arrive with daylight left, walk to the Nyungwe canopy walkway: 160 m long and 70 m above a ravine, about an hour's walk from the Uwinka Reception Centre; international visitors pay USD 40, booked via kivubelt.travel (Visit Rwanda). Wear suitable footwear, take a light raincoat; boots, a raincoat and a walking stick can be rented at park headquarters

Rusizi, about an hour's drive from Nyungwe, is the closest town; Global Affairs Canada advises a high degree of caution in parts of Rusizi district near the DRC border, so check current advisories when choosing where to sleep
days.drive_time: Kigali to Nyungwe, ~5 hrs (New Times); no tourism-board figure
days.lodging_suggestion: Lodge near Nyungwe National Park (check location against current advisories)

days.title: Chimpanzee tracking in Nyungwe
activities: Early chimpanzee tracking: Visit Rwanda's itinerary describes a trek of one to four hours with about an hour with the chimpanzees; the permit must be booked in advance through the RDB booking portal (price not checked for this guide) and expect a very early start
Return to your lodge to rest, then use the afternoon for forest trails; the footpaths can be muddy, especially after rain
If you skipped the canopy walkway on day 5, do it now (see day 5)

days.title: Nyungwe to Kigali and depart
activities: Drive back to Kigali, about 5 hours (New Times figure); book an evening or late flight home
A stop in Huye is common on this road, but opening hours of its museums were not checked for this guide
Fly home from Kigali International Airport

food_culture.name: Tilapia from Lake Kivu and Rwandan lakes
food_culture.description: Grilled or fried tilapia is a common lakeside lunch in Rwanda, served whole with chips or boiled banana. Ask your lodge what fish is on the menu.

food_culture.name: Ubugari and isombe
food_culture.description: Ubugari is a stiff cassava or maize porridge eaten with stews, and isombe is a pounded cassava-leaf dish; together they are a classic Rwandan home meal and a safe vegetarian choice when lodges offer a local menu.

food_culture.name: Urwagwa (banana beer)
food_culture.description: A traditional Rwandan beer fermented from bananas, served at social gatherings and ceremonies. Try it only from a reputable venue and drink moderately.

food_culture.name: Remembrance and Umuganda
food_culture.description: The last Saturday of each month is Umuganda, a day of community service across Rwanda, and the Kigali Genocide Memorial opens in the afternoon only on that day. April is the national commemoration period for the Genocide against the Tutsi; visitors are asked to dress and behave respectfully at memorial sites.

food_culture.name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
food_culture.description: The memorial's own site calls it the final resting place for 250,000 victims of the Genocide against the Tutsi and a place of reconciliation and peace education; many guides are survivors. It is a place of mass burial, not an attraction, so visit with time to spare and a quiet frame of mind.

food_culture.name: Inema Arts Centre
food_culture.description: A Kigali gallery and studio space that Visit Rwanda lists among its Kigali stops, showing contemporary Rwandan art. It is a good place to buy a locally made piece directly.

title: Accra, Cape Coast Castle, Kakum + Kumasi, Ghana
best_time_description: The Ghana Tourism Authority describes October to March as the dry season (and warns that haze during the Harmattan, roughly November to March, spoils long views). It also says it can rain at any time in Kakum's rainforest, so pack a raincoat in any month. Fetu Afahye, Cape Coast's durbar of chiefs, falls on the first Saturday of September, and the Asante king sits in session at Manhyia every sixth Sunday (Akwasidae), so those dates add colour but also crowds.
description: Ghana's classic first-timer arc: Accra's independence-era sites, then the UNESCO-listed Cape Coast and Elmina castles and the Kakum rainforest canopy walkway on the Central Region coast, and inland to Kumasi for the Asante palace museum, the fort and Kente weaving at Bonwire. Seven days, mostly by road, with bus times from the state bus company STC.

days.title: Arrive Accra
activities: Settle in and keep the first day light after the flight; visa and yellow fever certificate checks happen on arrival, so have the e-visa or ETA and the vaccination card to hand.
Independence Square, where the Independence Arch and the Black Star Monument stand (Ghana Tourism Authority).

Nationalism Park in Osu, between Independence Square and the Accra Sports Stadium: listed by the Ghana Tourism Authority as open daily 10am to 10pm with an adult ticket of GHC 20 (confirm on the day; the page does not say whether that is the foreign rate).

days.title: Museums and Black Star history, Accra
activities: National Museum of Ghana, 2 Barnes Road, Adabraka: open 9am to 4:30pm daily per the Ghana Museums and Monuments Board (GMMB). GMMB's published non-Ghanaian adult ticket for the National Museum and castles is GH¢80, a figure its fees page labels as pre-revision, so ask the current price at the desk.

Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park on Prof. Atta Mills High Street: the Ghana Tourism Authority lists 8:30am to 11pm Monday to Friday and 9am to 11pm at weekends, with a non-Ghanaian adult ticket of GHS 100 (an April 2025 listing, so confirm the price).
W.E.B. Du Bois Centre, 1 Circular Road, Cantonments (his museum, former home and tomb): hours and fees are not published, so call +233 30 277 6502 before going.
Jamestown is worth a walk for its old streets, but note that GMMB closed James Fort and Ussher Fort to the public from 18 December 2025 until further notice, so do not plan to go inside them.

days.title: Accra to Cape Coast Castle
activities: Head west along the coast to Cape Coast in the morning by pre-arranged car or bus. The state bus company STC lists Accra to Takoradi at about 4 hours (stc.gov.gh); it publishes no Cape Coast time on that page, so confirm the Cape Coast stop and departure times with STC on +233 557943605.

Cape Coast Castle: open daily 9am to 4:30pm (GMMB). Guided tours cover Dalzel Tower, the dungeons used in the slave trade, and the cannons; the West African Historical Museum is inside. GMMB's non-Ghanaian adult ticket was GH¢80 at the 1 July 2023 review, and the board says fees have been revised since, so check at the gate.
The castle is a UNESCO-listed national monument; plan on the full guided tour, which is the only way to see the dungeons.

days.title: Kakum canopy walk and Elmina Castle
activities: Kakum National Park is 39 km north of Cape Coast (Ghana Tourism Authority). The park is listed as open 6am to 4pm; go first thing for the 333 m canopy walkway, seven suspension bridges up to 27 m above the forest floor. The fee chart on the tourism authority's page is an image, so ask at the park (033 213 0265) and take a raincoat and sturdy shoes.

Elmina (St George's) Castle, built by the Portuguese in 1482: open daily 9am to 4:30pm (GMMB), non-Ghanaian adult ticket GH¢80 at the 1 July 2023 review (since revised; confirm). GMMB gives no Cape Coast to Elmina time, so ask your driver or hotel for the current journey time and leave enough margin before the 4:30pm close.
Within walking distance of Elmina Castle: Fort St Jago (Coenraadsburg), the Dutch cemetery, the Posuban shrines and the fishing harbour (GMMB).
days.drive_time: Kakum: 39 km north of Cape Coast (tourism authority); Elmina time not published

days.title: Cape Coast to Kumasi
activities: Travel inland to Kumasi, Ashanti Region, in daylight: the UK FCDO advises against road travel outside main towns after dark. STC lists Accra to Kumasi at about 4 hours (GHS 120), but publishes no Cape Coast to Kumasi time, so check with STC or hire a reputable pre-booked driver.
Kejetia Market, which the Ghana Tourism Authority calls the largest open-air market in West Africa; haggling is expected.

days.title: Kumasi: the Asante capital
activities: Manhyia Palace Museum: listed 9am to 5pm, GHS 10 (Ghana Tourism Authority), with guided tours of royal regalia, gold work and Asante history. The tourism authority does not say which days it is closed, so call +233 032 202 3680 first.
Kumasi Fort and Military Museum: GMMB lists 8am to 5pm, closed Sundays and public holidays, with a guided tour at GH¢5.

Bonwire Kente village, about 19 km from Kumasi by the tourism authority's figures: workshop and weaving demonstrations at the visitor centre, listed 8am to 5pm daily (another line on the same page says 9am), fees not listed; call 0244378599.
If you are in Kumasi on an Akwasidae Sunday (every sixth Sunday), the Asante king sits in session at Manhyia with drumming and processions.

days.title: Kumasi back to Accra
activities: STC bus from Kumasi to Accra: about 4 hours, GHS 120 on the Accra to Kumasi fare listed by the operator (stc.gov.gh); departure times are by phone or the STC booking site, so book ahead.
Leave a wide margin if you have an evening international flight, and avoid arriving by road after dark.

food_culture.name: Jollof rice
food_culture.description: Rice cooked in a spiced tomato base and served with chicken, fish or fried plantain; a staple order at Accra restaurants and a dish West Africans playfully argue over.

food_culture.name: Banku and grilled tilapia
food_culture.description: Fermented corn and cassava dough eaten with grilled tilapia, fresh pepper and shito; a common lunch along the coast and around the lagoons.

food_culture.name: Fufu with light soup
food_culture.description: Pounded cassava and plantain served in a peppery soup; the signature meal of Asante cooking and easy to find in Kumasi.

food_culture.name: Waakye
food_culture.description: Rice and beans cooked with dried millet leaves, sold with spaghetti, boiled egg, gari and stew from street stalls, often for breakfast.

food_culture.name: Sobolo
food_culture.description: A chilled hibiscus drink spiced with ginger and cloves, sold in bottles and cups across Ghana.

food_culture.name: Kente weaving
food_culture.description: Strips of silk or cotton woven on narrow looms and sewn together; Bonwire near Kumasi is the royal Kente weaving village, where the Ghana Tourism Authority says visitors can try spinning, warping and weaving.

food_culture.name: Akwasidae at Manhyia
food_culture.description: Every sixth Sunday the Asante king sits in session at Manhyia Palace with processions, drumming and music, as described by the Ghana Tourism Authority.

food_culture.name: Fetu Afahye
food_culture.description: Cape Coast's festival with a durbar of chiefs, held on the first Saturday of September according to the Ghana Tourism Authority.

title: Volta Region: Keta, Ho, Wli Falls + Mount Afadjato, Ghana
best_time_description: The Ghana Tourism Authority says Wli Falls are most impressive from April to October, but the upper-falls hike is usually too slippery and dangerous in the rainiest months. It calls October to March the dry season (best for butterflies at Mount Afadjato) while noting that views from Afadjato and Mount Gemi are generally poor during the Harmattan haze, November to March. October and April are the overlap. The Anlo Hogbetsotso festival at Anloga has its main durbar on the first Saturday of November and the Asogli Yam Festival in Ho is in September.
description: A hiking-and-heritage loop through Ghana's Volta Region: the Keta lagoon coast and lighthouse, Ho's regional museum, the hill village of Amedzofe, Wli (the Ghana Tourism Authority's 'highest waterfall in Ghana'), Mount Afadjato and the Tafi Atome monkey sanctuary, ending with Kente weaving.

days.title: Accra to Keta
activities: Travel east along the coast to Keta in the morning. The Ghana Tourism Authority and GMMB publish no Accra to Keta journey time, so ask your driver or a local station for the current time before booking onward plans.

Keta Cape St Paul Lighthouse in Woe, just off Keta's main road: built in 1901 and billed as the country's oldest lighthouse; the climb to the top is described as somewhat daunting and rewards you with views of the beaches and Woe's farmland.

Fort Prinzenstein, Keta: GMMB says the building is in poor condition with parts lost to the sea, and a revitalisation project began in 2025. GMMB does not say whether it is open to visitors, so call GMMB on +233-302 221633 before relying on a visit.
Do not swim on the open beach: the UK FCDO warns that southern-coast beaches have dangerous rip tides and undertows.

days.title: Keta to Ho
activities: Continue inland to Ho, the regional capital. No official Keta to Ho time was found; plan a daylight arrival (the FCDO advises against road travel outside main towns after dark).

Volta Regional Museum, 43 Glala Street, Ho: open daily 8am to 5pm (GMMB). GMMB's non-Ghanaian adult ticket for forts and regional museums was GH¢40 at the 1 July 2023 review (since revised; confirm). Exhibits include Volta Region Kente designs, chiefs' stools and the chair of state of the last German colonial governor.
In September Ho hosts the Asogli Yam Festival with a durbar of chiefs at Jubilee Park, per the Ghana Tourism Authority.

days.title: Amedzofe and Mount Gemi
activities: Amedzofe, the highest habitable village in Ghana at over 600 m, is 35 km from Ho; trotros run infrequently from the Ho lorry station, so a hired car is easier. The visitor centre is listed open 6am to 5:30pm daily; fees are not published.
Mount Gemi summit: about 1.5 hours, with 360-degree views; go early as the trail has no shade.
Amedzofe Falls: about 2 hours, with a very steep rope-assisted final stretch; water is at its peak May to November and may be greatly reduced or dry January to March.
Short village walk to the old German church and bell tower (about 30 minutes).
Continue towards Hohoe in the afternoon; no official Ho to Hohoe time was found.

days.title: Wli Falls
activities: Wli Waterfalls, in the Hohoe municipality near the Togo border and about 280 km from Accra: drive east from Hohoe, turn right at Lipke Bakwa and continue about 3 km to Wli.

Lower falls: about 1.5 hours with a guide, mostly flat. Upper falls: the tourism authority gives 3 to 5 hours depending on the section and says the upper hike is usually too slippery in the rainiest months, so ask the guide before committing.
Entrance and guide fees are not listed by the tourism authority; pay at the visitor centre.
days.drive_time: Wli turn-off to village: about 3 km (tourism authority)

days.title: Mount Afadjato and Tagbo Falls
activities: Liati Wote village is 24 km from Hohoe; the visitor centre is on the left as you enter and is open 8am to 5pm daily. Hike with a guide arranged there.

Mount Afadjato (885 m): about 2.5 hours, difficulty 3 of 5 on the tourism authority's scale; climb early morning or late afternoon because there is little shade. Views are generally poor in the Harmattan (November to March).
Tagbo Falls hike: about 2 hours, mostly shaded, through butterfly habitat, cocoa and coffee farms, ending at a cold plunge pool. Water flow is reduced in the dry season.
Fees are not listed; ask at the visitor centre or the Ghana Tourism Authority (Info@ghana.travel).
days.drive_time: Hohoe to Liati Wote: 24 km (tourism authority)

days.title: Tafi Atome monkey sanctuary
activities: Tafi Atome Monkey Sanctuary is 43 km south of Hohoe: leave the main Ho to Hohoe road at Logba Alekpeti and follow the sign along a 5 km dirt road to the visitor centre. Listed open 6am to 6pm daily; entrance fees are not listed.
Monkey sanctuary tour with a guide takes 1 to 1.5 hours; the tourism authority says the monkeys forage 6 to 8am and 3:30 to 6pm in November to January and are otherwise out at any time.
Optional village tour (about 1 hour), pineapple farm visit (45 minutes) and evening drumming or bonfire stories.
Stay in the rustic 6-room guesthouse by the visitor centre or a home-stay; the community cook serves meals in an open-air shelter.
days.drive_time: Hohoe to Tafi Atome: 43 km south, then 5 km dirt road (tourism authority)

days.title: Kente weaving and return to Accra
activities: Tafi Abuipe Kente weaving village is 14 km by car or 7 km by trail from Tafi Atome (tourism authority); allow about 2 hours to watch the weavers.

Leave for Accra in daylight; the tourism authority gives Wli as about 280 km from Accra but no journey time, so build in a generous buffer if you have a flight, and do not drive after dark outside main towns (FCDO).
days.drive_time: Tafi Atome to Abuipe: 14 km by car (tourism authority)

food_culture.name: Banku with grilled tilapia or okro soup
food_culture.description: Fermented corn and cassava dough, a core food across southern Ghana and particularly associated with Ewe cooking; eat it with grilled fish and fresh pepper near Lake Volta and the lagoons.

food_culture.name: Akple with fetri detsi
food_culture.description: Akple, a smooth maize and cassava dough, served with okro soup (fetri detsi) is a classic Ewe meal in the Volta Region.

food_culture.name: Kenkey and fried fish
food_culture.description: Fermented, steamed corn dough wrapped in leaves or husks and eaten with fried fish and pepper sauce; sold at roadside stalls and markets in towns like Keta.

food_culture.name: Sobolo
food_culture.description: A chilled hibiscus drink spiced with ginger, sold in cups and bottles across Ghana.

food_culture.name: Kente weaving at Tafi Abuipe
food_culture.description: A village weaving Volta-style Kente on narrow looms; the Ghana Tourism Authority lists a Kente weaving visit as a 2-hour activity from Tafi Atome.

food_culture.name: Hogbetsotso Za
food_culture.description: The Anlo-Ewe festival at Anloga marking the exodus from Notsie, with a durbar of chiefs on the first Saturday of November and a week of purification rites, dancing and drumming (Ghana Tourism Authority).

food_culture.name: Asogli Yam Festival
food_culture.description: Ho's September harvest festival, in which the Asogli State thanks God and the ancestors for the harvest, hails and feasts on the new yam and holds a durbar of chiefs at Jubilee Park.

title: South + West Mauritius: Gorges, Chamarel + Le Morne
best_time_description: May to October is the cooler, drier half of the year (the Mauritius Meteorological Services puts the cool dry winter at June to September, with October and May as transition months and October the driest month), which suits the gorge trails and the Le Morne climb. November to April is warm and humid and May is the end of cyclone season, so a trip from January to March needs a flexible plan. Cyclone season runs November to May (Global Affairs Canada, Australian DFAT), so January to March is the peak risk window; the Mauritius Meteorological Services calls February and March the wettest months and runs a four-class cyclone warning system (Class I is issued 36 to 48 hours before gusts of 120 km/h). During cyclones the airport may close and flights be cancelled, so buy flexible fares and insurance and keep a spare night at the end of the trip.
description: A south-and-west loop for people who want forest, mountains and a living heritage story rather than resort time: the endemic ebony forest of Ile aux Aigrettes, the Hindu lake at Grand Bassin, Black River Gorges National Park, Chamarel's coloured dunes, and the UNESCO-listed Le Morne peninsula. Drive on the left; the whole island is only about 61 km north to south.

days.title: Arrive Mauritius, Mahebourg
activities: Land at Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport, which sits on the southeast coast; complete the free All-in-One Travel Form and Health Declaration Form before boarding
Pick up a hire car (international companies are at the airport; drive on the left) or arrange a taxi through your accommodation
Walk the Mahebourg waterfront in the afternoon

Check current conditions before you travel: on 13 October 2026 the US Embassy reported countrywide localised demonstrations, traffic disruption and a lack of public transport, so confirm the situation with your accommodation

days.title: Mahebourg Museum + Ile aux Aigrettes
activities: Morning: Ile aux Aigrettes EcoTour with the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation, a guided trail of about 1.5 to 2 hours plus a short boat trip to and from the 26-hectare coralline island 850 m off the southeast coast; book online ahead through the foundation's booking partner (tour times and prices are on that booking page)
Look for the restored dry coastal forest, rare reptiles, tortoises and birds such as the pink pigeon and Mauritius fody
Afternoon: Mahebourg Museum in Gheude Castle, with a nearly complete dodo skeleton, old maps and relics salvaged from shipwrecks and naval battles (check opening times locally)

days.title: Grand Bassin + Black River Gorges
activities: Drive inland to Grand Bassin (Ganga Talao), a sacred crater lake in the Savanne mountains with a 33 m statue of Shiva at its entrance; dress modestly and expect monkeys

Continue to Black River Gorges National Park, the largest in Mauritius (about 17,000 acres, more than 50 km of trails); walk a marked trail and stop at the Alexandra Falls viewpoint, following the signs

Black River Peak at 828 m is the island's highest point. The park's entry fee and visitor-centre hours could not be confirmed from the National Parks and Conservation Service pages, so ask your accommodation or the park office before you set out

Allow time for slow roads: the longest cross-island drives take about 1 hour 20 minutes (61 km north to south, per the Mauritius Tourism Promotion Authority), and this leg is shorter than that; check a live map for traffic

days.title: Chamarel: coloured earth, waterfall + coffee
activities: Chamarel 7 Coloured Earth Geopark: open 8:30 am to 5:30 pm October to May (last ticket 5 pm) and 8:30 am to 5 pm June to September, including Sundays and public holidays; non-resident adult ticket Rs 800, children 5 to 11 Rs 400, under 5 free; pay in Mauritian rupees (cash, cards other than Diners Club, or mobile payment), tickets are non-refundable and valid for one entry

Inside the gate it is a 1.5 km drive to the two waterfall viewpoints and 3 km to the dunes, with parking at both; the ticket also covers the Aldabra tortoise park (suggested visit 45 minutes to 2 hours). Walking down to the base of the falls on your own is prohibited; the park points to a guided provider
Visit the Chamarel coffee plantation (the park's own coffee shop and souvenir shop open daily 9:30 am to 5 pm)

days.title: Le Morne Brabant
activities: Le Morne Cultural Landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site tied to escaped slaves who sheltered on the mountain in the 18th and early 19th centuries; Mauritius Now calls it a symbol of suffering, sacrifice and freedom
Optional summit hike of roughly three hours, started before dawn with an expert guide (arrange through a licensed local operator; the final stretch is steep and rocky)
Afternoon at Le Morne beach, known for kitesurfing on the windy peninsula

days.title: West coast and departure buffer
activities: Slow morning on the west coast; the tourism board lists Tamarin Bay street food and Ile aux Benitiers (snorkelling to Crystal Rock) as nearby options

Drive back to the airport; allow the full cross-island figure (up to about 1 hour 20 minutes) plus a buffer, and keep a spare night before an international flight in the November to May cyclone season
days.lodging_suggestion: Near the airport or Le Morne

food_culture.name: Chamarel coffee
food_culture.description: Chamarel's plantation is described by the operator of the Chamarel 7 Coloured Earth Geopark as Mauritius' only coffee plantation, and its coffee shop sits inside the park.

food_culture.name: Maha Shivaratri pilgrimage to Grand Bassin
food_culture.description: Grand Bassin (Ganga Talao) is the centre of the Maha Shivaratri festival, when many Hindu worshippers walk to the lake to pray and make offerings, according to the Mauritius Tourism Promotion Authority. Outside the festival it is a quiet shrine-lined lake.

food_culture.name: Le Morne: memory of resistance
food_culture.description: The Le Morne peninsula is a UNESCO World Heritage Site because escaped slaves took refuge on the mountain; it is treated locally as a place of remembrance as well as a hike.

food_culture.name: Dodo and the museum at Mahebourg
food_culture.description: the Mahebourg Museum, in the colonial Gheude Castle, holds a nearly complete dodo skeleton, the island's best-known extinct bird.

food_culture.name: Street food at Tamarin Bay
food_culture.description: The tourism board points to street food on the west coast around Tamarin Bay; the Port Louis market list (samosas, dholl puri) is the same snack tradition.

title: Port Louis, Grand Baie + East Coast Islands, Mauritius
best_time_description: May to October is cooler and drier (the Mauritius Meteorological Services calls October the driest month and June to September the cool dry winter), which is best for boat days to Ile aux Cerfs and the northern islets. January to March is warm, humid and the wettest part of the cyclone season, so book flexible boat trips and keep a spare night. Cyclone season runs November to May (Global Affairs Canada, Australian DFAT), so January to March is the peak risk window; the Mauritius Meteorological Services calls February and March the wettest months and runs a four-class cyclone warning system (Class I is issued 36 to 48 hours before gusts of 120 km/h). During cyclones the airport may close and flights be cancelled, so buy flexible fares and insurance and keep a spare night at the end of the trip.
description: A capital-to-coast route: reef snorkelling at Blue Bay, a boat day to Ile aux Cerfs, Port Louis's World Heritage depot, market and hilltop fort, the historic gardens and sugar museum around Pamplemousses, then Grand Baie and the northern islets. It follows the airport, east coast, capital and north in one direction, so you never double back.

days.title: Arrive Mauritius, Blue Bay
activities: Land at Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport on the southeast coast; complete the free All-in-One Travel Form and Health Declaration Form before boarding (the Passport and Immigration Office calls both mandatory)
Afternoon at Blue Bay Beach, which Mauritius Now describes as having shady casuarinas, soft white sand and street-food vendors; weekdays are quiet and weekends bring live music and picnics

Check current conditions before you travel: on 13 October 2026 the US Embassy reported countrywide localised demonstrations, traffic disruption and a lack of public transport, so confirm the situation with your accommodation

days.title: Blue Bay Marine Park
activities: Snorkel from Blue Bay Beach or take a glass-bottom boat over the coral garden in the protected Blue Bay Marine Park (brain coral, butterflyfish, damselfish; turtles and dolphins are possible); boat operators, fares and times are set by the operators, so agree them at the beach
Optional: the Mahebourg Museum in Gheude Castle (dodo skeleton, shipwreck relics; check opening times locally)

days.title: East coast: Ile aux Cerfs
activities: Drive north along the east coast to Pointe Maurice

Take the beach shuttle to Ile aux Cerfs: according to Mauritius Now it runs every 30 minutes from 9:30 am to 6 pm to the Masala Jetty, with a separate golf shuttle every 20 minutes; crossing time and fares are on the Ile aux Cerfs Leisure Island site
Beach bars on the northern tip, parasailing and other watersports over the reef; the island has no hotels, only three eco-bubble lodges
Walk the east coast of the island to a quieter spot under the casuarinas
days.lodging_suggestion: Trou d'Eau Douce or Belle Mare

days.title: Port Louis: heritage, market + fort
activities: Drive to Port Louis (the cross-island figures from the tourism board are 45 km east to west in about 1 hour 15 minutes, and this leg is shorter than the full width); optional stop at Eureka House in Moka, a colonial home built around 1836 and now a museum

Aapravasi Ghat (UNESCO): remains of three original stone buildings, artefacts and a ten-minute film with testimonials from workers' descendants; the depot received more than 462,000 indentured labourers, mainly from India (hours and fees were not confirmed from an official page; check on arrival)
Port Louis Central Market for samosas, dholl puri and alouda; the market hours are not published on the tourism board page, so go in the morning and ask locally
Le Caudan Waterfront next door, with the Blue Penny Museum (the island's rare blue penny stamp) and the Caudan Arts Centre
Sunset at La Citadel (Fort Adelaide), a British fortress built 1830 to 1840 with 360-degree views over the city

days.title: Pamplemousses + sugar museum + Labourdonnais
activities: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Botanical Garden at Pamplemousses (opening hours and entry fee were not confirmed from an official page; check at the gate)

L'Aventure du Sucre in Pamplemousses, a museum in a historic sugar mill covering over 280 years of sugar history, with tasting of more than 30 sugarcane products (hours and fees are on the operator's site)
Domaine de Labourdonnais in the north: restored 19th-century chateau, underground museum, rum and juice tastings (confirm tour times and fees with the estate at domainedelabourdonnais.com)

days.title: Grand Baie + northern islets
activities: Day cruise by catamaran from the north coast to the northern islets; landing is prohibited on Coin de Mire (visitors are not allowed ashore for conservation reasons), Round Island (research only) and Serpent Island, but Ile aux Gabriel's white sandbar and Ile Plate are the usual swim and snorkel stops; confirm the itinerary, price and weather cancellation policy with the operator
Afternoon at Cap Malheureux's red-roofed church, Notre-Dame Auxiliatrice, one of the most photographed sights on the island, against the headland of Coin de Mire
Evening in Grand Baie: about 50 cafes and restaurants line the bay, with live bands and Sega on some weeknights and beach clubs busiest on Friday and Saturday

days.title: Grand Baie free day
activities: Choose a beach or snorkel morning around Grand Baie; this is your weather buffer if a boat day was cancelled in the cyclone season
Optional dive or private cruise (arrange with a licensed operator)

days.title: Return to the airport
activities: Drive back toward the southeast airport; the tourism board's longest island-wide figure is about 61 km north to south in roughly 1 hour 20 minutes by car, so allow that plus a buffer, and check live traffic around Port Louis
Keep a spare night before an international flight in the November to May cyclone season, when the airport may close

food_culture.name: Dholl puri and samosas
food_culture.description: Street-food kiosks at Port Louis Central Market sell samosas and dholl puri, according to Mauritius Now, which also lists alouda as a local drink.

food_culture.name: Alouda
food_culture.description: A creamy local cold drink sold in the Port Louis market area, listed by the Mauritius Tourism Promotion Authority among the dishes to try.

food_culture.name: Sugarcane and rum tastings
food_culture.description: Domaine de Labourdonnais offers handcrafted rum, juice and jam tastings and rum workshops, and L'Aventure du Sucre in Pamplemousses lets visitors taste more than 30 sugarcane products and cane-juice cocktails.

food_culture.name: Aapravasi Ghat and the indentured labourers
food_culture.description: Aapravasi Ghat is the UNESCO-listed immigration depot where more than 462,000 indentured labourers, mostly from India, arrived after slavery was abolished; about 70 percent of Mauritians descend from them, according to Mauritius Now.

food_culture.name: Sega and weekend nightlife in Grand Baie
food_culture.description: Grand Baie has live bands and Sega performances during the week and beach clubs busiest on Friday and Saturday nights, per the tourism board.

title: Muscat, Nizwa, Jebel Akhdar + Wahiba Sands, Oman
best_time_description: October to March is the best window: Visit Oman calls it the pleasant, cool part of the year, and winter is the coolest and driest season. Jebel Akhdar's rose fields bloom in spring (March to May). Summer on the plains and in the dunes is very hot (Visit Oman gives an average of about 35 C), so avoid June to September for the desert and mountain legs. Wadis can flash-flood after heavy rain, mainly October to March (UK FCDO), so check the forecast on any wadi day.
description: Oman's classic first loop by 4x4: Muscat's mosque and souq, the fort town of Nizwa, the terraced villages of Jebel Akhdar, a night in the Wahiba Sands dunes and a swim at Wadi Bani Khalid. About 750 km of driving over 7 days, with the two hardest stretches (the mountain plateau and the dunes) done in a properly equipped 4x4. Check your government's current travel advice first: the UK FCDO's July 2026 update reports regional tensions, including strikes in Oman.

days.title: Arrive Muscat
activities: Collect the hire 4x4 at the airport or in town. UK FCDO: a UK photocard licence can be used for the first 6 weeks (paper licences or some hire firms may need an International Driving Permit); fines for traffic offences can reach 3,000 rials and mobile phones may not be used while driving.
Evening stroll along Mutrah Corniche and into Mutrah Souq (shop hours vary; many shops close for a midday break)

Before you go: check your government's travel advice. The UK FCDO (updated 22 July 2026) reports regional tensions with strikes and attacks including in Oman, and warns of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.

days.title: Muscat: Grand Mosque, museums and Opera House
activities: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque: open to non-Muslim visitors only at set morning hours on set days. I could not reach the mosque's own website, so check its current visiting hours and closed days before you go. Dress rules: UK FCDO says clothing should cover the tops of the arms and legs to below the knee and not be tight; women should expect to be asked to cover their hair, so carry a scarf (confirm at the gate).
National Museum of Oman (check current opening hours and ticket price on arrival)
Royal Opera House Muscat: Visit Oman lists guided tours of the building; check the tour schedule and book ahead
Dinner in Mutrah or Qurum; tourists can drink alcohol only in licensed venues such as hotels (UK FCDO)

days.title: Muscat to Nizwa, then Bahla
activities: Drive Muscat (Grand Mosque) to Nizwa: about 139 km, roughly 1 h 40 min by road

Nizwa Fort and the souq beside it; check the fort's current opening hours and ticket price at the entrance. Nizwa's weekly Friday livestock market is the best-known local tradition; confirm timing locally if your trip falls on a Friday.

Afternoon: drive Nizwa to Bahla (about 40 km, roughly 35 min) to see the walled oasis town and its fort, a UNESCO World Heritage site; check whether the fort is open to visitors, as restoration closures have happened
days.drive_time: Muscat to Nizwa ~139 km, ~1 h 40 min; Nizwa to Bahla ~40 km, ~35 min

days.title: Nizwa to Jebel Akhdar (4x4 only)
activities: Drive Nizwa to the Sayq Plateau on Jebel Akhdar: about 61 km, roughly 55 min. 4x4 requirement: UK FCDO says desert and mountain trips are dangerous unless you have a well-equipped 4WD. Ask your hire company in writing whether your vehicle is permitted on the Jebel Akhdar road and whether insurance covers it; do not attempt it in a 2WD saloon.
Walk the terraced villages on the plateau rim on marked trails only (UK FCDO: follow marked trails; heat has caused deaths from dehydration)
In spring (March to May) the rose fields bloom and Visit Oman notes you can tour a rose distillery; the rest of the year there are no roses
Plan to be off the mountain roads by dusk: Visit Oman travel tips advise against driving at night in rural areas
days.drive_time: Nizwa to Sayq Plateau ~61 km, ~55 min

days.title: Jebel Akhdar to the Wahiba Sands
activities: Drive to Bidiyah, the usual gateway to the Wahiba Sands: about 198 km, roughly 2 h 50 min by paved road

4x4 requirement: the dunes are soft sand. Only drive in with a high-clearance 4x4, a driver experienced in dune driving, or a camp's own transfer vehicle; UK FCDO advises carrying plenty of water and a phone, travelling in convoy if possible, sharing your plans, and checking your insurance covers it. Many camps offer pick-up at the edge of the dunes; ask when booking.
Sunset from a dune ridge and dinner at a desert camp
days.drive_time: Jebel Akhdar to Bidiyah ~198 km, ~2 h 50 min

days.title: Wadi Bani Khalid and back to Muscat
activities: Sunrise on the dunes, then out to Bidiyah

Drive Bidiyah to Wadi Bani Khalid: about 47 km, roughly 50 min. Walk up the wadi to the pools (Visit Oman calls it the country's largest and most famous oasis). Swim in modest clothing (UK FCDO: swimwear only at tourist beaches or pools) and skip it if rain is forecast anywhere upstream, as wadis flood suddenly.
Drive Wadi Bani Khalid to Muscat: about 218 km, roughly 2 h 50 min
days.drive_time: Bidiyah to Wadi Bani Khalid ~47 km, ~50 min; Wadi Bani Khalid to Muscat ~218 km, ~2 h 50 min

days.title: Muscat: dhow cruise and departure
activities: Visit Oman lists a sunset dhow cruise off Muscat and tours of the Royal Opera House and Amouage perfume factory; book ahead and confirm times
Return the 4x4 and fly out. Note recreational drones are prohibited (Visit Oman) and UK FCDO says flying one needs a licence.

food_culture.name: Omani kahwa with dates
food_culture.description: Cardamom-spiced coffee, often with saffron or rosewater, poured from a dallah pot into small handleless cups, usually with dates. Offered to guests at hotels, forts and homes; accept at least one cup. (Customs described from general knowledge, not an official source.)

food_culture.name: Omani halwa
food_culture.description: A dense sweet made with sugar, rosewater, ghee and nuts, served alongside kahwa. Nizwa's souq is known for halwa sellers. (General knowledge, not an official source.)

food_culture.name: Shuwa
food_culture.description: Marinated lamb or goat wrapped in leaves and slow-cooked underground for many hours, traditionally prepared for Eid. Rarely on tourist menus outside the festival period; ask hotels and camps in advance. (General knowledge, not an official source.)

food_culture.name: Fort and souq culture in Nizwa
food_culture.description: Nizwa's souq and fort are the center of the town's trade; the Friday morning livestock market is a long-running local tradition. Photograph people only with permission (Visit Oman and UK FCDO both advise asking first).

food_culture.name: Dress and conduct
food_culture.description: Oman is an Islamic country. UK FCDO advises modest dress in public, including malls, with arms and legs covered to below the knee, and stricter dress at religious sites. Many Omani men wear the white dishdasha with an embroidered cap (kuma) or turban (massar).

title: Salalah in Khareef Season + Wadi Shab and Sur, Oman
best_time_description: Go in Khareef, the southern monsoon season, when Dhofar turns green and stays far cooler than the rest of Oman. Visit Oman gives June to August and says Salalah temperatures of roughly 20 to 28 C against an Omani summer average of about 35 C; Oman Air describes Khareef as June to September; and Oman's civil aviation met service says the drizzle season in Dhofar runs from late June to mid-September. Expect low cloud and fog on the mountains (the met service advises fog lights). The east-coast extension in the same months is hot: do Wadi Shab at first light. UK FCDO notes Indian Ocean cyclones sometimes affect Oman in July and August.
description: Four nights in Dhofar for the Khareef: Salalah's frankincense heritage, the ancient port of Khor Rori, Mirbat, Wadi Darbat and the western blowholes at Mughsail. Then a flight to Muscat and the east coast: the Wadi Shab gorge walk, Bimmah Sinkhole and the old port of Sur. You will want a hire car for the Dhofar day trips. Check your government's current travel advice first: the UK FCDO's July 2026 update reports regional tensions, including strikes in Oman, and possible flight cancellations.

days.title: Arrive Salalah
activities: Fly Muscat to Salalah. Oman Air and SalamAir both fly it; Salalah airport's live board on 19 October 2026 listed Oman Air WY 903, 904, 907, 909 and 910 and SalamAir OV 101, 102, 105 and 106 between Muscat and Salalah. The airport page and Oman Air's Salalah page do not publish a flight time, so read it off the booking page. Oman Air's Salalah page puts the city about 10 km from the airport and lists taxi, private transfer and rental car options; hire counters are on Level 0.
Al Baleed Archaeological Park and the Museum of the Land of Frankincense: about 5.6 km, roughly 10 min from the airport; check opening hours and ticket on arrival

Before you go: check your government's travel advice. The UK FCDO (updated 22 July 2026) reports regional tensions with strikes and attacks including in Oman, and warns of possible flight cancellations.
days.drive_time: Salalah airport to Al Baleed ~5.6 km, ~10 min

days.title: East Dhofar: Khor Rori and Mirbat
activities: Drive Al Baleed to Khor Rori (Sumhuram), the ancient frankincense port inscribed by UNESCO as part of the Land of Frankincense: about 41 km, roughly 37 min; check the site's opening hours
Drive Khor Rori to Mirbat, a coastal town with old Omani houses: about 34 km, roughly 27 min
Return to Salalah in the afternoon. Mountain roads can be foggy in Khareef: use fog lights, as Oman's met service advises.
days.drive_time: Al Baleed to Khor Rori ~41 km, ~37 min; Khor Rori to Mirbat ~34 km, ~27 min

days.title: Wadi Darbat and the Dhofar mountains
activities: Drive Al Baleed to Wadi Darbat: about 47 km, roughly 48 min. In Khareef the valley is green and water flows; outside the season it is much drier
Keep clear of the water edge and any flowing channels after rain, as wadis flood suddenly (UK FCDO)
Visit Oman notes that Khareef is also the peak frankincense harvesting season; ask at the Al Baleed museum or a local producer about the trees
days.drive_time: Al Baleed to Wadi Darbat ~47 km, ~48 min

days.title: West Dhofar: Mughsail blowholes
activities: Drive Al Baleed to the Mughsail coast: about 47 km, roughly 39 min, for the blowholes and the beach
Stay behind any barriers at the blowholes and do not swim off open beaches in the monsoon sea (cautious general advice, not from an official page)
Roadside stalls sell fresh coconuts in season; carry cash. Dress modestly; swimwear only at tourist beaches or hotel pools (UK FCDO)
days.drive_time: Al Baleed to Mughsail ~47 km, ~39 min

days.title: Fly to Muscat, drive to Sur
activities: Morning flight Salalah to Muscat on Oman Air or SalamAir (see Day 1 for the airport board; book the earliest time you can)
Collect a hire car at Muscat airport and drive towards the east coast: airport to the Wadi Shab area about 176 km, roughly 2 h 27 min; then to Sur about 52 km further, roughly 56 min
Evening in Sur: stroll the waterfront; the town has long been a dhow-building port (check whether the dhow yard is open to visitors)
days.drive_time: Muscat airport to Wadi Shab area ~176 km, ~2 h 27 min; Wadi Shab to Sur ~52 km, ~56 min

days.title: Wadi Shab, Bimmah Sinkhole and Muscat
activities: Drive Sur to Wadi Shab: about 52 km, roughly 56 min; start at first light, because the coast is hot in Khareef-season months (Visit Oman gives a national summer average of about 35 C)

Visit Oman describes Wadi Shab as a hike past several caves, including one with a waterfall. Expect a short boat crossing at the start and swimming sections; wear modest clothing and sturdy sandals, bring water, and do not go in if rain is forecast upstream or in the preceding day (UK FCDO: flash floods; stay away for at least a day after heavy rain)
Bimmah Sinkhole (Hawiyyat Najm Park) is on the coast road towards Muscat: check its current opening hours and any entry rules
Drive on to Muscat, about 2 h 30 min from the Wadi Shab area (airport to Wadi Shab was measured at 2 h 27 min)
days.drive_time: Sur to Wadi Shab ~52 km, ~56 min; Wadi Shab to Muscat ~2 h 30 min

days.title: Muscat: Mutrah and departure
activities: Mutrah Corniche and Mutrah Souq (shop hours vary)

Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque if time allows: I could not reach the mosque's own website, so check its non-Muslim visiting hours and closed days before going. UK FCDO dress guidance: arms and legs covered to below the knee and clothing not tight; women should carry a scarf for the hair (confirm at the gate).
Return the hire car and fly out

food_culture.name: Khareef season in Dhofar
food_culture.description: Each summer the southern monsoon brings mist and drizzle to Dhofar, turning the mountains green. Visit Oman describes it as the summer escape from the heat; Oman Air describes it as running June to September and Oman's met service says the drizzle runs from late June to mid-September. Omanis and Gulf visitors travel to Salalah for it.

food_culture.name: Frankincense (luban) of Dhofar
food_culture.description: Dhofar's Boswellia trees yielded the frankincense that made Khor Rori (Sumhuram) and Al Baleed rich, and the region is UNESCO-listed as the Land of Frankincense. Visit Oman notes Khareef is the peak harvesting season. Resin is sold in souqs and burnt in homes as incense.

food_culture.name: Fresh coconut water in Salalah
food_culture.description: In Khareef coconuts are sold fresh from roadside stalls around Salalah. Prices vary; take small cash. (General knowledge, not an official source.)

food_culture.name: Omani halwa and kahwa
food_culture.description: Sticky halwa with sweet spiced coffee (kahwa) served in small cups is the standard welcome in Omani homes and hotels. (General knowledge, not an official source.)

food_culture.name: Dress and conduct
food_culture.description: Oman is an Islamic country. UK FCDO advises modest dress, with arms and legs covered to below the knee, tourists drinking alcohol only in licensed venues such as hotels, no public displays of affection, and no photography of people without permission.

title: Doha Classic: Museums, Souq + Corniche, Qatar
best_time_description: November to February is Qatar's cool season (Visit Qatar puts it at 15-20 degrees C, with sunny skies), when walking the Corniche, Souq Waqif and Katara in the open air is comfortable. Outside those months it is hot and most of the day is best spent in the museums. Doha Metro, museums and the souq are all air-conditioned or covered, so the route works year-round with outdoor stops moved to the evening.
description: A compact first-timer route through Doha using the Metro: the Msheireb Museums, Souq Waqif, the Museum of Islamic Art on the Corniche, the National Museum of Qatar and Katara Cultural Village. Plan the order around three weekly closing days: Msheireb Museums close Sundays, the National Museum of Qatar closes Tuesdays, the Museum of Islamic Art closes Wednesdays. Hours below are as published by each museum in October 2026.

days.title: Arrive Doha + Souq Waqif
activities: Take the Doha Metro from Hamad International Airport (the Red Line connects Terminal 1 to the city centre) and change at Msheireb, the interchange where the Red, Green and Gold lines meet, for the Gold Line to Souq Waqif. A day pass costs a maximum of QAR 6 (Visit Qatar); tap in and out with a travel card bought from a station vending machine, trains run about every 6 minutes. Metro stops for Friday prayers on Friday mornings, so a Friday-morning arrival needs a taxi (Karwa taxis are the turquoise ones).
