Walk Souq Waqif's alleys at dusk: the Gold Souq, the Falcon Souq (you can hold a falcon under the shopkeeper's supervision), the spice stalls and the Souq Waqif Art Centre, as listed by Visit Qatar

Dinner in the souq: Visit Qatar names karak tea and regag at Shay al Shamoos, makhboos at Al Jasra, fahsa at Bander Aden and kunafa and baklava at Al Aker Sweets. Confirm any venue is open before you go; the souq's cafes stay open late.
days.lodging_suggestion: Doha, near Souq Waqif or Msheireb Downtown (both on the Gold Line)

days.title: Museum of Islamic Art + the Corniche
activities: Museum of Islamic Art (MIA), Corniche. Published hours: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Saturday 9am-7pm; Thursday 9am-9pm; Friday 1:30pm-7pm; closed Wednesday. MIA notes it will also be closed on Sunday 25 October 2026. Tickets can be reserved online on the Qatar Museums site. MIA says its free shuttle buses, taxis or a car reach the museum, and its small car park fills quickly at weekends.
MIA Park, open 24 hours per MIA, and a walk on the Corniche (Visit Qatar describes it as a 7 km stroll)

Evening at Katara Cultural Village: take the Red Line to Katara station. See the Katara Mosque (blue and gold tilework), the Gold Mosque, the amphitheatre and the public beach; Visit Qatar also lists Al Thuraya Planetarium and the Qatar Museums Gallery in Katara. Check each venue's own hours.
days.lodging_suggestion: Doha, near Souq Waqif or Msheireb Downtown

days.title: National Museum of Qatar + Msheireb Museums
activities: National Museum of Qatar (NMoQ), Museum Park Street: take the Gold Line, whose stops include the Qatar National Museum. Published hours: Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Saturday 9am-7pm; Thursday 9am-9pm; Friday 1:30pm-7pm; closed Tuesday. Last entry is 45 minutes before closing, and NMoQ notes some galleries may be closed for enhancement. NMoQ will close at 3pm on Sunday 25 October 2026 (last gallery entry 2.15pm).

Msheireb Museums in Msheireb Downtown Doha: four restored heritage houses (Mohammed Bin Jassim House, Company House, Radwani House, Bin Jelmood House) plus the DNA exhibition. Entry is free. Hours: Monday-Thursday and Saturday 9am-5pm, Friday 3pm-9pm, closed Sunday; last admission 30 minutes before closing. Dress code: cover shoulders to knees, and entry may be refused otherwise. The free Msheireb Tram loops 2 km around the district (Visit Qatar).
Spare evening: a second visit to Souq Waqif, or dinner in Msheireb Downtown
days.lodging_suggestion: Doha, near Souq Waqif or Msheireb Downtown

days.title: Flexible morning + departure
activities: Use this morning for whichever of MIA, NMoQ or the Msheireb Museums fell on a closing day (Wednesday, Tuesday, Sunday respectively), or for MIA Park and the Corniche
Metro back to Hamad International Airport (Red Line to Terminal 1); allow for the Friday-morning Metro shutdown if you fly on a Friday

food_culture.name: Machboos (makhboos)
food_culture.description: The spiced rice-and-meat dish Visit Qatar lists among Souq Waqif's traditional meals, served for example at Al Jasra in the souq.

food_culture.name: Karak tea and regag
food_culture.description: Visit Qatar points to karak tea and regag (thin crepes) at Shay al Shamoos in Souq Waqif; the souq's roadside cafes also serve Arabic coffee and fresh juices late into the night.

food_culture.name: Fahsa
food_culture.description: A slow-cooked meat stew in clay pots, eaten sitting on the floor in the traditional style at Bander Aden in Souq Waqif, per Visit Qatar.

food_culture.name: Kunafa and baklava
food_culture.description: Sweet pastries sold at Al Aker Sweets in Souq Waqif, as named by Visit Qatar.

food_culture.name: Falconry
food_culture.description: Falconry is a traditional sport in Qatar and Souq Waqif has a Falcon Souq, with a dedicated falcon hospital, where visitors can see the birds close up.

food_culture.name: Dress and conduct
food_culture.description: Msheireb Museums ask visitors to dress conservatively, covering shoulders to knees, as a sign of respect for Qatari culture; the same courtesy is sensible at the mosques in Katara.

title: Doha + the Desert Coast: Al Zubarah, Mangroves + the Inland Sea, Qatar
best_time_description: November to February. Visit Qatar gives November to April as the best period for the Inland Sea (not too hot or cool) and November to February for Purple Island; there is no shade or facilities on Purple Island, so summer visits are best avoided. Hold the desert days for the cool season.
description: Doha as a base for three day trips: the UNESCO-listed pearling town of Al Zubarah in the north-west, the Al Thakira mangroves and Purple Island near Al Khor on the north-east coast, and a 4x4 trip to Khor Al Adaid, the Inland Sea, in the south-east. Doha needs a hire car (a 4x4 for the mangroves and Purple Island, per Visit Qatar) or a driver; the Inland Sea can only be reached with a 4x4 and an experienced off-road driver, so most visitors book a tour.

days.title: Arrive Doha + Souq Waqif
activities: Doha Metro from Hamad International Airport (Red Line, Terminal 1) to Msheireb, then the Gold Line to Souq Waqif; a day pass costs a maximum of QAR 6 and trains run about every 6 minutes (Visit Qatar). The Metro stops on Friday mornings for prayers.
Evening in Souq Waqif: the Falcon Souq, spices and the cafes that stay open late. Pick up supplies and arrange a hire car or a driver for the next three days.
days.lodging_suggestion: Doha, near Souq Waqif or Msheireb Downtown

days.title: Al Zubarah Archaeological Site
activities: Al Zubarah, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2013, is about 100 km north-west of Doha (Qatar Museums). Check the drive on a live map before you set off. The site stretches 2.5 km from the fort to the coast and covers houses, mosques, date presses and a market from an 18th-19th century pearling and trading town that was burned in 1811.

Open Saturday to Thursday 9am-5pm and Friday 12:30-5pm; entry is ticketed (book on the Qatar Museums site). A boardwalk and a shuttle between the fort and the town help you get around; the service centre by the fort has restrooms.
Return to Doha for the evening
days.drive_time: About 100 km north-west of Doha each way (Qatar Museums); no official drive time found, check a live map

days.title: Al Thakira Mangroves + Purple Island (Al Khor)
activities: Al Thakira Mangroves, Al Khor: one of Qatar's oldest and largest mangrove forests, about 40 minutes from Doha according to Visit Qatar, which says it is reached by car but in an off-road vehicle. Guided kayak or stand-up paddleboard tours run on the waterways; bird-watching (herons, flamingos) and low tide over the mangrove roots are the draws.

Purple Island (Bin Ghannam Island), near Al Khor, an hour's drive from Doha per Visit Qatar: a wooden bridge, mangroves, kayaking and walking. Visit Qatar warns there are no facilities and no shade on the island, so bring water, a hat and sturdy footwear, and take your rubbish with you. Camping is allowed.
No source gives the drive between the two sites; both are near Al Khor, so confirm the transfer on a live map and book kayak tours ahead.
Return to Doha
days.drive_time: Al Thakira about 40 min from Doha; Purple Island about 1 hr from Doha (Visit Qatar)

days.title: Khor Al Adaid, the Inland Sea
activities: Khor Al Adaid (the Inland Sea): a nature reserve declared in 2007 on a tentative UNESCO list, about 80 km south of Doha (Visit Qatar says just under 80 km, with an hour's drive from Mesaieed or Sealine Beach). There is no road and a 4x4 with an experienced off-road driver is a must, with tyres deflated to 18-20 psi from Mesaieed. Entry is free.

Book a desert safari or daily Inland Sea tour; options include dune bashing, sandboarding, a swim (Visit Qatar says the water is calm and warm and it is safe to swim), camel rides and watching for Arabian oryx, flamingos and turtles.
Visit Qatar's best season for the Inland Sea is November to April.
days.drive_time: Just under 80 km south of Doha; about 1 hr off-road from Mesaieed/Sealine Beach (Visit Qatar)
days.lodging_suggestion: Doha (or an overnight at Sealine Beach, the Regency Sealine Camp or the Outpost Al Barari, the three stays named by Visit Qatar)

days.title: Museum of Islamic Art + departure
activities: Museum of Islamic Art, Corniche: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Saturday 9am-7pm; Thursday 9am-9pm; Friday 1:30pm-7pm; closed Wednesday. MIA notes it is also closed on Sunday 25 October 2026. MIA Park is open 24 hours.
Metro or taxi to Hamad International Airport (Red Line to Terminal 1). Metro does not run on Friday mornings.

food_culture.name: Fahsa
food_culture.description: A slow-cooked meat stew in clay pots eaten sitting on the floor at Bander Aden in Souq Waqif, as described by Visit Qatar.

food_culture.name: Karak tea
food_culture.description: Spiced milky tea served with regag crepes at Shay al Shamoos in Souq Waqif, per Visit Qatar; a good flask-filler before the desert days.

food_culture.name: Pearling
food_culture.description: Al Zubarah was a pearl-fishing and trading town, and Qatar Museums describe it as the last city to rely on pearl diving in the eighteenth century; at Souq Waqif a former pearl diver runs a pearl shop where you can ask about the trade.

food_culture.name: Arabian oryx and desert wildlife
food_culture.description: The Arabian oryx is among the wildlife Visit Qatar lists around Khor Al Adaid, with dugongs, turtles, flamingos, the Arabian gazelle (rheem) and the desert fox.

food_culture.name: UNESCO heritage
food_culture.description: Al Zubarah has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2013 and the Inland Sea is on UNESCO's tentative list; Qatar Museums runs ticketed access at Al Zubarah.

title: Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, the Dead Sea + Masada, Israel
best_time_description: March to May and October to November are the comfortable windows: Masada's Snake Path is restricted in hot weather (INPA sets last ascent from about 7-10 AM depending on the forecast), and the Dead Sea desert wadis can flash-flood in winter, spring and autumn rains. Check the Israel Meteorological Service before a Masada or Ein Gedi day. Built for a Sunday arrival so Shabbat falls in Jerusalem (days 6-7).
description: A classic first trip in 8 days: the beaches, Bauhaus streets and Old Jaffa of Tel Aviv, a 36-43 minute fast train up to Jerusalem's Old City and Yad Vashem, a Dead Sea day with Masada and Ein Gedi, and Shabbat in Jerusalem. Every place is outside the areas the UK FCDO advises against all travel to, but both the FCDO and Global Affairs Canada warn about regional tension, so read the safety notes on day 1.

days.title: Arrive Tel Aviv, Old Jaffa
activities: Arrive at Ben Gurion Airport. Israel Railways runs from the airport to Tel Aviv Savidor-Center in about 18 minutes, every 30 minutes (rail guide dated 10 June 2026; rail.co.il blocked automated access, so confirm the live timetable). Airport trains do not run Friday night or Saturday; taxis do.

Safety and closures: Advisories read 2026-10-19: the UK FCDO (updated 22 July 2026) advises against all travel to Gaza, within 500m of the Gaza border, Tulkarm/Jenin/Tubas governorates of the West Bank, and northern Israel and the Golan north of Route 89 (Nahariyya-Dalton), north of the Dalton-Route 91 line and north of Route 91, plus 500m of the Golan 'Alpha line'; it advises against all but essential travel to the rest of the West Bank (excluding East Jerusalem, Bethlehem Governorate, Ramallah Municipality, and Jericho municipality and areas south of it including the Allenby crossing; Highway 1, Highway 3, Route 443 and Highway 45 are carved out). Global Affairs Canada (updated 29 July 2026) says avoid non-essential travel to Israel (Jerusalem included) and avoid all travel to Palestine, the Golan east of Highway 98, within 5 km of the Lebanon border and within 10 km of the Gaza border. Airspace closures, flight cancellations and rocket/missile alerts can happen at short notice; GAC advises installing an alert app such as Home Front Command and knowing your nearest shelter, and the FCDO warns travel insurance may be invalid if you travel against its advice.
Entry: you need an approved ETA-IL before you fly (applied for on israel-entry.piba.gov.il; passport valid at least three months from arrival).
Evening walk through Old Jaffa and its port, then the Tel Aviv beachfront promenade at sunset.
days.lodging_suggestion: Tel Aviv, near the beach or Neve Tzedek

days.title: Tel Aviv: White City, markets, beach
activities: Walk Rothschild Boulevard and the Bauhaus-style streets of the White City, a UNESCO World Heritage site
Carmel Market and the Neve Tzedek neighbourhood; many market stalls and cafes close early on Friday and on Shabbat, so do this on a weekday
Afternoon at a city beach or the Tel Aviv Museum of Art (check its current opening days on its website)
Dinner in Jaffa or Sarona Market

days.title: Train to Jerusalem, Mahane Yehuda
activities: Israel Railways fast line from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem Yitzhak Navon: 43 minutes from Tel Aviv Center-Savidor or 36 minutes from HaHagana, every 30 minutes Sunday-Thursday (rail guide dated 10 June 2026). No tickets need booking; buy at the station machines.
Check in, then walk the Mahane Yehuda market (its stalls wind down on Friday afternoon before Shabbat)
Late afternoon at the Western Wall plaza and the Jewish Quarter; the plaza is a place of worship, so dress modestly
days.lodging_suggestion: Jerusalem, near the Old City or Mahane Yehuda

days.title: Day trip: Dead Sea, Ein Gedi and Masada
activities: Egged bus 486 runs from Jerusalem Central Bus Station to the Dead Sea, Ein Gedi and Masada: about 1 hour to the public Dead Sea beach and about 1 hour 30 minutes to Ein Gedi per a Jerusalem tourism page (check live times on egged.co.il or Moovit; no buses from Friday afternoon to Saturday evening). A guided or private day tour is the alternative.

Masada National Park (UNESCO): reserve ahead on the Nature and Parks Authority site, which says booking guarantees entry at your time slot. INPA lists winter hours of 08:00 to 16:00 (Friday 08:00 to 15:00; summer closing 17:00, Friday 16:00); the park entrance and the last cable car close one hour before. The Snake Path opens about an hour before sunrise and closes for ascent two hours before closing; the climb takes about an hour and is rated high difficulty. Tanners' Tower is temporarily closed.

Ein Gedi Nature Reserve (Nature and Parks Authority): book the streams in advance and check the INPA site for which trails are open; the Dead Sea wadis flood in winter, spring and autumn rains, so do not enter wadi beds when flooding looks likely.
Float at a public Dead Sea beach such as Ein Bokek before heading back; confirm the last bus back to Jerusalem before you go

Road safety: FCDO excludes Jericho municipality and the areas south of it (the Dead Sea road) from its West Bank warning, and GAC treats Highway 1 and Route 90 as avoid-non-essential rather than avoid-all-travel; both still warn against travel in the wider West Bank, so do not detour off the main road.
days.lodging_suggestion: Jerusalem (or an overnight at Ein Bokek to catch Masada at sunrise)

days.title: Jerusalem Old City
activities: Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif: non-Muslim visits are controlled by Israeli police through the Mughrabi Gate and have reportedly been allowed only on Sunday-Thursday in set morning and early-afternoon windows, and the compound can close at short notice; confirm before you plan around it (the sources found are dated, no current official schedule was found). Visitors cannot enter the buildings.
Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Via Dolorosa in the Christian and Muslim Quarters
Jaffa Gate to the Tower of David, then a walk on the Old City ramparts
East Jerusalem is excluded from the FCDO's West Bank warning; GAC still advises avoiding non-essential travel to Jerusalem, so stay aware of local alerts

days.title: Yad Vashem and Mount Herzl (Friday)
activities: Yad Vashem, the Holocaust memorial museum on Mount Herzl: reservations are required, it is closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays, and it closes earlier on Fridays and holiday eves. Its own pages quote different hours (one gives 09:00-14:00 on Fridays), so check its opening-hours page; its reservation notice lists closures including 27 October 2026 (Election Day) and 2 October 2026 (Simchat Torah eve).
Back in the centre before Shabbat starts at sunset: shops, markets and cafes shut from Friday afternoon, and most intercity transport stops
Friday evening: walk to the Western Wall to see Shabbat welcomed (modest dress)

days.title: Shabbat in Jerusalem
activities: Shabbat: Israel Railways and Egged intercity buses largely stop from Friday afternoon until after dark on Saturday (rail guide dated 10 June 2026: Tel Aviv-Jerusalem fast trains hourly on Fridays until about 14:30, Tel Aviv-Haifa-Akko hourly until about 13:00, nothing on Saturday until after dark; airport trains do not run Friday night or Saturday). Taxis and some city buses (for example in Haifa) still run. Plan a slow day on foot: the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Western Wall plaza remain open to visitors; Yad Vashem and most museums are closed on Saturday.
Walk the Jerusalem neighbourhoods and the Old City souk (many Jewish-quarter shops are closed; much of the Muslim Quarter trades on)
After dark on Saturday, trains and buses restart

days.title: Train to Ben Gurion Airport, depart
activities: Israel Railways Jerusalem Yitzhak Navon to Ben Gurion Airport: about 26 minutes, every 30 minutes (rail guide dated 10 June 2026). Allow extra time; Ben Gurion security checks are thorough and flights can be disrupted, so check your airline before leaving.
If your flight leaves on Friday night or Saturday, use a taxi, not the train

food_culture.name: Hummus and the Israeli breakfast
food_culture.description: Hummus served warm with tahini, and the Israeli breakfast spread of salads, eggs, cheeses and bread, are everyday meals in both Tel Aviv and Jerusalem; many hummus places are counter-service and open only until the afternoon.

food_culture.name: Shakshuka
food_culture.description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, served in the pan with bread; a North African-rooted staple of Israeli cafe menus.

food_culture.name: Sabich
food_culture.description: A Tel Aviv street-food pita filled with fried aubergine, egg, salad, tahini and amba (pickled mango sauce), of Iraqi-Jewish origin.

food_culture.name: Arabic coffee and mint tea
food_culture.description: Small cups of cardamom-scented coffee and sweet mint tea are the usual welcome in the Old City's Muslim and Christian Quarters and the Jaffa old town.

food_culture.name: Shabbat
food_culture.description: From Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall most of Jewish Israel rests: shops close, intercity trains and buses stop, and families gather for the Friday night meal with challah and wine. Jerusalem is far quieter than Tel Aviv on Shabbat.

food_culture.name: The four quarters of the Old City
food_culture.description: Jerusalem's Old City is divided into Jewish, Christian, Muslim and Armenian quarters; each has its own holy sites, markets and rhythm, and dress and behaviour expectations are modest everywhere.

title: Haifa, Acre, Nazareth + the Sea of Galilee, Israel
best_time_description: March to May and October to November: mild for walking Haifa's terraces and Acre's walls, and before the Galilee summer heat. Winter can be wet and cool; Acre's Old City has changed hours around the Akko Festival and Sukkot, so check its site if you travel then. Built for a Sunday arrival, ending on a Friday morning before Shabbat transport stops.
description: A 6-day northern loop by train, bus and short transfers: Haifa's Baha'i Gardens, the crusader and Ottoman port of Acre, Nazareth, then Tiberias and the Sea of Galilee with the Roman city of Beit She'an. It stays south of the line the UK FCDO draws along Route 89 and Route 91 (it does not go to Rosh Hanikra, the Lebanon border strip, the Golan or Metula), so check the safety notes on day 1.

days.title: Arrive, train to Haifa
activities: Arrive at Ben Gurion Airport, train to Tel Aviv Savidor-Center in about 18 minutes, then Tel Aviv-Haifa: 50-60 minutes, twice an hour, some trains continuing to Akko and Nahariya (rail guide dated 10 June 2026; rail.co.il blocked automated access, so confirm the live timetable). Do not ride on to Nahariya: it is at the edge of the zone the FCDO advises against all travel to. On Fridays these trains run hourly only until about 13:00.

Safety and closures: Advisories read 2026-10-19: the UK FCDO (updated 22 July 2026) advises against all travel to Gaza, within 500m of the Gaza border, Tulkarm/Jenin/Tubas governorates of the West Bank, and northern Israel and the Golan north of Route 89 (Nahariyya-Dalton), north of the Dalton-Route 91 line and north of Route 91, plus 500m of the Golan 'Alpha line'; it advises against all but essential travel to the rest of the West Bank (excluding East Jerusalem, Bethlehem Governorate, Ramallah Municipality, and Jericho municipality and areas south of it including the Allenby crossing; Highway 1, Highway 3, Route 443 and Highway 45 are carved out). Global Affairs Canada (updated 29 July 2026) says avoid non-essential travel to Israel (Jerusalem included) and avoid all travel to Palestine, the Golan east of Highway 98, within 5 km of the Lebanon border and within 10 km of the Gaza border. Airspace closures, flight cancellations and rocket/missile alerts can happen at short notice; GAC advises installing an alert app such as Home Front Command and knowing your nearest shelter, and the FCDO warns travel insurance may be invalid if you travel against its advice.
Entry: an approved ETA-IL is needed before you fly (passport valid three months from arrival).
Evening on Hadar or the German Colony's Ben-Gurion Avenue in Haifa

days.title: Haifa: Baha'i Gardens and the Carmel
activities: Baha'i Gardens (Terraces): the outer gardens are open 09:00-17:00 daily and the Shrine of the Bab and inner gardens 09:00-12:00 (the Baha'i site's own page, read 2026-10-19). Guided tours are by reservation only. The site lists closure days, for example Monday 5 October 2026; check its page for the days when you go. Dress modestly.
Viewpoints at 61 Yefe Nof (upper terraces) and 21 Hagefen (German Colony plaza), both viewing-only per the same page
Afternoon: Wadi Nisnas arts quarter and market; Haifa's city buses run on Shabbat, unlike most Israeli cities, which is why Haifa is a good place to spend one

days.title: Acre (Akko) Old City
activities: Train Haifa to Akko; the station is outside the Old City, and a JNF-USA Western Galilee information page gives bus 3A (about 10 minutes, about 5 NIS with a Rav-Kav card) or a taxi (about 10 minutes, about 20 NIS) into the Old City. A bus Haifa-Akko takes about 40 minutes (lines 251, 271, 272, 361).

Old Akko sites (Knights Halls, Templars Tunnel, Turkish Bath, Visitors Center, Okashi Art Museum): 09:00-17:00 Sunday-Thursday and Saturday, 09:00-16:00 Friday and holiday eves; the ticket office closes 60 minutes before closing, winter hours from 25 October 2026 are the same (akko.org.il). An All-Inclusive ticket is listed at 55 NIS. The Templars Tunnel elevator is out of service. The Ramchal Synagogue is closed Saturdays and holidays. The site warns of changes during the Akko Festival and Sukkot.
Walk the sea walls and the harbour, and the Turkish souk, then eat seafood at the port
Return to Haifa by train, or continue towards Nazareth by bus (no journey time verified; check Moovit and leave early)

days.title: Nazareth and on to Tiberias
activities: Nazareth: the Basilica of the Annunciation and the Old City market; check Mass times and dress modestly
Onward to Tiberias by bus (no verified journey time; use Moovit or egged.co.il to pick the connection)
Evening on the Tiberias promenade beside the Sea of Galilee

days.title: Sea of Galilee and Beit She'an
activities: Morning on the north-west shore: Mount of Beatitudes, Tabgha and Capernaum (a Franciscan site with the ancient synagogue ruins); these lie south of the FCDO's Route 89/Dalton boundary, but stay off the roads north of it

Beit She'an National Park (Roman-Byzantine Scythopolis) in the Jordan Valley, inside Israel and not named in either advisory; check the Nature and Parks Authority site for hours and closures, and check live alerts before taking Route 90
Return to Tiberias

days.title: Depart before Friday afternoon
activities: Friday is the day to leave: intercity buses and trains wind down from Friday afternoon and stop until after dark on Saturday, so catch a morning bus from Tiberias towards Tel Aviv or Haifa and the airport (confirm the last Friday departure on egged.co.il or Moovit; no journey time was verified)
If you would rather stay for Shabbat, expect a quiet Tiberias with most shops shut and no intercity buses; choose Haifa instead, where city buses still run
From Tel Aviv, the airport train takes about 18 minutes from Savidor-Center and does not run Friday night or Saturday

food_culture.name: Hummus, falafel and fresh pita
food_culture.description: In Haifa's Wadi Nisnas and Acre's souk, hummus and falafel counters serve generous plates with pickles, salad and tahini; many close by mid-afternoon.

food_culture.name: Sea bream and mezze at the Acre harbour
food_culture.description: Acre's fishermen's harbour restaurants serve grilled fish with small salads, a traditional coastal meal in the Old City.

food_culture.name: St Peter's fish
food_culture.description: Whole tilapia, grilled or fried, is the lakeside meal on the Tiberias waterfront, named after the Galilee fishing trade of the Gospels.

food_culture.name: Arak and local wine
food_culture.description: Anise-flavoured arak with mezze, and Galilee wines, are common with a long meal in Arab towns and in Haifa.

food_culture.name: Shabbat in a mixed city
food_culture.description: Haifa has a large Arab and Jewish population and is unusual among Israeli cities because city buses run on Shabbat, while Tiberias goes quiet and Acre's Arab quarters stay open.

food_culture.name: Baha'i Gardens and Acre's mixed old city
food_culture.description: The Terraces of the Baha'i Faith on Mount Carmel surround the Shrine of the Bab, and Acre's Old City layers crusader halls, an Ottoman mosque and fishermen's quarters in one walled town.

title: Helsinki, Porvoo, Tampere + Turku, Finland
best_time_description: June to August gives the longest days, the Porvoo-Helsinki summer boat (it runs in summer, almost daily per Visit Porvoo) and lake and sea-sauna weather; May and September are quieter and cooler. Winter is cold and dark, and this route is built around outdoor walking, ferries and lake views, so it is a summer-shoulder trip. Check opening hours of each museum before you go.
description: Finland's southern arc by train and bus: Helsinki's harbour, sea fortress and market hall, a day trip to the wooden old town of Porvoo, then west to Tampere between its two lakes and on to medieval Turku on the Aura River. No domestic flights, every leg 1.5 to 2 hours or less.

days.title: Arrive Helsinki
activities: Airport train (HSL lines I or P) from Helsinki Airport station to Helsinki Central: about 30 minutes (HSL gives about 27 minutes for the I train and about 32 for the P train); an ABC ticket is needed
Walk Senate Square and Helsinki Cathedral, then the South Harbour and Market Square
Dinner near the harbour; try salmon soup (lohikeitto)

days.title: Helsinki: sea fortress and sauna
activities: HSL ferry from the eastern side of Market Square to the Suomenlinna sea fortress: about 15 minutes each way, covered by an AB ticket (the Suomenlinna site says ferries run daily, first departure from Market Square about 6:00)
Explore Suomenlinna's bastions, tunnels and museums (check Suomenlinna's own site for museum opening times)
Afternoon at the Old Market Hall by Market Square for Karelian pies and Finnish cheese
Evening sauna by the sea: choose a public sauna and book ahead where required (check the sauna's own booking page)

days.title: Day trip to Porvoo
activities: Bus from Helsinki Kamppi bus station to Porvoo: about 50 minutes by motorway per Visit Porvoo (other Finnish tourism pages say just over an hour); operators include Matkahuolto and OnniBus
Walk Old Porvoo's cobbled lanes and colourful wooden houses, and the red riverside warehouses
Porvoo Cathedral on the hill above the old town
Coffee and a Runeberg torte, the pastry named after the national poet J. L. Runeberg, who lived in Porvoo

In summer you can instead take the m/s J. L. Runeberg cruise through the archipelago (about 3 hours one way, runs almost daily in summer, leaving Helsinki in the morning and Porvoo in the afternoon per Visit Porvoo; check msjlruneberg.fi for dates)
Bus back to Helsinki (return bus less than an hour per Visit Porvoo)

days.title: Train to Tampere
activities: VR train from Helsinki Central to Tampere: about 1.5 hours at the fastest (VR); book ahead for peak times
Tampere Market Hall: try mustamakkara, the local black sausage, with lingonberry jam
Walk between Lake Näsijärvi and Lake Pyhäjärvi and along the Tammerkoski rapids through the old Finlayson factory area
Evening sauna: Tampere is known for its saunas (check opening times and booking of the one you choose)
days.lodging_suggestion: Central Tampere near the railway station

days.title: Tampere: ridge, lakes and Moomins
activities: Pyynikki Ridge and its observation tower, then doughnuts at the tower-side cafe (check seasonal opening hours)
Moomin Museum in Tampere Hall (check opening days; timed tickets may apply)
Vapriikki museum centre by the rapids
Lake cruise from Laukontori harbour in summer (check the operator's timetable; services are seasonal)
days.lodging_suggestion: Central Tampere near the railway station

days.title: Train to Turku
activities: VR train from Tampere to Turku: about 1 hour 40 minutes at the fastest; VR says seven direct trains run on weekdays, so check the timetable and book ahead
Turku Castle, a medieval castle on the sea (check opening days; closed or limited outside the main season)
Turku Cathedral, Finland's mother church, and the Aura River banks
Dinner on the river: Turku has restaurant boats and riverside terraces, most open in summer
days.lodging_suggestion: Central Turku by the Aura River

days.title: Turku market hall + departure
activities: Turku Market Hall for archipelago bread (saaristolaisleipä) and local fish
VR train from Turku to Helsinki: about 2 hours at the fastest (VR), then the airport train I or P to Helsinki Airport in about 30 minutes
Leave a buffer of at least 3 hours before an international flight

food_culture.name: Karelian pies (karjalanpiirakka)
food_culture.description: Thin rye-crust pies filled with rice porridge, traditionally served with egg butter (munavoi). Sold at Helsinki's Old Market Hall and in most Finnish bakeries and cafes.

food_culture.name: Salmon soup (lohikeitto)
food_culture.description: A creamy salmon and potato soup, a staple lunch in Helsinki market halls and harbour-side cafes.

food_culture.name: Runeberg torte (Runebergin torttu)
food_culture.description: A small almond and rum-flavoured cake topped with raspberry jam, named after the national poet J. L. Runeberg; Porvoo, where he lived, is the place to try it, usually in February around his birthday but sold in Porvoo cafes much of the year.

food_culture.name: Mustamakkara
food_culture.description: Tampere's black sausage, a blood sausage eaten hot at Tampere Market Hall with lingonberry jam.

food_culture.name: Archipelago bread (saaristolaisleipä)
food_culture.description: A dark, sweet rye bread from the Turku archipelago, sold at Turku Market Hall.

food_culture.name: Sauna
food_culture.description: Saunas are part of everyday Finnish life; public saunas in Helsinki, Tampere and Turku welcome visitors. Etiquette: shower first, and ask the sauna's own page whether swimwear is allowed, as rules vary by venue.

food_culture.name: Coffee break (kahvitauko)
food_culture.description: Finland is among the world's heaviest coffee drinkers; a coffee and a cinnamon bun (korvapuusti) at a cafe is a daily ritual, and the doughnut cafe on Pyynikki Ridge in Tampere is a local landmark.

title: Lapland: Rovaniemi, Santa Claus Village + Levi, Finland
best_time_description: Two different trips. Northern lights season in Rovaniemi runs from late August to early April per Visit Rovaniemi, and Levi's official FAQ gives late August to April; winter (December to March) adds snow, with Levi's downhill front slopes open from October to May and cross-country skiing usually October to end of April per Levi. Midnight sun in Rovaniemi runs from early June to early July (Visit Rovaniemi; bright nights from late May into August), and you cannot see the aurora then. Winter is the more expensive and booked-up season: reserve flights, lodging and activities well ahead.
description: Finland's Arctic north: Rovaniemi on the Arctic Circle with Santa Claus Village and the Arktikum museum, then a bus to the Levi fell for skiing and aurora hunting in winter or hiking under the midnight sun in summer, flying home from nearby Kittilä.

days.title: Arrive Rovaniemi
activities: Fly Helsinki to Rovaniemi (Finnair operates several flights a day year-round per Visit Rovaniemi; check Finnair for the flight time), or take the VR Santa Claus Express night train from Helsinki (VR: fastest journey 8 hours 22 minutes; seat or sleeper cabin; book ahead)
From the airport, the Airport Express bus runs via Santa Claus Village (no pre-reservation needed, tickets at airportbus.fi); check current timetable
Settle in; evening walk along the Kemijoki river
days.drive_time: Flight from Helsinki; transfer by Airport Express bus

days.title: Santa Claus Village + the Arctic Circle
activities: Local bus line 8 runs all year between Rovaniemi city centre and Santa Claus Village (about 8 km north of the centre per the Village's site; check the Linkkari journey planner for times)
Cross the Arctic Circle line, which is clearly marked on the ground in the village
Check the Village's own opening hours page for the season before you go; winter and summer hours differ
Evening: aurora watching if you travel between late August and early April (Visit Rovaniemi); it needs a dark, clear sky and is never guaranteed

days.title: Rovaniemi: Arktikum and Ounasvaara
activities: Arktikum museum and science centre on the Ounasjoki river, on Arctic nature and life in the north (check opening days and hours)
Ounasvaara hill on the edge of town: winter skiing and snowshoe trails, summer walking trails and views over the two rivers
Winter only: husky, reindeer or snowmobile excursions with local operators; book in advance
Summer only (early June to early July): walk or cycle through the midnight sun period at any hour

days.title: Bus to Levi
activities: Bus from Rovaniemi to Levi: about 2.5 hours per Matkahuolto (Levi is about 170 km north of Rovaniemi); check departure times and book ahead in winter
Arrive in Levi village, then a first walk or snow-shoe outing on the fell

days.title: Levi fell: ski and aurora, or hike
activities: Winter: downhill skiing on Levi's front slopes (open from October to May per Levi) or cross-country skiing (usually October to end of April)
Summer: hiking on the Levi fell and long bright evenings; the sun does not set in midsummer, so people play golf at night (Levi's FAQ)
Autumn to early spring: guided aurora outing from Levi; Levi says the season starts late August and lasts until April

days.title: Fly home from Kittilä
activities: Kittilä airport is 15 km south of Levi (about a 10-minute drive per Levi's FAQ); the airport bus links Levi and Kittilä airport, usually around flight times (off-season it may need booking ahead)
Finnair flies Helsinki to Kittilä daily year-round per Levi; allow a generous buffer for winter weather

food_culture.name: Sautéed reindeer (poronkäristys)
food_culture.description: Thin-sliced reindeer sautéed with onion and served with mashed potatoes and lingonberries, the classic Lapland main course in Rovaniemi and Levi restaurants.

food_culture.name: Squeaky cheese (leipäjuusto) with cloudberry jam
food_culture.description: A baked fresh cheese served warm with cloudberry (lakka) jam as dessert in northern Finland.

food_culture.name: Campfire coffee
food_culture.description: Coffee boiled over an open fire is served on many winter excursions and at wilderness huts; drink it with a pulla bun if offered.

food_culture.name: Sauna and the ice hole
food_culture.description: Lapland lodgings often include a sauna, and some have a hole cut in the ice or a cold plunge afterwards. Follow the venue's safety rules and never go in alone.

food_culture.name: Arctic Circle crossing at Santa Claus Village
food_culture.description: Rovaniemi lies on the Arctic Circle, which is marked on the ground at Santa Claus Village, one of the places visitors cross the line (Visit Rovaniemi).

title: Ljubljana, Lake Bled + Bohinj, Slovenia
best_time_description: Late spring (May to June) and early autumn (September to early October) are the sweet spot: Vintgar Gorge is open only from April to October (hours shorten from 21 September, 9:00 to 15:00), Ljubljana Castle stays open 365 days a year, and the lakes are quieter than in July and August. The Vogel cable car above Lake Bohinj is scheduled to stay closed until at least 1 December 2026, so for views from Vogel pick a later year or check vogel.si first.
description: Slovenia's greatest hits in five easy days: the riverside old town and hilltop castle of Ljubljana, a night by the island church of Lake Bled with a walk through the 1,600 m Vintgar Gorge, then quieter Lake Bohinj inside Triglav National Park, all linked by trains and buses from the capital.

days.title: Arrive Ljubljana
activities: Walk the old town on both banks of the Ljubljanica River, from Preseren Square across the Triple Bridge to the riverside embankments

Ride the funicular up to Ljubljana Castle: the ride takes about 60 seconds and costs EUR 6.00 return for adults (EUR 3.30 one way). The castle is open 365 days a year, 9:00 to 19:00 from October to April and 9:00 to 22:00 from May to September (funicular 9:00 to 18:00 or 9:00 to 20:00); last tickets are sold one hour before closing (ljubljanskigrad.si)
Dinner in the old town (see food_culture for dishes to try)

days.title: Ljubljana to Lake Bled
activities: Morning in Ljubljana: browse the central market area and the riverside promenades before leaving

Go to Bled by train or bus. By train, take the Ljubljana line to Lesce-Bled station (about an hour on routes I could see; the station is on the Munich-Salzburg-Villach-Ljubljana line and 4 km from the lake; the Bled bus station is directly opposite the railway station, bled.si). The other route is a train to Jesenice then a change to Bled Jezero station, only 1.5 km from the lake. Arriva buses also run Ljubljana to Bled, about 1 hour 20 minutes on route planners. Timetable pages of Slovenske zeleznice (potniski.sz.si) and Arriva could not be opened by automated tools, so confirm departures on the live timetable before you travel.
Walk or cycle the lake shore and, if the weather allows, take a traditional pletna rowing boat to the island church
Climb to Bled Castle for views over the lake; its official site gives winter hours (November to March) of 8:00 to 18:00 and summer hours of 8:00 to 20:00, and advises buying tickets online

days.title: Vintgar Gorge, then Lake Bohinj
activities: Vintgar Gorge is 4 km from Bled and cannot be reached by car: walk or cycle from Bled, take the Vintgar shuttle e-bus from the main bus station in Bled, or park at the free Vintgar Lip lot and take the shuttle to the Visitor Centre. Entry is by digital ticket bought online for your chosen date (vintgar.si)

The gorge is open April to October only; from 21 September to the end of the season it is open 9:00 to 15:00, so start in the morning. The one-way path runs 1,600 m from the Visitor Centre to the Sum Waterfall and a safety helmet is mandatory on that section. The all-in-one pass is listed at EUR 15 for adults, but the same site also shows a lower gorge-only figure, so check the live price list

Afternoon bus from Bled to Lake Bohinj, roughly 40 to 45 minutes on route planners with Arriva as the main operator and few departures out of season, so check the timetable before you plan the day. Timetable pages of Slovenske zeleznice (potniski.sz.si) and Arriva could not be opened by automated tools, so confirm departures on the live timetable before you travel.
Evening by the lake shore at Ribcev Laz, the eastern end of the lake

days.title: Lake Bohinj and Triglav National Park
activities: Walk the lake shore: paths run along both the north and south shores to the lower cable car station at the western end (vogel.si)
Triglav National Park information centre at Bohinj can advise on current trail and waterfall conditions (tnp.si, +386 4 578 02 00)
Savica Waterfall is one of the park's listed landmarks at the head of the valley; ask the Bohinj information centre about access and seasonal conditions before you go

Vogel cable car note: the main cable car is closed for extended maintenance and the operator's page says it is scheduled to stay closed until 1 December 2026, with the exact reopening date still to be announced

days.title: Return to Ljubljana
activities: Bus back towards Ljubljana via Bled (Arriva buses link Ljubljana and Bled in about 1 hour 20 minutes on route planners), or train via Lesce-Bled; leave buffer if you have a flight. Timetable pages of Slovenske zeleznice (potniski.sz.si) and Arriva could not be opened by automated tools, so confirm departures on the live timetable before you travel.
Last walk or coffee along the Ljubljanica before departing

food_culture.name: Kremsnita (Bled cream cake)
food_culture.description: A custard-and-whipped-cream slice under a flaky pastry lid that Lake Bled is known for; eating one lakeside is the town's most traditional treat.

food_culture.name: Kranjska klobasa (Carniolan sausage)
food_culture.description: A pork sausage from Slovenia's Upper Carniola region, usually served with sauerkraut or turnips and mustard; widely sold from Ljubljana's market stalls to mountain-hut menus.

food_culture.name: Struklji
food_culture.description: Rolled dough filled with cottage cheese, tarragon or walnuts, boiled or baked; a traditional Slovenian dish found on menus around Bohinj and across the country.

food_culture.name: Potica
food_culture.description: A rolled yeast-dough cake with a swirled walnut or other filling, baked for holidays and family gatherings throughout Slovenia.

food_culture.name: Slovenian wine and local fruit brandy
food_culture.description: Slovenia has three wine regions and a strong home-distilling tradition; restaurants in Ljubljana's old town typically list Slovenian wines alongside fruit brandies.

food_culture.name: Plecnik's Ljubljana
food_culture.description: The architect Joze Plecnik shaped much of central Ljubljana, including the Triple Bridge and the riverside market colonnade; the old-town walk follows his work.

food_culture.name: Pletna boats of Lake Bled
food_culture.description: Flat-bottomed wooden rowing boats propelled by a standing oarsman carry visitors to the church on Bled Island, a tradition of the lake.

title: Postojna + Skocjan Caves, Piran + Soca Valley, Slovenia
best_time_description: May, June and September are best: Skocjan Caves run their longest route and the most departures from April to September, and the Soca Valley is at its most accessible. In October to April the Skocjan tour ends at the Big Collapse Doline exit (about 3 km instead of 5 km). Skocjan Caves are about 12 C inside, so bring a jacket even in summer. Several sites are seasonal (Tolmin Gorges, the cave under Predjama Castle only June to August).
description: Underground and along the sea and river: Postojna Cave and Predjama Castle, the UNESCO Skocjan Caves, the old Adriatic port of Piran with the Secovlje salt pans, then north to the emerald Soca Valley around Kobarid and Bovec. Transit between the coast and the Soca is long, so this works best with a rental car.

days.title: Ljubljana to Postojna Cave and Predjama Castle
activities: Travel from Ljubljana to Postojna by Slovenske zeleznice train or by bus (Nomago and Arriva serve Postojna). Timetable pages of Slovenske zeleznice (potniski.sz.si) and Arriva could not be opened by automated tools, so confirm departures on the live timetable before you travel.

Postojna Cave: you must choose an exact date and time when buying; tickets are sold only on the official website postojnska-jama.eu. The page lists adults at EUR 34.90 for the cave alone. Arrive 30 minutes before your tour; boarding of the cave train is 15 minutes before the tour time. The park says it is open every day, including holidays.

Predjama Castle, built into a cave mouth a few kilometres from Postojna: single ticket EUR 24.00 (combined Postojna Cave + Predjama listed at EUR 55.00); an app-guided tour is included and audio guides rent for EUR 2.90. A shuttle runs in high season (up to 20 minutes). The cave under the castle is open only June to August because of hibernating bats

days.title: Skocjan Caves
activities: Skocjan Caves (UNESCO) are reached from Divaca; the park's reception can advise on transfers and a summer hop-on shuttle that ran on a trial basis, so call +386 5 7082 110 before relying on it

Tickets are sold online at park-skocjanske-jame.mojekarte.si; the park warns tours sell out on some days in summer and recommends buying in advance. Departures per day vary by month, from 2 per day in January, February, November and December to 8 in July and August, so check the live timetable

Full route is about 5 km and 2.5 to 3 hours with roughly 1,000 steps; from January to April and October to December the tour ends early at the Big Collapse Doline exit (about 3 km, 500 to 800 steps). Adult prices: EUR 16 (November to March), EUR 18 (April and October), EUR 22 (May, June, September), EUR 24 (July and August). Cave temperature 12 C, no photography, closed 1 January and 25 December

Continue to the coast by bus (Nomago connects Koper with Postojna and Nova Gorica; Arriva continues Koper to Portoroz and Piran, arriva.si). Timetable pages of Slovenske zeleznice (potniski.sz.si) and Arriva could not be opened by automated tools, so confirm departures on the live timetable before you travel.

days.title: Piran and the Secovlje Salina
activities: Walk Piran's old town: Tartini Square, the Church of St George above the harbour and the town walls

Secovlje Salina Nature Park (kpss.si): a protected area of historic salt pans with a Saltworks Museum; visit on foot or by bicycle, or join a guided tour. The park announces free admission on the first Sunday of every month from October 2026, and works in the Lera area were planned from 15 September 2026, so confirm hours and access on the park's site or by calling +386 5 6721 350
Evening on the Piran waterfront

days.title: Coast to the Soca Valley
activities: This is a transit day. Take an Arriva bus from Piran to Koper (about 40 to 47 minutes on route planners), then a Nomago bus from Koper to Nova Gorica (arriva.si/en/with-the-bus-to-the-sea names Nomago as serving Koper from Nova Gorica), then a regional bus up the valley towards Tolmin and Kobarid. I could not find a verified through service with times, so check the Nomago timetable and allow most of the day, or hire a car in Koper or Nova Gorica

Kobarid Museum (kobariski-muzej.si): open every day all year, 10:00 to 17:00 from October to December, 9:00 to 18:00 April to June and in September, 9:00 to 19:00 July and August, 10:00 to 17:00 January to March; permanent exhibition, the Kobarid Historical Trail and the Italian Charnel House

days.title: Kobarid and Tolmin Gorges
activities: Kozjak waterfall: a 15 m waterfall in the gorge of the Kozjak stream near Kobarid, reached by a short walk (soca-valley.com)

Tolmin Gorges: the lowest entry point of Triglav National Park. It is a seasonal site with timed online ticketing and the opening dates vary by source, so check soca-valley.com or the gorge's ticket page for your date before planning around it
Evening in Kobarid

days.title: Bovec and Trenta
activities: Bovec tourist information is at Rupa 17, 5230 Bovec and can advise on river activities and the season
Dom Trenta is one of the three Triglav National Park visitor centres (with Bled and Bohinj) and the best place to ask about trail and road conditions in the upper Soca valley (tnp.si)
Walk the Soca riverbank near Bovec

days.title: Return to Ljubljana
activities: Allow a full day to return from the Soca Valley to Ljubljana: I could not verify a direct public-transport timetable, so check Nomago and Slovenske zeleznice (via Nova Gorica or Bled) or return a rental car. Timetable pages of Slovenske zeleznice (potniski.sz.si) and Arriva could not be opened by automated tools, so confirm departures on the live timetable before you travel.

food_culture.name: Kraski prsut (Karst prosciutto)
food_culture.description: Air-dried ham from the Karst plateau, cured partly by the dry bora wind and sliced thin; a staple of tasting plates around Postojna and Skocjan.

food_culture.name: Teran wine
food_culture.description: A deep red wine from the Karst region, traditionally made from the Refosco grape on the area's red soil and served with Karst ham.

food_culture.name: Soska postrv (marble trout) from the Soca
food_culture.description: The marbled-pattern trout native to the Soca River basin; restaurants in Kobarid and Bovec serve it grilled or pan-fried.

food_culture.name: Frika
food_culture.description: A Soca Valley dish of potato and local cheese fried together into a crisp-edged cake, long associated with the Tolmin area.

food_culture.name: Adriatic fish and shellfish in Piran
food_culture.description: Piran's waterfront restaurants serve grilled sea bream, sea bass, squid and mussels from the northern Adriatic.

food_culture.name: Traditional salt-making at Secovlje
food_culture.description: Hand harvesting of sea salt in the Secovlje salt pans, a centuries-old craft on the Slovenian coast that the nature park's Saltworks Museum documents.

food_culture.name: Karst cave heritage
food_culture.description: Postojna Cave and the Skocjan Caves are two of Slovenia's best-known natural sites; Skocjan is a UNESCO World Heritage cave system, and the surrounding Karst plateau gave the world the term 'karst'.

food_culture.name: Isonzo Front memory in Kobarid
food_culture.description: Kobarid's museum and historical trail preserve the story of the Soca Valley's First World War battlefields and the Italian Charnel House on the hill above town.

title: Bucharest, Peles, Brasov, Bran + Sighisoara, Romania
best_time_description: Late spring and early autumn suit this route: Bran Castle runs its longer 9:00-19:00 schedule from 1 April to 1 November (shorter 9:00-18:00 days from 2 November), and Peles Castle's visiting schedule shows it closed Mondays and Tuesdays. In 2026 Peles is also closed 2 November to 1 December for conservation, and Pelisor until 3 November, so late autumn trips need to be checked against peles.ro. Season advice here is editorial, not a sourced climate figure.
description: Romania's classic first-timer circuit: Bucharest's grand boulevards and old town, a train up the Prahova Valley to Peles Castle in Sinaia, medieval Brasov, Bran Castle, then the walled citadel of Sighisoara in Transylvania, finishing with a train back to Bucharest.

days.title: Arrive Bucharest
activities: Arrive at Bucharest Henri Coanda Airport; CFR Calatori runs trains between Aeroport Henri Coanda and Bucuresti Nord (the CFR timetable site lists the route), or take a taxi. Check live train times on CFR Calatori's timetable (mersultrenurilor.infofer.ro or bilete.cfrcalatori.ro); the 2025-2026 timetable is valid until 12 December 2026.
Evening walk through the Old Town (Lipscani) for dinner
Note: Peles Castle (Day 3) is closed Mondays and Tuesdays per its visiting schedule, so time your arrival so Day 3 falls on a Wednesday to Sunday
days.lodging_suggestion: Old Town or Calea Victoriei, Bucharest

days.title: Bucharest sights
activities: Walk Calea Victoriei and see the Romanian Athenaeum and Revolution Square

Visit one museum of your choice in the Old Town or at the Palace of the Parliament; tours of the Palace of the Parliament are guided and booked in advance, so check the official visiting page for the current booking rules and hours before going

Buy your Peles Castle ticket online at bilete.peles.ro for tomorrow: tickets are only sold there or at the SelfPay stations near the castles, are valid for one day and time slot only, and cannot be rescheduled or refunded
days.lodging_suggestion: Old Town or Calea Victoriei, Bucharest

days.title: Bucharest to Sinaia: Peles Castle
activities: Train from Bucuresti Nord to Sinaia (Bucuresti Nord - Sinaia is a route on CFR's timetable site, on the line toward Brasov). Check live train times on CFR Calatori's timetable (mersultrenurilor.infofer.ro or bilete.cfrcalatori.ro); the 2025-2026 timetable is valid until 12 December 2026.

Peles Castle: open Wednesday 10:00-17:00 and Thursday-Sunday 09:15-17:00, closed Monday and Tuesday; last entry 16:00; entry in timed slots, first come first served inside your slot; adult ticket 100 lei (ground and first floor); English guided tours run through the day. Closed 2 November to 1 December 2026 for general cleaning and preventive conservation
Pelisor Castle next door (adult ticket 30 lei, same days and hours) is closed 28 September to 3 November 2026
Continue by train to Brasov in the evening (Sinaia - Brasov is on the same line toward Brasov)

days.title: Brasov
activities: Walk Council Square (Piata Sfatului) and the old town
Visit the Black Church and climb Mount Tampa or ride the Tampa cable car; opening hours were not verified for this guide, so check before you go
Rest of the day free for Brasov's old streets and cafes

days.title: Bran Castle day trip from Brasov
activities: Travel from Brasov to Bran by bus or taxi; no timetable was verified for this guide, so check current bus times at the Brasov bus stations

Bran Castle: open 1 April to 1 November Monday 12:00-19:00 and Tuesday-Sunday 9:00-19:00 (these are last-entry times); 2 November to 31 March Monday 12:00-18:00, Tuesday-Sunday 9:00-18:00; adult ticket 100 lei, students with card 60 lei, children 5-17 40 lei (the site also shows promotional 'from 40 RON' standard tickets, so confirm the price at checkout). A guided Royal Tour with Fast Pass runs every hour on the hour and is sold separately
Return to Brasov in the evening

days.title: Brasov to Sighisoara
activities: Train from Brasov to Sighisoara. CFR Calatori's route IR 16021 leaves Bucuresti Nord at 11:20 for Timisoara Nord (arriving 23:12) via Brasov and Sighisoara, in service from 14 March 2026; its published announcement gives only those end-point times, so get the Brasov departure and Sighisoara arrival times from the timetable site. Check live train times on CFR Calatori's timetable (mersultrenurilor.infofer.ro or bilete.cfrcalatori.ro); the 2025-2026 timetable is valid until 12 December 2026.
Walk the UNESCO-listed Sighisoara citadel: Clock Tower, covered scholars' stairs and the Church on the Hill (opening hours not verified, check locally)
Dinner in the citadel or the lower town

days.title: Sighisoara to Bucharest
activities: Morning at the citadel's walls and towers

Train back to Bucharest: CFR Calatori's IR 16023 leaves Timisoara Nord at 09:09 and reaches Bucuresti Nord at 21:11, on the same Sighisoara-Brasov route (announced for service from 15 March 2026); the Sighisoara departure time was not published, so confirm it on the timetable site. Check live train times on CFR Calatori's timetable (mersultrenurilor.infofer.ro or bilete.cfrcalatori.ro); the 2025-2026 timetable is valid until 12 December 2026.
Overnight in Bucharest before your flight

food_culture.name: Sarmale
food_culture.description: Cabbage rolls stuffed with minced pork and rice, simmered for hours and served with mamaliga and sour cream. A staple of Romanian home cooking and festive tables.

food_culture.name: Mamaliga cu branza si smantana
food_culture.description: Cornmeal porridge served with salty cheese and sour cream, a traditional Romanian staple found on restaurant menus across Transylvania and the south.

food_culture.name: Mici (mititei)
food_culture.description: Grilled skinless sausages of minced meat and spices, eaten with mustard and bread, a classic of Bucharest beer gardens and market stalls.

food_culture.name: Papanasi
food_culture.description: Fried or boiled cheese doughnuts topped with sour cream and sour cherry jam, a common dessert in Brasov and Sighisoara restaurants.

food_culture.name: Tuica and palinca
food_culture.description: Plum brandy (tuica) and double-distilled fruit brandy (palinca) are traditional Romanian spirits, often offered with a meal or as a welcome.

food_culture.name: Martisor
food_culture.description: Every 1 March Romanians give each other a small charm tied to a red-and-white string to welcome spring; the custom is shared with neighbouring countries and is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.

food_culture.name: Transylvanian Saxon heritage
food_culture.description: Brasov and Sighisoara grew as medieval Transylvanian Saxon towns, and their fortified old centres, towers and churches reflect that German-speaking merchant culture; the Historic Centre of Sighisoara is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Cluj-Napoca, Sibiu + the Transfagarasan Road, Romania
best_time_description: Plan this one for summer into early autumn. The Transfagarasan (DN7C) is closed each winter by CNAIR, Romania's national road company, on the section from Piscu Negru (km 104+000) to Balea Cascada (km 130+800); in 2025 it closed on Monday 20 October, and the date moves with the weather, so check cnadnr.ro before booking Day 5. Brukenthal Palace is closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Season advice here is editorial, not a sourced climate figure.
description: A Transylvanian road trip from university-town Cluj-Napoca and the Turda Salt Mine to medieval Sibiu, then a day driving over the high Fagaras mountain pass on the Transfagarasan to the Arges valley, ending in Bucharest.

days.title: Arrive Cluj-Napoca
activities: Fly into Cluj-Napoca (Avram Iancu International Airport) or arrive by train; Check live train times on CFR Calatori's timetable (mersultrenurilor.infofer.ro or bilete.cfrcalatori.ro); the 2025-2026 timetable is valid until 12 December 2026.
Evening walk around Unirii Square and St Michael's Church in the old centre

days.title: Turda Salt Mine
activities: Day trip to the Turda Salt Mine from Cluj-Napoca by car, bus or regional train; no timetable was verified for this guide, so check current times

Turda Salt Mine: open Monday-Sunday 09:00-17:00, last entry 16:20; adult ticket 75 lei Monday-Friday and 90 lei at weekends and public holidays (seniors 50/60 lei, children 3-18 48/59 lei); tickets are sold online at bilete.salinaturda.eu
Return to Cluj-Napoca for the evening

days.title: Cluj-Napoca to Sibiu
activities: Travel from Cluj-Napoca to Sibiu by car, train or bus. Journey times were not verified for this guide; check them on CFR Calatori's timetable site or your rental-car route planner. Check live train times on CFR Calatori's timetable (mersultrenurilor.infofer.ro or bilete.cfrcalatori.ro); the 2025-2026 timetable is valid until 12 December 2026.
Evening walk in Sibiu's Large Square (Piata Mare) and Small Square

days.title: Sibiu museums and ASTRA
activities: Brukenthal Palace (European and National art galleries): Wednesday-Sunday 10:00-18:00, ticket office closes 17:15, closed Monday and Tuesday; adult ticket 50 lei, and a 48-hour ticket is 120 lei. The other Brukenthal museums (History, Natural History, Contemporary Art, Pharmacy) are open Wednesday-Sunday 9:00-17:00. If this day falls on a Monday or Tuesday, swap in the ASTRA museum all day

ASTRA National Museum Complex (open-air village museum): open 09:00-17:00 from October to April and 08:00-20:00 from May to September; adult ticket 50 lei, students 10 lei; the site does not state a closed day

days.title: Transfagarasan (DN7C) drive
activities: Needs a car: drive the Transfagarasan from the Sibiu side over the Fagaras mountains. Seasonal closure: CNAIR closes DN7C every winter between Piscu Negru (km 104+000) and Balea Cascada (km 130+800); in 2025 it closed on Monday 20 October (CNAIR press release, under mountain-road rules AND 615-2020) and the closure is decided by CNAIR inspection commissions on weather and avalanche grounds, so the date is not fixed. I found no 2026 winter-closure notice on the pages I could open, and the spring reopening date also varies, so check cnadnr.ro before planning this day outside summer

Stop at Balea Cascada and Balea Lake at the top of the pass. If the road is closed, drive from Sibiu to Curtea de Arges on the lower Olt valley route (DN7) instead and treat this as a scenery-free transfer day
Continue south toward Vidraru Dam and Curtea de Arges; travel time was not verified, so check your route planner and allow a long day

days.title: Poenari, Curtea de Arges, Bucharest
activities: Poenari Citadel above the Arges valley (a steep stair climb up to the ruined fortress, administered by the Arges County Museum): opening hours and prices were not verified from an official page, so confirm with the museum and check for closures before driving there
Curtea de Arges Monastery, an active church and cathedral (visiting hours not verified from an official page, confirm locally); visitors are expected to dress modestly
Drive or take a bus to Bucharest; travel time was not verified, check your route planner

days.title: Depart Bucharest
activities: Free morning in Bucharest, then your flight from Bucharest Henri Coanda Airport; CFR Calatori runs trains between Aeroport Henri Coanda and Bucuresti Nord. Check live train times on CFR Calatori's timetable (mersultrenurilor.infofer.ro or bilete.cfrcalatori.ro); the 2025-2026 timetable is valid until 12 December 2026.

food_culture.name: Ciorba de burta
food_culture.description: Tripe soup soured with vinegar and finished with sour cream and garlic, a classic Romanian soup served across the country and often credited as a hangover cure.

food_culture.name: Bulz
food_culture.description: A traditional shepherd's dish from the Carpathian mountains: a cornmeal ball filled with cheese and baked or grilled over embers, often with sour cream and fried bacon.

food_culture.name: Mici with mustard
food_culture.description: Grilled skinless sausages of minced meat and spices, a popular Romanian street and beer-garden food, usually eaten with mustard and bread.

food_culture.name: Papanasi
food_culture.description: Cheese doughnuts served with sour cream and sour cherry jam, found on restaurant dessert menus in Cluj-Napoca and Sibiu.

food_culture.name: Palinca
food_culture.description: A strong double-distilled fruit brandy from Transylvania, usually plum, and a common drink in the Cluj and Sibiu regions.

food_culture.name: Transhumance shepherding
food_culture.description: The Fagaras mountain area has a long tradition of seasonal sheep grazing in high pastures, which is why cheeses such as telemea and brânză de burduf are sold along mountain roads.

food_culture.name: Transylvanian Saxon heritage in Sibiu
food_culture.description: Sibiu's Upper Town, squares and fortifications were built by Transylvanian Saxon merchants, and Sibiu was named a European Capital of Culture in 2007.
